# Finger Lickin Music - Complete Implementation Plan

Plan version 1.0.0 (2026-10-25). Covers specification FLM-1.0 (base), FLM-1.1.0 (edge cases and
failure modes), FLM-1.2.0 (essential product improvements) and FLM-1.3.0 (maximum-polish checklist),
stored verbatim in `docs/SPECIFICATION.txt`. Status: planning complete; implementation not started.
Nothing described in this document exists in code yet. This single file is the executable roadmap
and the complete design from which the game is implemented, start to finish.

## 0. How to use this plan

### 0.1 Plan identity

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Plan version | 1.0.0 |
| Plan date | 2026-10-25 |
| Document | `Finger Lickin Music/docs/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` (this file) |
| Repository | `s070s/HTML-Games`; folder `Finger Lickin Music/` at the repository root, next to `Beat Em Up/`, `ClassTimeKiller/`, `Mech Flight Sim/` |
| Shipped file | `Finger Lickin Music/FingerLickinMusic.html` (players open this file; no build step is needed to play) |
| Test build | `Finger Lickin Music/FingerLickinMusic.test.html` (gitignored; written by `node tools/build.mjs`; contains the self-test modules) |
| Specification copy | `Finger Lickin Music/docs/SPECIFICATION.txt`, 3,193 lines, the four specification parts concatenated in order |
| Development ledger | `Finger Lickin Music/docs/LEDGER.md` (ADR-16; template in Appendix D) |
| Live status | `Finger Lickin Music/docs/STATUS.md` (structure in 0.7; template in Appendix D) |
| Implementation status at version 1.0.0 | Nothing is implemented. Every requirement in Part 15 is Unimplemented or Deferred. |

Specification parts covered, with their line ranges inside `docs/SPECIFICATION.txt`:

| Code | Title | Version | Lines | Sections |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B | Complete Product Requirements and Technical Specification (base) | FLM-1.0 | 1-1894 | 1-29 |
| E | Edge Cases and Critical Failure Modes | FLM-1.1.0, dated 2026-10-23 | 1896-2253 | 1-13 |
| I | Essential Product Improvements | FLM-1.2.0, dated 2026-10-23 | 2256-2699 | 1-21 |
| P | Complete Maximum-Polish Checklist | FLM-1.3.0, dated 2026-10-23 | 2705-3193 | 1-22 |

Citation form used in every part of this plan: part code, one space, section number, for
example `B 7.3`, `E 2.3`, `I 5.1`, `P 6.3`. Line numbers above let the reader open the spec
copy at the right place; sections are cited, lines are not.

Plan versioning: the implementing session may raise only the patch number (1.0.x) and only
for corrections that do not change an ADR, a module boundary, a data model name, or the T
section list. Any such correction is recorded in the LEDGER "Decisions" section and, when a
requirement row is affected, in Part 15 (B 27 last paragraph: the roadmap changes only through
documented changes to the traceability matrix and the plan). Minor and major changes are the
owner's decision and are not made by the implementing session.

### 0.2 What this document is and is not

This document is:

- The complete, decided design of Finger Lickin Music: architecture decisions (Part 2),
  repository layout and tooling (Part 3), module map and interfaces (Part 4), data model and
  serialization (Part 5), normative module designs with algorithms and unit tests (Part 6),
  user interface (Part 7), import and export strategy (Part 8), performance budgets (Part 9),
  security, privacy, accessibility and failure recovery (Part 10).
- An executable roadmap: Part 11 lists every T section in dependency order with entry
  criteria, deliverables, verification and exit criteria; Part 12 lists every test; Part 13
  the risks; Part 14 the release checklist and final report; Part 15 the traceability matrix.
  Together these are the thirteen planning artifacts of B 1.2 and the end-to-end table of
  contents of B 1.1, and they satisfy the additions demanded by E 12 and I 20.
- The single source of truth for names: modules, types, fields, events, screens, status
  words. Where the specification is silent or allows alternatives, this plan has chosen, and
  the choice is final for version 1.0.0 except the three open questions in Part 2.19.

This document is not:

- A status report. At version 1.0.0 nothing is implemented, built, verified, tested or
  measured, and no sentence in it claims otherwise. Results are recorded later in
  `docs/STATUS.md`, `docs/LEDGER.md` and `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md`.
- A replacement for the specification. The spec says what; this plan says how. When the two
  appear to disagree, follow the plan where it records a decision with a reason (an ADR in
  Part 2 or an item in Part 1.5), otherwise follow the spec and record the discrepancy in the
  LEDGER "Open issues" section.
- Permission to omit. Priorities P0, P1, P2 define sequencing, not permission to omit
  requested functionality silently (B 4.1).
- Finished code. Algorithms are given as pseudocode or numbered steps and signatures are
  exact; the implementing session writes the code.

### 0.3 Reading order

1. Read Part 0 (this part) completely, then Parts 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 completely, then Parts 9
   and 10 completely, before writing any code. These parts fix the names, the numbers, the
   module boundaries, the clock rules and the recovery rules that every module depends on.
2. Read Appendix D (templates) when performing 0.4 step 3, and Appendix C (prohibited
   mistakes and their guards) together with the 0.5 checklist at every phase gate. Use
   Appendix B (glossary) whenever a term is unclear.
3. Read the Part 6 module design for a module (`6.N M-NN`) immediately before implementing
   that module, in full, including its unit test table; it is normative. Do not read all of
   Part 6 up front; it is long and the details must be fresh when the code is written.
4. Execute Part 11 in T order. Each T section names the Part 6 sections, Part 7 screens,
   Part 8 tables, Part 12 tests and Part 15 requirement rows it covers; read those when the T
   section directs. Parts 7, 8, 12, 13, 14 and 15 are reference material consulted this way,
   not read front to back.
5. Re-read Part 0 sections 0.4 to 0.7 at the start of every session (fresh or resumed) and at
   every phase gate.

### 0.4 One-session execution procedure

The procedure assumes one session that runs from Phase 01 to Phase 16. It is written so that
a cut-off at any point loses at most one T section of ledger information, and so that a fresh
session can continue from Part 0 and the LEDGER alone.

Step 0. Preconditions. The working directory is the repository root (the directory that
contains `.git/` and `Finger Lickin Music/`). The folder already contains `docs/` with this
plan and the specification copy, and `README.md`, committed by the planning session. Check:

```text
cd <repository root>
git status --porcelain                 # must print nothing (clean tree)
node --version                         # must print v22 or newer
test -f "Finger Lickin Music/docs/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md" && test -f "Finger Lickin Music/docs/SPECIFICATION.txt" && echo OK
```

If any check fails, stop and report; the plan cannot be executed without the specification
copy, a clean tree, or Node 22.

Step 1. Create the implementation branch from the commit that contains this plan (normally
`main` after the owner merges the planning branch; otherwise the planning branch itself):

```text
git checkout -b flm-implementation
```

Step 2. Create the source folders and add the test-build ignore line (Part 3.10):

```text
cd "Finger Lickin Music"
mkdir -p src tools server test-corpus docs
printf '\n# Finger Lickin Music test build (tools/build.mjs writes it next to the game)\nFinger Lickin Music/FingerLickinMusic.test.html\n' >> ../.gitignore
```

Step 3. Create `docs/LEDGER.md` and `docs/STATUS.md` from the Appendix D templates. The first
LEDGER entry records: the date; "Phase 00: planning artifacts satisfied by
IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md 1.0.0"; the result of validating the plan against the specification
during the 0.3 reading (any inconsistency found and how it was resolved); the environment
assumptions of 0.10 as confirmed or refuted by the Step 0 checks; and the line `RESUME: T01.01`.
STATUS.md starts with every requirement row Unimplemented or Deferred exactly as Part 15 lists
them (0.7). Commit the two documents:

```text
git add docs/LEDGER.md docs/STATUS.md ../.gitignore
git commit -m "Finger Lickin Music docs: start implementation ledger and status"
```

Step 4. For each T section of Part 11, in order:

1. Read the T section. Confirm every dependency it lists is marked done in STATUS.md section
   2 or in the LEDGER; if not, stop and resolve the ordering (record it in the LEDGER).
2. Read the Part 6 module section(s), Part 7 screen(s), Part 8 table(s) and Part 5 types the
   T section names.
3. If this is the first T section of a phase, re-read the 0.5 checklist and Appendix C.
4. Implement exactly the deliverables the T section names: the files, functions, screens,
   tests and documents, with the names given in Parts 4, 5 and 6. Do not implement
   deliverables of later T sections early.
5. Build. Until `tools/build.mjs` exists (it is created in Phase 01), the build step is
   `node --check src/<file>.js` for every new or changed source file. Afterwards:

```text
node tools/build.mjs
```

   The build must exit 0. A size warning (above the envelope of the current phase, OI-45) is recorded in the LEDGER; a size
   failure (above 2.5 MB) blocks the section until resolved.

6. Run the self-test groups named in the T section's Verification. Until `tools/selftest.mjs`
   exists (Phase 01), verification is `node --check` plus opening `src/shell.html` as
   described in the T section. Afterwards, for each named group `<g>`:

```text
node tools/selftest.mjs --group <g>
```

   Every named group must pass. A failing test is fixed before the section is marked done;
   a test that cannot run in this environment (needs a real device, another browser, a
   network) is recorded in STATUS.md with the reason, and the requirement stays Partial.

7. Update STATUS.md: set the status of every R-ID the T section covers (rules in 0.7), update
   the header lines and section 2, add any placeholder or limitation to section 5.
8. Update the LEDGER: at minimum rewrite the `RESUME:` line of the current entry to name the
   next T section; add decisions and assumptions made during the section.

Step 5. At each phase gate (after the last T section of a phase):

1. Run the full regression suite and, when Part 11 says so for the phase, the performance
   scenarios:

```text
node tools/build.mjs
node tools/selftest.mjs --all
node tools/perf.mjs
```

   `--all` must pass completely (B 1.4: preserve all previously accepted functionality). A
   regression found here is fixed before the gate commit.
2. Re-read the 0.5 checklist and tick every box in the LEDGER entry; walk Appendix C; re-read
   the Part 13 risk register and update the status of risks the phase retires (13.3).
3. Write the full LEDGER entry for the phase using the Appendix D entry format and the phase
   gate checklist, ending with `RESUME: T<next phase>.01`.
4. Update STATUS.md sections 1 to 7 and the header.
5. Commit code and documents together, one commit per gate, message in plain words:

```text
cd <repository root>
git add -A -- "Finger Lickin Music" .gitignore
git commit -m "Finger Lickin Music: Phase 01 - application shell, build tool, self-test runner"
```

   Replace the phase number and description. Documents-only commits (a ledger checkpoint
   before a pause, a plan patch) use the prefix `Finger Lickin Music docs: `.
6. Never push. Pushing happens only when the owner says so for that job
   (`.claude/project-profile.md`). Record "push pending owner approval" in the LEDGER
   "Owner actions" section.

Step 6. When context runs low. Triggers: a harness warning about context, a compaction
notice, or the session noticing it cannot recall a Part 4 or Part 5 definition without
re-reading. Then, in this order and nothing else:

1. Finish only the verification of the current T section (do not start another).
2. Write the LEDGER entry with the `RESUME:` line naming the next T section (or the current
   one, if its verification did not pass, with the failing test names).
3. Update STATUS.md header lines.
4. Commit everything so no work is lost. If the commit is not at a phase gate, mark it:

```text
git add -A -- "Finger Lickin Music" .gitignore
git commit -m "Finger Lickin Music: WIP T05.03 (paused, not a phase gate)"
```

5. Stop. Do not push.

Step 7. Resuming in a fresh session:

1. Read Part 0 completely, then the top LEDGER entry, then STATUS.md.
2. Complete the 0.3 reading order (Parts 1-5, 9, 10) before touching code.
3. Rebuild and run the full suite to confirm the recorded state:

```text
cd "Finger Lickin Music"
node tools/build.mjs
node tools/selftest.mjs --all
```

   If the result differs from the LEDGER, fix or record the difference first.
4. Continue at the T section named by `RESUME:`.

Step 8. Finishing. Phase 16 produces the final `FingerLickinMusic.html`, `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`
(Part 8.7, written in Phase 12 and finalized here), `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md` (Part 14), the
final STATUS.md, and the Part 15 Status column update (0.7). The last commit is
`Finger Lickin Music: Phase 16 - packaging and final delivery`. The LEDGER's final entry ends
with `RESUME: none (delivered)` and lists the owner actions that remain (push, merge, device
tests the environment could not run, licence choice per Part 10.3).

### 0.5 Implementation discipline checklist

The implementing session re-reads this list at the start of every phase and ticks each box
in the phase-gate LEDGER entry. A box that cannot be ticked blocks the gate until it can, or
the reason is recorded in STATUS.md with the affected requirements.

From B 1.4:

- [ ] The T sections of Part 11 are followed in dependency order; no T section starts before
      the sections it depends on are done.
- [ ] Traceability is maintained: every T section names its R-IDs, every test is registered
      in its self-test group, and STATUS.md is updated after every T section.
- [ ] The smallest independently testable subsystem is implemented first (within a phase,
      modules in M-number order; within a module, the public API before the screens).
- [ ] Each subsystem is validated (its self-test group passes) before the next is integrated.
- [ ] Previously accepted functionality is preserved when shared systems change:
      `node tools/selftest.mjs --all` passes at every phase gate and any regression is fixed
      before the gate commit.
- [ ] STATUS.md is the continuously updated list of Implemented, Partial, Blocked,
      Unimplemented and Deferred requirements.
- [ ] No feature is reported complete merely because its UI exists; Implemented requires the
      tests named in Part 15 to pass.
- [ ] No placeholder behavior stands in for a required functional system without the
      limitation being documented in STATUS.md section 5 and disclosed in the UI where the
      user meets it.
- [ ] No claim of file-format compatibility, multiplayer synchronization, offline operation
      or performance targets is made without recorded verification (FT, IT, XT, PT evidence
      named in the LEDGER).
- [ ] A requirement that conflicts with the single-file constraint is recorded as a conflict
      with the smallest acceptable exception before proceeding (LEDGER "Decisions"; the
      exceptions already adopted are in Part 2.18).

From E 10, the fifteen prohibited mistakes, as guards:

- [ ] No single global state object: each module keeps its state behind its own namespace,
      and modules communicate only through public APIs and the event bus (Part 4.6).
- [ ] Rendering time is never musical time: musical position comes from
      `Transport.positionAt(audioCtx.currentTime)`, never from frame counts (ADR-05).
- [ ] MIDI is never treated as audio: MIDI events drive `FLM.Instruments`; audio files become
      audio tracks only and never note data (ADR-06).
- [ ] No instrument is treated as monophonic: polyphony is preserved in the model, the
      synthesizer, the charts and the visualization.
- [ ] No generic animation for every instrument: per-instrument controllers in M-20 drive the
      gestures; abstract visualizers cover the rest.
- [ ] Four buttons are never assumed to represent every arrangement without loss: the
      `ChartGenerator` reports omitted source events and the source is never deleted.
- [ ] Browser storage is never the only backup: Export is the real backup and every
      "Save failed" dialog offers it (ADR-08).
- [ ] The timeline protocol (Part 5.16, M-24 clock sync) is defined before any multiplayer
      code is written, and Phase 13 implements that protocol, not a new one.
- [ ] Not all assets load at startup: instrument patches compile on first use, content expands
      lazily, progress is reported only for measurable steps (Part 9.4).
- [ ] No dependency without a packaging strategy: zero runtime dependencies (ADR-02); the
      shipped file works from `file://` with no network.
- [ ] No format support claimed from one sample: every claim rests on the corpus of Part 8.9
      and its FT tests.
- [ ] UI completion is never feature completion: every feature has functional tests.
- [ ] Every mode transition cleans up: `FLM.Modes.assertClean()` reports zero leaks after
      every leave (Part 4.7).
- [ ] Fidelity never degrades silently: tier changes, synthesized (not sampled) instruments,
      fallbacks and unsupported features are visible in the UI and documented.
- [ ] No subsystem is left untested until the end: each T section ends with its named tests
      passing.

Added by this plan:

- [ ] Every placeholder or limitation is documented in STATUS.md section 5 with the exact UI
      text that discloses it.
- [ ] Nothing is described as done, verified, tested or measured without a recorded run: the
      LEDGER names the command and its result.
- [ ] Every assumption is recorded in the LEDGER "Assumptions" section (0.6).
- [ ] The LEDGER `RESUME:` line is current before any pause.
- [ ] Only the names fixed in Parts 4 and 5 are used for modules, namespaces, types, fields,
      events, screens, transport states and modes; no synonyms.
- [ ] New files are UTF-8 with BOM, LF endings, ASCII content (ADR-09; 0.9).

### 0.6 Autonomy and assumptions

- Authorization. The owner has explicitly authorized autonomous execution, so the B 1.3
  autonomous path applies: the implementing session does not wait for approval of the
  planning artifacts (they are this document). Its first act is the 0.3 reading, during which
  it validates the plan against the specification and records the outcome in the first LEDGER
  entry (0.4 step 3).
- Assumptions register. Every assumption the session makes, about the environment, a browser
  behavior, a spec reading, or a missing detail, is written to the LEDGER "Assumptions"
  section as one line containing: the assumption, why it was needed, how it will be verified,
  and its state (open, confirmed, refuted). A refuted assumption triggers a LEDGER
  "Decisions" line stating what changed.
- No omission because of difficulty. If a requirement cannot be completed, its STATUS.md
  status becomes Blocked with the reason and what would unblock it. The session never
  relabels a requirement Deferred on its own; Deferred is reserved for the items Part 1.5
  lists and for new deferrals the owner approves, each recorded in the LEDGER.
- Single-file conflicts. When a requirement conflicts with the single-file constraint, the
  session records the conflict and the smallest acceptable exception in the LEDGER
  "Decisions" section and STATUS.md section 5, and discloses it on SCR-About through the
  Part 7.11 text catalog (B 1.4 last bullet, B 5.4). The exceptions already adopted are in
  Part 2.18: manual-signaling WebRTC, the optional public STUN server, the optional relay
  server, and Web MIDI only in secure contexts.
- Open questions. Only OQ-1, OQ-2 and OQ-3 (Part 2.19) remain open, each with its fallback
  already decided. The session selects the fallback when the corresponding test fails and
  records the selection in the LEDGER; it does not reopen any other decision.
- Owner actions. The session cannot push, merge, run tests on physical devices or in Firefox,
  Safari, iOS or Android, or choose the game's licence (Part 10.3). It lists each such item
  in the LEDGER "Owner actions" section and in the final report (Part 14) and never presents
  the missing result as obtained.

### 0.7 Status tracking

`docs/STATUS.md` is the live list demanded by B 1.4 ("a continuously updated list of
implemented, partially implemented, blocked, and unimplemented requirements"). It is updated
after every T section (0.4 step 4.7) and at every phase gate. Its exact structure:

```text
# Finger Lickin Music - STATUS

Plan version: 1.0.0
Updated: <YYYY-MM-DD> (UTC date of the last change to this file)
Current phase: Phase <NN>
Last completed T section: <Tpp.nn or none>
Build: <FingerLickinMusic.html size in bytes, or "not built">
Self-test (--all): <passed>/<total> on <YYYY-MM-DD>, or "not run"
Live and device tests (LT, XT): <count run>/<count defined>, or "not run"

## 1. Counts per specification part

| Part | Rows | Implemented | Partial | Blocked | Unimplemented | Deferred |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B (FLM-1.0) | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> |
| E (FLM-1.1.0) | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> |
| I (FLM-1.2.0) | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> |
| P (FLM-1.3.0) | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> |
| Total | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> | <n> |

## 2. Phase gates

| Phase | T sections done / total | Gate commit | Gate date | --all result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 00 | satisfied by plan 1.0.0 | n/a | 2026-10-25 | n/a |
| Phase 01 | <d> / <t> | <short hash or -> | <date or -> | <passed/total or -> |
| Phase 02 to Phase 16 | one row each with the same five columns | - | - | - |

## 3. Not Implemented, listed individually

| R-ID | Status | Phase | Reason (one line) | Disclosure (screen, doc, or n/a) |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## 4. Not yet reached, summarized per phase

| Phase | Unimplemented rows | Deferred rows |
|---|---|---|

## 5. Placeholders and limitations

| Module or screen | Limitation | Spec ref | Disclosure (exact UI text or document) | Affected R-IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## 6. Known defects

| Defect | Severity | Found in T section | Regression test | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## 7. Measurements recorded

| Budget (Part 9.1 row) | Value or "not measured" | Tool and scenario | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
```

Rules:

1. Rows per part equals the row count of the matching Part 15 subsection (15.1 for B, 15.2
   for E, 15.3 for I, 15.4 for P). The five status columns sum to Rows.
2. Section 3 lists individually every requirement that is not Implemented and whose Phase
   has started, plus every Partial, Blocked and Deferred requirement regardless of phase.
   Section 4 summarizes requirements of phases not yet started, so the file stays readable
   while most of the matrix is untouched. A requirement moves from section 4 to section 3
   when its phase starts.
3. Status transitions. Unimplemented -> Partial when code for the requirement exists but not
   every test named in its Part 15 Tests column passes in the latest `--all` run, or when a
   named test cannot run in this environment (reason "awaiting owner device test").
   Partial -> Implemented when every named test passes in the latest `--all` run, and for
   P0 and P1 the `AT-<R-ID>` acceptance test passes. Any status -> Blocked when work cannot
   proceed; the reason names the blocker and what unblocks it. Deferred only as 0.6 allows.
   Implemented -> Partial again if a later `--all` run fails one of its tests (recorded in
   section 6 as a defect).
4. Section 5 is the complete list of placeholders and limitations (B 1.4, E 10 item 14). Each
   row gives the exact disclosure text or names the document that discloses it; "none" is
   not an acceptable disclosure for a limitation the user can meet.
5. Section 6 defects carry severity Critical, High, Medium or Low (Part 13.2 rules) and name
   the regression test added when fixed (I 17 last rule); state is open or fixed.
6. Section 7 holds every Part 9.1 budget with its measured value or "not measured"; values
   measured under software GL in the headless environment are marked "(software GL)".
7. Phase 16 pass: the Part 15 matrix Status column is updated by hand from STATUS.md, row by
   row; afterwards the counts in STATUS.md section 1 must equal the counts of the Part 15
   Status column per part, and the LEDGER final entry records both sets of counts.
8. STATUS.md never says "done" for a phase whose gate commit does not exist.

### 0.8 Definition of completion

The project is complete only when all of the following hold (B 1.5):

1. The final artifact `FingerLickinMusic.html` has been tested against the acceptance
   criteria of B 26 through the Part 12 acceptance tests: every P0 and P1 requirement has its
   `AT-<R-ID>` test and that test passes (B 25.7).
2. Its supported file formats and limitations are documented in `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`
   (Part 8.7) and on SCR-About, with Supported, Partial, Conversion or Unsupported for every
   format and version (B 3.6, I 6.4).
3. Its desktop and mobile controls work: keyboard, touch, gamepad and optional Web MIDI pass
   their IT tests, and the XT tests the environment allows; the rest are listed as owner
   actions.
4. Its core gameplay systems operate: Quick Play, Instrument Mode, Free Play, Studio, Song
   Library, Import, Dance Mode on the built-in content, verified by IT tests.
5. Its delivery format satisfies the standalone HTML requirement to the extent technically
   possible: one file, zero runtime dependencies, works from `file://`, with the Part 2.18
   exceptions documented (B 5.2 to 5.4).
6. The release-blocking gate in Part 12 section 12.10 (the ten conditions of E 13) has no
   unresolved item.
7. The final report of Part 14 (the fourteen items of B 28) is written to
   `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md` and distinguishes implemented and tested functionality from
   partial functionality, unverified behavior and future work.

A visually convincing mockup, a partial prototype, or a collection of nonfunctional screens
is not an acceptable final implementation (B 1.5). Lower-priority features may be deferred
only when their status is documented in STATUS.md and `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md` and the core
acceptance criteria remain satisfied (E 13).

### 0.9 Conventions

#### 0.9.1 Identifier forms

| ID form | Meaning | Owning part | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R-B<sec>-<nn>` | Requirement from base spec section `<sec>` | Part 15 (traceability) | `R-B7.3-04` |
| `R-E<sec>-<nn>` | Requirement from edge-case spec | Part 15 | `R-E2.3-01` |
| `R-I<sec>-<nn>` | Requirement from improvements spec | Part 15 | `R-I5.1-02` |
| `R-P<sec>-<nn>` | Requirement from polish checklist | Part 15 | `R-P6.3-05` |
| `M-<nn>` | Source module (fixed list in Part 4) | Part 4 | `M-05` |
| `ADR-<nn>` | Architecture decision (fixed list ADR-01..ADR-16) | Part 2 | `ADR-03` |
| `T<pp>.<nn>` | Table-of-contents section, phase `pp` (00-16) | Part 11 | `T04.03` |
| `UT-<MM>-<nn>` | Unit test owned by module MM | Part 6 (module designs) | `UT-05-07` |
| `IT-<nnn>` | Integration test | Part 12 | `IT-014` |
| `FT-<nnn>` | File-format test | Part 12 | `FT-031` |
| `TT-<nnn>` | Timing test | Part 12 | `TT-006` |
| `PT-<nnn>` | Performance test | Part 12 | `PT-003` |
| `XT-<nnn>` | Cross-device/browser test | Part 12 | `XT-010` |
| `FI-<nnn>` | Fault-injection test | Part 12 | `FI-008` |
| `LT-<nnn>` | Live manual test | Part 12 | `LT-022` |
| `AT-<R-ID>` | Acceptance test for requirement R-ID (deterministic name) | Part 12 lists; anyone may reference | `AT-R-B7.3-04` |
| `RISK-<nn>` | Risk register entry | Part 13 | `RISK-07` |
| `SCR-<name>` | UI screen | Part 7 | `SCR-MainMenu` |
| `DLG-<name>` | Dialog | Part 7 | `DLG-SaveFailed` |
| `EVT-<name>` | Event bus topic | Part 4 | `EVT-transport.state` |

An ID is defined in exactly one part (the owning part) and referenced anywhere. Requirement
rows are numbered `-01, -02, ...` within the spec's own section number by walking the spec in
order; every bullet, numbered item, table row or sentence that states an obligation is one
row (Part 15.0 explains the columns). Unit tests are defined inline in Part 6 and compiled
into Part 12; `AT-<R-ID>` exists for every P0 and P1 requirement.

#### 0.9.2 Status vocabulary

Only these five words, capitalized, describe a requirement's state:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Implemented | Code exists and every test named for the requirement in Part 15 passes in the latest full run; for P0 and P1 the acceptance test passes. |
| Partial | Code exists but some named test does not pass or cannot run in the environment; the reason is recorded. |
| Blocked | Work cannot proceed; the blocker and what unblocks it are recorded. |
| Unimplemented | No code yet. The state of every requirement at plan version 1.0.0 unless Deferred. |
| Deferred | Intentionally not built in v1 with its rules documented; only the items Part 1.5 lists or the owner approves. |

#### 0.9.3 Compatibility vocabulary

Only these four words describe how a file format or feature is handled:

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Supported | The format or version imports with the features listed as preserved in the Part 8 tables and the matrix in `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`, verified by FT tests on the corpus. |
| Partial | The format imports, but listed features are lost or approximated; each loss produces a warning code (Part 8.8) and is listed in the matrix. |
| Conversion | The input is imported through a conversion path into a different representation (audio files become audio tracks; notation becomes events); the conversion and its losses are stated. |
| Unsupported | The format or version is identified by the format identifier and refused with a message naming it (for example GP6/GP7 `.gpx`/`.gp`, SoundFont `.sf2`). |

#### 0.9.4 Priorities (B 4.1)

| Priority | Meaning |
|---|---|
| P0 | Required for a minimally complete product (B 4.2 list). |
| P1 | Required for the full intended product (B 4.3 list). |
| P2 | Advanced features or enhancements that may follow the stable core (B 4.4 list). |

Priorities define sequencing, not permission to omit requested functionality silently.
Part 15 assigns a priority to every row; where the spec does not assign one, Part 15.0 states
the derivation rule used.

#### 0.9.5 Writing and encoding rules for new files (ADR-09)

- Every new text file is UTF-8 with a leading BOM and LF line endings. The repository's
  `.gitattributes` (`* text=auto`) normalizes endings in the repository; the working copy on
  Linux is LF. The build strips per-file BOMs and emits one leading BOM in the output files.
- Content is plain ASCII: no em dashes, en dashes, curly quotes, arrows, bullets other than
  `-`, or box-drawing characters. Use `-` for dashes, `->` for arrows, `"` for quotes.
- JS and HTML source: 2-space indent, `'use strict'` in every module IIFE, semicolons always,
  no transpiling, ES2020 syntax at most (optional chaining and nullish coalescing allowed; no
  decorators, no top-level await, no ES modules in the browser bundle). Node tools in
  `tools/` and `server/` are `.mjs` ES modules using Node built-ins only.
- Source files are `src/shell.html` plus `src/NN-name.js`; load order is file-name order; a
  module references only lower-numbered modules plus the event bus (Part 4.2). Each module
  attaches exactly one namespace object to `FLM` and nothing else to `window`.
- Markdown documents (`docs/*.md`, `README.md`): GitHub tables with a header row and a
  `|---|` separator, every row with the header's column count, no `|` inside cells.
- Commit messages: `Finger Lickin Music: <plain words>` for code (with or without docs),
  `Finger Lickin Music docs: <plain words>` for documents-only commits. Never push without
  the owner's go.

#### 0.9.6 Terminology rule

Use the names in Parts 4 and 5 exactly: module IDs and files (`M-05`, `src/05-audio.js`),
namespaces (`FLM.Audio`), types and fields (`Song`, `Track`, `NoteEvent`, `TempoMap`,
`Chart`, `ChartNote`, `DanceChart`, `DanceStep`, `InputEvent`, `Calibration`,
`CharacterConfig`, `Project`, `RecordingTake`, `NetMessage`), transport states
(`stopped | countin | playing | paused | recording`), mode names (`menu | quickplay |
instrument | freeplay | studio | library | import | dance | multiplayer | customize |
settings | help | about | diagnostics | tutorial | results`), mapping profiles A to F
(B 8.3), difficulty names (instrument charts `beginner, intermediate, advanced, expert`;
dance charts `easy, normal, hard`), judgments (`perfect | great | good | miss`), screen IDs
(`SCR-*`, `DLG-*`), event topics (`EVT-*`), quality tiers (High, Balanced, Low, Abstract),
and the Standalone edition and Online edition (Part 1.4). Do not invent synonyms in code,
documents, UI text or commit messages. Appendix B defines every term of art.

|---|---|---|---|
| Node | Version 22 or newer (`node --version`; v22.22.0 observed when this plan was written) | `node --version` | Stop and report; no tool in this plan runs on older Node and no install is permitted. |
| Playwright with Chromium | Preinstalled; `require('playwright')` resolves and `chromium.launch()` works | `node -e "require('playwright')"` | Fallback 1: `chromium.launch({ executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium' })` (on the planning machine this path is a symlink to `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-<build>/chrome-linux64/chrome`). Fallback 2: start Chromium with `--remote-debugging-port=9222` and attach with `chromium.connectOverCDP('http://127.0.0.1:9222')` (Part 3.4). If none works, self-tests run by opening `FingerLickinMusic.test.html` manually and STATUS.md records "self-test: not run headless". |
| Headless GL | SwiftShader through ANGLE (`--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`) | Part 3.4 launch flags | WebGL tests still run on software GL; tier selection, frame rate and memory numbers are "(software GL)" in STATUS.md section 7, never presented as device results. |
| Network | None required; CDNs are blocked; no fetch at build, test or run time | n/a | Nothing to do; any tool that needs the network is a plan violation (ADR-02). The relay server for IT tests runs locally on `127.0.0.1` only. |

| Operating system and shell | Linux, case-sensitive paths, bash; the game folder name contains spaces | n/a | Always quote paths containing `Finger Lickin Music`. |

| Disk and time | The build output is under 2.5 MB; a full `--all` self-test run finishes within the timeout policy of Part 3.4 | `node tools/build.mjs` exit code | A timeout is a failing test, recorded as such; the session does not raise timeouts to make a run pass. |

## 1. Product scope and delivery profiles

### 1.1 Product summary and the five pillars

Finger Lickin Music is a browser music game delivered as one HTML file,
`Finger Lickin Music/FingerLickinMusic.html` (B 2, B 5, B 29). In that one file the
player performs any of 128 General MIDI instruments with four buttons against a scrolling
chart, improvises in Free Play with six mapping profiles, records and layers tracks in a
multitrack Studio, imports MIDI, MusicXML and Guitar Pro 3-5 arrangements and turns any
track into a playable chart without altering the source, watches a procedurally built 3D
band whose every movement is derived from the scheduled musical events, plays a
four-direction Dance Mode on the same musical timeline, customizes the band members, keeps
a local progression record, and plays with 2-4 people over WebRTC using copy-paste invite
codes (an optional relay server adds room codes in the Online edition). Every mode is a
different experience on one engine (I 1.1): one integer-tick timeline at PPQ 960, one
Transport anchored to the audio clock, one Web Audio synthesizer, one input abstraction,
one renderer with four quality tiers, one Project model. At plan version 1.0.0 nothing is
implemented; "v1" below means the first release produced by executing this plan (game
`FLM.VERSION` 1.0.0).

The five pillars of I 21 are the acceptance lens for the whole plan. A feature counts
toward a pillar only when the named evidence exists (test IDs are assigned in Part 12).

| Pillar (I 21) | What it means in this product | Acceptance evidence | Primary modules |
|---|---|---|---|
| Musical accuracy | Integer ticks (PPQ 960), TempoMap and MeterMap respected, polyphony never collapsed, GM program mapping correct, drums on channel 10, imports preserve the source with warnings for anything not preserved | UT for M-03, M-04, M-05, M-10 to M-14; TT drift tests (abs drift < 2 ms after a 10 min loop, scheduled start within 1 ms); FT corpus (every file in Part 8.9); AT for B 3.1, B 3.5, B 9, B 11, B 15, B 26.3 | M-02 to M-06, M-10 to M-14 |
| Immediate playability | Quick Play demo playable <= 5 s desktop and <= 8 s mobile after file open; four buttons on keyboard, touch and gamepad; profiles A-F; deterministic chart generation per difficulty; calibration applied exactly once | PT startup scenario; UT for M-07, M-08, M-09 (boundary tests at exactly +/- window, determinism); IT input -> audio and input -> scoring; XT on the five browsers; LT on physical devices | M-07, M-08, M-09, M-26, M-27 |
| Expressive visualization | Animation and stage effects derive from `sched.noteOn`/`sched.noteOff` and audio time, never from frame count; performers are still during rests; abstract visualizers and the Abstract tier keep the event-to-visual relationship when humanoid animation is unavailable | UT for M-19 to M-21 (pose amplitude at event time, stillness in rests, determinism); IT imported MIDI -> animation; XT tier selection per device; FI `render.contextLoss` and `render.slowFrames` | M-18 to M-22 |
| Creative freedom | Free Play with record and replay, Studio with count-in, overdub, loop record, piano roll, quantize, undo/redo, mixer, markers; export to `.mid`, `.flm.json`, WAV | UT for M-15, M-17; IT record -> save -> reload, multitrack playback and mixing; FT round trips (Part 8.11) | M-15, M-16, M-17 |
| Reliability | Safe write with read-back and `.bak`, autosave only at safe points, panic for all voices, full mode teardown proven by `FLM.Modes.assertClean()`, parsers that never crash on the malformed corpus, fault injection, the E 13 release gate | FI tests for every `FLM.debug.inject` fault (Part 10.9); IT 20 enter/leave cycles with growth <= 10 MB; FT malformed and truncated files; LT interruption cases; the Part 12.10 gate | M-01, M-16, M-28, M-29, M-31 |

Pillar coverage is re-read at every phase gate (Part 11) and in the Phase 16 review
(Part 14). A feature whose evidence is missing is reported as Partial or Unimplemented in
`docs/STATUS.md`, never as Implemented because its screen exists (B 1.4, E 10 item 12).

### 1.2 The unified engine and its modes

The engine is a fixed set of shared systems, each existing exactly once for the lifetime of
the page. A mode "binds" a system when the mode manager (M-28) hands it to the mode on
enter and takes it back in the leave sequence of Part 4.7. No mode constructs its own copy
of a shared system, two modes are never active at the same time, and `mode.enter` for the
next mode is emitted only after `mode.leave` of the previous mode has completed and
`assertClean()` has passed (I 1.1, E 10 items 1 and 13).

| Shared system | Namespace | Exactly one of | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transport | `FLM.Transport` | transport state machine, position, loop, speed, count-in | Drives the Scheduler cursor; the only writer of musical position |
| Audio | `FLM.Audio` plus `FLM.Instruments` | `AudioContext`, bus graph, `VoiceAllocator`, `Scheduler`, metronome | Created at the audio unlock gesture and never recreated except by hard panic rebuild of the graph (same context) |
| Input | `FLM.Input` | listener set, `InputState`, calibration anchor | Gameplay controls only; DOM widgets use ordinary DOM events through M-26 |
| Mapping | `FLM.Mapping` | active profile A-F and its parameters | Converts `InputEvent` to musical actions for sound; charts are generated by `ChartGenerator` in the same module |
| Rhythm | `FLM.Rhythm` | `Judge`, `ScoreState`, chart cursor | Used by instrument, dance, multiplayer and tutorial; `restart()` clears all state |
| Render | `FLM.Render` | GL context (or `Flat2D`), scene graph root, stats | Tier chosen at boot and on downgrade; never advances musical time |
| Stage | `FLM.Stage` plus `FLM.Rig`, `FLM.Animation`, `FLM.Character` | performer slots 0-4, props, effects, camera, highway | Composed from the current characters and the current Song's tracks |
| Project | `FLM.Project` with `FLM.Storage` | the current `Project` (persistent or transient) | "Transient" means created for a mode and never saved unless the user asks |

Mode table. Screens are listed by `SCR-*` name; layouts and states are specified in Part 7.
`SCR-Pause` is a screen inside the gameplay modes, not a mode. Exit paths name the
destination mode and the guard dialog where one applies.

| Mode | Screen(s) | What the user does | Binds | Exit paths |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| menu | SCR-MainMenu | Chooses one of the twelve entries (brief section 7 order); reads one-line reasons on disabled entries; sees the current project name when one is open; sees the daily challenge card | Render, Stage (idle band built from the saved characters, silent; in the Abstract tier a static title card) | Any entry -> that mode. Root of the screen stack: browser back does nothing here |
| quickplay | SCR-QuickPlay | Quick Start level: picks a song (built-in or imported), an instrument track or Dance, a difficulty, then Play. Customize level (reached from the "Instrument Mode" menu entry): also control layout and profile, backing tracks on or off, visualization on or off, chart preview per difficulty, practice options (I 6.3), audio and input shortcuts | Project (the chosen song loaded into a transient read-only Project when no project is open), Render, Stage (idle preview of the band for the chosen song) | Play -> instrument or dance with origin `quickplay` or `instrumentmode`; Back -> menu |
| instrument | SCR-Instrument, SCR-Pause | Plays the four-button chart of one track while the arrangement plays; practice tools from SCR-Pause (mute target, accompaniment level, loop, speed, restart at section) | Transport, Audio, Input, Mapping, Rhythm, Render, Stage, Project (read-only) | Song end -> results; `Escape` -> SCR-Pause -> Resume, Restart (full leave then enter with identical parameters), Quit -> origin |
| freeplay | SCR-FreePlay | Triggers notes and chords with profiles A-F (`Digit1-6`), picks instrument, key, scale or chromatic, octave (`KeyQ`/`KeyE`) and register, sustain, note duration, velocity, metronome, tempo, quantize on or off; records and replays takes | Transport (tempo override, metronome, count-in, recording), Audio, Input, Mapping, Render, Stage (one performer: the player's character), Project (transient Project named "Free Play session", created on the first take) | Back -> menu (DLG-UnsavedChanges when a take exists); Open in Studio -> studio with the same Project (it becomes persistent on first save) |
| studio | SCR-Studio | Creates, renames, reorders, duplicates and deletes tracks; assigns instruments; records with count-in; overdubs; loop-records; edits in the piano roll; quantizes; mixes; sets tempo, meter, key and scale; adds section markers; saves; exports | Transport, Audio, Input, Mapping, Render, Stage (collapsible panel; hidden by default in mobile portrait), Project (read-write) | Back -> menu (DLG-UnsavedChanges when dirty); Play this track -> instrument with origin `studio`; Characters -> customize (Project stays loaded); Export -> dialogs, stays in studio |
| library | SCR-Library | Browses built-in songs, imported songs and saved projects with filters; per item: Play, Open in Studio, Dance, Export, Delete | Project (an item is loaded only when an action is chosen; browsing reads index records) | Play -> quickplay prefilled; Open in Studio -> studio; Dance -> dance with origin `library`; Import -> import; Back -> menu |
| import | SCR-ImportInspect | Picks a file (picker or drag and drop); reads the `InspectionReport`; plays and stops a preview of the candidate; previews the generated chart per difficulty and changes the mapping; confirms or cancels | Transport, Audio (preview of the candidate Song only), Project (the candidate is held outside the current Project until confirmed) | Confirm "Save to Library" -> library with the song added; Confirm "Play now" -> quickplay prefilled; either path shows DLG-ImportReplace first when a project is open and dirty; Cancel -> previous screen with the current Project untouched |
| dance | SCR-Dance, SCR-Pause | Select state: picks song, difficulty (easy, normal, hard) and layout (arrows or pads). Play state: steps on four directions in time, holds and jumps; practice speed and loop | Transport, Audio, Input, Rhythm (lanes = directions), Render, Stage (choreography avatar), Project (read-only) | Song end -> results; `Escape` -> SCR-Pause -> Resume, Restart, Quit -> origin (`dance` select state when entered from the menu) |
| multiplayer | SCR-Multiplayer; play uses the SCR-Instrument layout with the multiplayer HUD additions of Part 7.6 | Reads the privacy statement; creates or joins a room by invite and answer codes (or by 6-character room code through the relay in the Online edition); sets display name and avatar; readies up; the host picks the experience (Synchronized Play or Cooperative Band), song and charts; plays; sees results; reads sync diagnostics | Transport (slaved to the shared clock, host-driven), Audio, Input, Mapping, Rhythm, Render, Stage, Project (read-only), plus `FLM.Net` | Results -> lobby; Leave -> menu (connection closed, room state cleared); host leaves -> results -> SCR-Multiplayer create-or-join state |
| customize | SCR-Characters | Edits a `CharacterConfig`: presets, seeded randomize, every option of the catalog, instrument and slot, animation style; hears and sees a looped preview phrase of the chosen instrument | Transport, Audio (the instrument's preview phrase from M-30 looped at -12 dB, toggleable), Render, Stage (the edited character alone), Project (characters are saved to settings, and to the open Project when one is open) | Back -> previous mode (menu or studio) with the Project still loaded; changes are kept on Back, no dialog |
| settings | SCR-Settings, DLG-Calibration, DLG-RemapConflict | Changes settings by category (Part 5.11); runs the calibration wizard; remaps controls | Input (capture for remapping; tap test), Audio (test tones, metronome preview), Transport (metronome ticks inside DLG-Calibration only) | Back -> previous screen; every change applies immediately and persists on change |
| help | SCR-Help | Reads controls and mode explanations; presses a key, pad or gamepad button to see its current binding | Input (display only; no musical action) | Back -> previous screen |
| about | SCR-About | Reads edition, version, build date, honest limits, licenses, privacy summary | none | Back -> previous screen |
| diagnostics | SCR-Diagnostics | Views timing, audio, render, storage and network metrics and the log tail; exports diagnostics JSON; toggles the stats overlay; runs the self-test in the test build | none bound; reads metrics from every module; Audio only for the "Test tone" button | Back -> previous screen |
| tutorial | SCR-Tutorial | Follows the seven steps of I 11.3: trigger a note, two simultaneous notes, follow a rhythm, change instrument, record a short take, import a song (guided to the picker, skippable), enter studio or dance | Transport, Audio, Input, Mapping, Rhythm (steps 1-3 only), Render, Stage, Project (tutorial Song `tut-basics` from M-30; the recording step uses a transient Project) | Finish or Skip all -> menu (onboarding flag set); step 7 -> studio or dance with origin `tutorial` |
| results | SCR-Results | Reads the `PerformanceSummary`, section stats, personal-best delta, new achievements and unlocks; retries or returns | Render, Stage (idle performers); reads and writes `FLM.Progress` | Retry -> the same gameplay mode with identical parameters (full leave then enter); Back -> the origin screen with its selection state restored; in multiplayer -> lobby |

Origin rule. Every gameplay launch (instrument, dance, tutorial, multiplayer play) carries an
`origin` value from the fixed set `menu`, `quickplay`, `instrumentmode`, `library`,
`import`, `studio`, `dance`, `multiplayer`, `tutorial`, `daily` (the daily challenge card).
SCR-Results "Back" and SCR-Pause "Quit" return to the screen that origin names, with that
screen's filters, selection and scroll position restored (P 21). Retry and Restart never
reuse scoring state: they run the full leave sequence and then enter again (P 5.2).

Menu entry to mode map (B 6.2 order): Quick Play -> quickplay (Quick Start level);
Instrument Mode -> quickplay (Customize level); Free Play -> freeplay; Studio -> studio
(opens the last project or a new empty one); Song Library -> library; Import Music ->
import; Dance Mode -> dance (select state); Multiplayer -> multiplayer; Characters ->
customize; Settings -> settings; Help and Controls -> help; About -> about. Diagnostics is
reached from Settings and from `?diag`; Tutorial from SCR-FirstLaunch, Help and the daily
card when onboarding is incomplete; Results only from gameplay.

### 1.4 Delivery profiles

B 5.4 and I 14.3 require two operating contexts. Both are the same source and the same
client; they differ only in the build flag `tools/build.mjs --online <relayUrl>` (Part 3.3),
which stamps the edition and relay URL into build constants and widens the CSP
`connect-src` to the relay origin (ADR-12). The Standalone edition is the primary
deliverable (B 3.7). Nothing in either edition requires an account, telemetry or a
download at runtime.

| Feature | Standalone edition | Online edition | Needs | When the need is not met |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| All local modes: menu, quickplay, instrument, freeplay, studio, library, dance, customize, tutorial, results, settings, help, about, diagnostics | Full | Full | Nothing beyond the browser | n/a |
| Import of MIDI, MusicXML, Guitar Pro 3-5, audio files | Full | Full | `<input type=file>` or drag and drop from `file://` (verified per browser, 1.6) | Picker blocked -> drag and drop remains; message names the alternative |
| Export: `.mid`, `.flm.json`, `.flmdance.json`, `.flmchar.json`, `.flmsettings.json`, WAV mix | Full | Full | `a[download]` with a Blob URL; fallback opens a data URL in a new tab (Part 5.14, Part 6.16) | Both blocked -> DLG-SaveFailed-style notice naming copy-to-clipboard for JSON formats |
| Local persistence (localStorage, IndexedDB `flm-db`) | Full | Full | Storage available on the current origin | IndexedDB unavailable -> localStorage-only with a 2 MB project cap and a visible notice; both unavailable -> session-only with export offered on every save |
| Progression: history, personal bests, achievements, unlocks, daily challenge | Full, local | Full, local | Local date for the daily seed | n/a |
| Multiplayer by invite and answer codes (WebRTC P2P, 2-4 players) | Full | Full | Players exchange codes through any channel of their own; same network, or the STUN toggle for NAT traversal | ICE fails -> DLG-NetError with Retry and the LAN hint; standalone play unaffected |
| Public STUN toggle (`stun:stun.l.google.com:19302`) | Available, off by default | Available, off by default | Reachability of the Google STUN service (OQ-3), an external dependency named in the lobby when on | Unreachable -> host candidates only after the 3 s gathering timeout; lobby note "STUN server not reachable; connections may only work on the same network." |
| Relay rooms by 6-character room code | Not available: the control is hidden, About states the Standalone sentence, `?online=` is ignored with a toast | Available | `server/relay.mjs` reachable at the build-time URL over `ws://` or `wss://`; CSP widened at build | Unreachable -> DLG-NetError "Could not reach the relay server at {relayUrl}. You can still play by exchanging invite codes directly." and the lobby switches to invite codes |
| Downloadable sound banks or assets | None | None (I 14.3 permits them; v1 ships none) | n/a | n/a |
| Web MIDI input | Where `Caps.webMidi` and `Caps.secureContext` are true | Same | Secure context and browser support | Control hidden with its reason (1.5) |
| Updates | Replace the file | Replace the file | n/a | n/a |
| Accounts, telemetry, leaderboards beyond the local device | None | None | n/a | n/a |

Edition sentences shown on SCR-About (also the first paragraph of the Multiplayer screen's
"How this works" panel):

- Standalone: "Standalone edition. Everything runs from this file on your device: no server,
  account or network connection is needed. Multiplayer uses direct peer-to-peer connections
  that you set up by exchanging invite codes."
- Online: "Online edition. This build can also use the relay server at {relayUrl} to connect
  players by room code. The relay only forwards messages between players and stores
  nothing. Every other feature works without it."

Toast shown when `?online=<relayUrl>` is present in a Standalone build: "Relay rooms need
the Online edition build. Invite codes still work."

Graceful failure rules (B 5.4, B 17.5, E 11, P 13):

1. The relay URL is used only by `FLM.Net`'s relay transport adapter; no other module
   reads it. A failed or absent relay changes exactly one thing: the "Join by room code"
   and "Create room" controls are replaced by the invite-code flow, with the DLG-NetError
   text above shown once per attempt.
2. STUN is used only inside `RTCPeerConnection` ICE gathering when the toggle is on. Its
   failure is detected by the gathering timeout (3 s, Part 6.24) and reported by the lobby
   note above; the invite code is still produced from the candidates gathered.
3. Multiplayer as a whole is disabled on the main menu only when `RTCPeerConnection` is
   missing (`Caps` check at boot), with the reason "Multiplayer needs WebRTC, which this
   browser does not provide." Every other entry stays enabled.
4. No network failure ever stops the Transport, mutes Audio, closes a Project or writes to
   storage. Leaving the multiplayer mode runs the standard leave sequence (Part 4.7) plus
   closing the `RTCPeerConnection` and the relay socket.
5. The relay never interprets game payloads except `join` and `leave` (Part 3.7); a relay
   restart drops the room, every client sees DLG-NetError and returns to the create-or-join
   state with local results kept.

Relay hosting requirements, recorded here for B 17.1 and detailed in Part 3.7: Node 22 or
newer, one TCP port from `PORT`, plain `http` upgrade handling with TLS terminated by a
reverse proxy for `wss://`, no persistence, no credentials, no personal logging. Budgets:
memory <= 64 MB at 100 concurrent rooms, outbound bandwidth <= 100 KB/s per room at the
worst-case rate limits (4 peers, 60 messages/s each, state at 10 Hz), room idle expiry
10 min. Operating cost is one small always-on process; the Standalone edition has no
operating cost.

Global reverb decision (recorded for Part 6.5 and Part 7.6): one aux bus fed post-fader from
every `ChannelStrip` and from live input, one "Reverb" control 0-100 % (default 15 %,
drums tracks excluded from the send by default with a per-track "send to reverb" toggle
default on for melodic tracks and off for `isDrums` tracks), bypassed entirely at 0 % and on
the Low and Abstract tiers unless the user turns it on, never applied to the metronome bus.

About screen "Limits of this version" block (Part 7.11 reproduces it verbatim and appends
the polyphony and track limits line from Part 9.9):

```text
Limits of this version
- Instrument sounds are synthesized by this file; no sampled sound bank is included, so
  timbres approximate General MIDI instruments rather than reproduce recordings.
- Import: MIDI (.mid, .midi) format 0, 1 and 2; MusicXML (.xml, .musicxml, .mxl);
  Guitar Pro 3, 4 and 5 (.gp3, .gp4, .gp5). Guitar Pro 6 and 7 files (.gpx, .gp) cannot
  be imported. Audio files (.wav, .mp3, .ogg, .flac, where this browser can decode them)
  are imported as backing audio only; notes are never generated from audio.
- MusicXML and Guitar Pro files are imported as musical events; sheet music and
  tablature are not displayed.
- Studio effects are a master limiter and one global reverb. Per-track EQ, delay,
  compression and automation are not included.
- Multiplayer: 2 to 4 players in Synchronized Play or Cooperative Band. Shared studio
  editing, two players on one keyboard, joining a song in progress and continuing after
  the host leaves are not included.
- MIDI devices are used only where the browser offers Web MIDI on a secure page.
- Browser and file-format support is listed in docs/COMPATIBILITY.md and reflects
  recorded tests, not assumptions.
```

### 1.6 Browser support policy

Target browsers (B 5.1, B 25.5) and the version floors decided for v1. Floors are the
oldest versions the implementation is designed for; Phase 15 tests run on the current
stable release and the previous major release of each, and the published claim names the
versions actually tested (B 25.5 "versions and devices must be recorded").

| Browser | Floor | Why this floor | Claim at plan version 1.0.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop Chromium (Chrome, Edge) | 110 | Stable WebGL2, `AudioContext.outputLatency`, Pointer Events, `navigator.storage.estimate`, IndexedDB on `file://` | Not yet verified |
| Desktop Firefox | 115 (ESR) | Stable WebGL2 and Web Audio; Web MIDI absent by default (optional feature) | Not yet verified |
| Desktop Safari | 16.4 | WebGL2 on by default, `OfflineAudioContext` and `AudioContext.resume()` stable, Pointer Events | Not yet verified |
| iOS Safari | 16.4 | Same engine as desktop Safari 16.4; multi-touch Pointer Events subject to OQ-1 | Not yet verified |
| Android Chrome | 110 | Same as desktop Chromium; mobile tier selection | Not yet verified |

Policy:

1. A browser is published as Supported in `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`, `README.md` and
   SCR-About only after every XT test for it passes in Phase 15 on the delivered
   `FingerLickinMusic.html` opened from `file://` and from `http://` (E 9, I 17 last
   paragraph, P 18). A browser with failing XT tests is published as Partial with the list
   of failing capabilities, or Unsupported.
2. Until Phase 15 every claim reads "not yet verified"; the Phase 16 final report (Part 14)
   replaces that text with the recorded browser version, device, OS and date.
3. Compatibility is never inferred from the engine name (B 5.1); iOS Safari and desktop
   Safari are tested separately, and so are Android Chrome and desktop Chromium.
4. Other Chromium-based browsers (Brave, Opera, Samsung Internet) are not tested and not
   claimed; the About screen does not mention them.

Local-file (`file://`) behaviors to verify per browser. Each row becomes XT tests in
Part 12; `Caps` (M-01) detects the runtime facts at boot so the fallbacks switch
automatically.

| Behavior | What to verify on `file://` | Fallback when unavailable | Where the result is recorded |
|---|---|---|---|
| IndexedDB availability and persistence | `indexedDB.open('flm-db')` succeeds; records survive reload; quota via `navigator.storage.estimate()` when present | localStorage-only path with the 2 MB project cap and the notice of Part 6.16 (`E-STO-009`) | Part 9.2 device matrix, `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` |
| localStorage availability | Read and write of `flm.v1.*` keys inside try/catch; private-mode behavior | Session-only settings; export offered on every save | Same |
| Audio unlock | `AudioContext` created on the first gesture reaches `running`; iOS needs the silent-buffer kick; `statechange` to `suspended` after backgrounding re-unlocks through DLG-ResumeAudio | DLG-AudioBlocked with a retry button; the game never auto-plays before the gesture | Same |
| File import | `<input type=file>` opens and returns a `File`; drag and drop onto `#app` works; `.mxl` and `.gp5` are not filtered out by the accept list | Drag and drop; a hint naming it | Same |
| Download | `a[download]` with a Blob URL saves `.mid`, `.flm.json` and `.wav` with the given file name | Open a data URL in a new tab with instructions to save it | Same |
| History API | `history.pushState` per screen does not throw (Part 7.4) | Hash-based navigation (`#/screen`) selected automatically when `pushState` throws | Same |
| Secure context and Web MIDI | `window.isSecureContext`; `navigator.requestMIDIAccess` presence; permission prompt behavior | MIDI row disabled with its reason (1.5) | Same |
| Multi-touch Pointer Events | Four simultaneous `pointerdown` events with distinct `pointerId` on the pads (OQ-1) | Touch Events listener path if XT tests fail on any supported device | Same, plus the LEDGER assumptions section |
| WebGL2, WebGL1, context attributes | Context creation per tier; `webglcontextlost` recovery within 3 s | WebGL1, then Abstract tier (`canvas#flat`) | Same |
| `OfflineAudioContext` render of a full mix | WAV export of a 2 min project completes within memory on iOS (OQ-2) | MediaRecorder capture of the live mix | Same |
| Background throttling | Timers and `requestAnimationFrame` stall while hidden; `visibilitychange` fires; the Transport re-anchors on return and logs drift > 5 ms | Auto-pause in gameplay modes (Part 6.4) | Same |

### 1.7 Built-in content summary

Five original demo arrangements (ADR-14) ship as compact data in `src/30-content.js`
(M-30). Titles, chord progressions and melodies are invented for this product; no
copyrighted melodies are used. Each arrangement ships with instrument charts at four
difficulties for every melodic track (drums use profile F) and a dance chart at three
difficulties, all generated deterministically by `ChartGenerator` and
`DanceChartGenerator` at load time from the expanded `Song` (not hand-authored), and with
section `Marker`s for every section named below. Note data, patterns and the expansion
algorithm are specified in Part 6.30. Lengths are computed from the tempo and meter data
given here. GM program numbers are 0-based.

| id | Title | Style | BPM | Key | Meter | Length (s) | Tracks and GM programs | Notable features exercised |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `demo-poprock` | Neon Boulevard | Pop-rock band | 120 | G major | 4/4, 48 bars | 96.0 | Drums (channel 10), Bass 33 Electric Bass (finger), Rhythm Guitar 27 Electric Guitar (clean), Lead Guitar 29 Overdriven Guitar, Keys 4 Electric Piano 1 | Four-note strummed chords (G, D, Em, C voicings; chord size 4 and lane-by-pitch-order rules), eighth-note repeated-note bass, lead melody with clear melodic peaks (beginner selection rule), rock kit (36 kick, 38 snare, 42 and 46 hats, 49 crash at section starts), velocity step verse 80 to chorus 110, five performers filling all slots; sections Intro 4, Verse 8, Chorus 8, Verse 8, Chorus 8, Bridge 4, Chorus 8 |

| `demo-electro` | Circuit Bloom | Electronic | 110 | A minor | 4/4, 44 bars | 96.0 | Drums (channel 10), Synth Bass 39 Synth Bass 2, Arp 80 Lead 1 (square), Pad 88 Pad 1 (new age), Lead 81 Lead 2 (sawtooth) | Sixteenth-note arpeggios (expert density and min-spacing rules), `PitchBendEvent`s on the lead (2-semitone range, RPN 0 declared), CC 1 modulation sweep on the pad (synth knob gesture), four-on-the-floor 36 kick with 39 clap and 46 open hat offbeats, three- and four-note pad chords sustained 2 bars, a 4-bar break with pad only (long drum rest); sections Intro 8, Build 8, Drop 16, Break 4, Drop 8 |

Coverage across the set: one tempo change (`demo-piano`), one meter change (`demo-jazz`),
dense chords (`demo-poprock`, `demo-jazz`), sustain pedal (`demo-piano`), pitch bend and
CC 1 (`demo-electro`), CC 11 (`demo-dance`), sixteenth density (`demo-electro`), swing
grid (`demo-jazz`), every drum voice of the 12-voice kit used at least once across the
five drum tracks, one single-track song, one three-track song, three five-track songs.
Total expanded note count target 4,000-7,000 across the set so content expansion stays
within the load budget (Part 9.4).

Tutorial sequence (ADR-14): `tut-basics` "First Steps", C major, 100 BPM, 4/4, 16 bars
(38.4 s), tracks Piano 0 (the player's part) and Drums (channel 10, a simple 36/38/42
pattern). Its seven step segments and the 4-bar recording loop are specified in Part 6.30.

Quick Play default selection (P 4 "start a built-in demo without importing a file"):
`demo-poprock`, track Keys, difficulty beginner, profile A, backing tracks on,
visualization on. The last selection is remembered in settings after the first play.

Character presets: the 8 named presets of Part 6.22 are content data in M-30 and populate
the five performer slots of the demo arrangements by default (slot assignment per
arrangement in Part 6.30).

### 1.8 Non-goals for v1

The following are explicitly outside v1. They are not Deferred requirements; they are not
requirements. Any of them appearing in a status report or the About screen as a feature is
a defect.

- Accounts, sign-in, cloud saves, telemetry, analytics or any outbound request other than
  the optional STUN lookup and the optional relay connection (ADR-15, B 23.2).
- Public matchmaking, room discovery lists, spectator mode, in-game text or voice chat,
  global leaderboards; all progression is local to the device.
- A bundled or downloaded sampled sound bank; any claim of acoustic fidelity (ADR-04).
- Audio-to-MIDI transcription, beat or tempo detection for imported audio, time-stretch or
  speed change of audio tracks (audio tracks play at 1.0 speed only; Part 8.12).
- Sheet music, tablature or notation display; MusicXML or Guitar Pro export.
- DAW-grade features: automation lanes, per-track effects, plugin formats, audio clip
  editing, microphone recording, MIDI output to external devices (Web MIDI is input only).
- Imported 3D models, textures or fonts; a stage or character model importer; a mod or
  plugin system; shaders beyond the ones specified in Part 6.18.
- Localization: v1 is English only; all user-facing strings live in the Part 7.11 catalog
  so a later localization does not touch module code.
- Service worker, web app manifest, PWA install or native wrappers; the single file is the
  offline mechanism (ADR-01).
- Minification, obfuscation or transpiling of the shipped source (B 19.4, ADR-09).
- Guitar Pro 6 and 7 import, Collaborative Studio, two players on one keyboard, host
  migration, late join during a song (all decided in 1.5).
- Any copyrighted melody, lyric, sample or artwork (B 23.3); every demo is original.
- Support claims for browsers, devices or formats without recorded XT and FT evidence
  (B 1.4, I 6.4, I 17).

## 2. Architecture and technology decisions

This part elaborates the sixteen fixed architecture decisions ADR-01 to ADR-16. Each decision
is final; later parts cite them as `ADR-NN` and may cite a numbered sub-decision as
"ADR-NN decision k". Every "Alternatives considered" table scores each alternative on the
nine B 19.3 criteria with an integer 1-5 (5 = best for this product), total out of 45. The
scores are planning judgments made at plan version 1.0.0, not measurements; the chosen row is
marked `(chosen)`. "Verification" names the test categories of Part 12 (UT, IT, FT, TT, PT,
XT, FI, LT, AT) and the observable each must establish; test IDs are assigned in Part 12.

Browser floor assumed throughout this part (the support policy itself is 1.6): Chromium 110,
Edge 110, Firefox 115, Safari 16.4, iOS Safari 16.4, Android Chrome 110. A claim about any browser is
published only after its XT tests pass (B 5.1).

### 2.1 ADR-01 Single-file delivery via a build step

Context: B 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 19.4, E 9, I 14.1, 14.3, P 18. The primary artifact must open
directly from disk without a build pipeline, yet the source must stay maintainable as about
31 modules plus tests. `ClassTimeKiller/` in this repository already uses a concatenating
build with a marker and is the precedent.

Decision:

1. Source lives in `Finger Lickin Music/src/`: `shell.html` plus module files
   `NN-name.js` (two-digit prefix, lower-case kebab name, exactly the names in BRIEF
   section 4 / Part 3.1). Test modules are `90-selftest.js` and `91-test-<group>.js`.
2. `node tools/build.mjs` reads `shell.html`, finds the marker `/*@@SCRIPT@@*/` (which must
   occur exactly once, inside the single application `<script>`), and replaces it with the
   module files joined in byte-wise ascending file-name order. Before each file the build
   inserts one banner line `/* @@FILE src/NN-name.js @@ */` so a line number in a stack
   trace can be mapped back; the build prints a "file -> first output line" table to stdout.
3. Two outputs in `Finger Lickin Music/`: `FingerLickinMusic.html` (modules `0*`-`3*` only;
   committed to the repository so players never need Node) and
   `FingerLickinMusic.test.html` (same plus `9*-*.js`; gitignored). No other output files.
4. Every input file may carry a UTF-8 BOM; the build strips them all and emits exactly one
   BOM at byte 0 of each output. All CRLF and lone CR are normalized to LF. Output encoding
   is UTF-8.
5. Size gate on each output: warn above the envelope of the current phase (read from the "Current phase" line of docs/STATUS.md, LEDGER OI-45), fail (exit code 3, no file written) above
   2.5 MB. The gate applies to the shipped file; the test file is reported but not failed.
6. Syntax gate: the joined script (without the HTML wrapper) is written to a temporary file
   in the OS temp directory and checked with `node --check`; a failure aborts the build with
   exit code 2 and the node error text.
7. Version stamping: the build reads the `VERSION = 'x.y.z'` constant from `01-core.js`
   (regular expression `/VERSION\s*=\s*'(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)'/`), fails if absent, and writes
   an HTML comment `<!-- Finger Lickin Music vX.Y.Z built YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ -->` as the
   first line after the doctype. `FLM.VERSION` at runtime comes from the constant, not from
   the comment.
8. Flags: `--check` builds to memory only (all gates, no files); `--online <relayUrl>`
   widens `connect-src` in the CSP meta to include the relay origin (`ws:` or `wss:` scheme
   as given) and sets `FLM.Core.BUILD.relayUrl`; without the flag the Standalone edition is
   built. The build never fetches anything.
9. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 usage or missing input, 2 syntax gate, 3 size gate.
10. The shipped file is a plain HTML document: one `<style>`, one inline SVG symbol sprite,
    the DOM scaffold, one tiny early error-handler `<script>` (fewer than 40 lines, no
    dependency on modules) and the single application `<script>`. No `<script src>`, no
    `<link>`, no `@import`, no `url()` other than `data:`.
11. Working with the source is optional for anyone but the implementing session; a change to
    the game is a change to `src/` followed by a rebuild and a commit of both source and the
    rebuilt shipped file in the same commit.

Alternatives considered:

| Alternative | Browser compat | Mobile perf | File size | License | Maint | Security | Func compl | Offline | Single-file | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hand-edit one monolithic HTML file, no build | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 1 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 39 |
| ES modules, many files served from a folder | 3 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 34 |
| npm bundler (esbuild or rollup) | 5 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 3 | 5 | 3 | 5 | 39 |
| Own Node concatenation at a marker (chosen) | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 43 |

Notes: ES modules fail on `file://` (module scripts are blocked by CORS in Chromium and
Firefox). An npm bundler needs network installs that are not available (ADR-02). Hand-editing
one 1 MB file is not maintainable for 31 modules and a test suite.

Consequences: easier - players open one file; stack traces stay readable (no minification);
tests ship separately without touching the player build. Harder - every edit needs a rebuild
before testing in the browser; the repository stores the built artifact, so the shipped file
and `src/` must be committed together (the T sections in Part 11 make the rebuild part of
every step). Limits the UI must disclose: none; the About screen states "Single file, no
build needed to play".

Verification: FT (the shipped file is byte-checked: single BOM, LF only, size, marker
absent, no external references); UT for `tools/build.mjs` run through `node` (ordering,
BOM stripping, size gate, exit codes); XT (the delivered file opens from `file://` in the five
browsers); LT (final file validated independently of the development folder, P 18).

### 2.2 ADR-02 Zero runtime dependencies

Context: B 5.3, 11.2, 12.6, 19.3, 19.5, 23.3, E 9, I 14.2, P 18. The spec permits libraries
when licensing and size allow, but demands a documented loading and failure strategy. The
development environment blocks CDNs, so no library can be fetched during implementation;
all three existing games in the repository ship their own renderers with zero dependencies.

Decision:

1. The shipped HTML contains no third-party code, fonts, images, sound data or models. The
   runtime dependency inventory (2.17) has exactly zero rows.
2. three.js was evaluated and rejected: MIT licensed, about 650 KB minified (43 percent of the
   1.5 MB target), its UMD build was discontinued after r160 so embedding a current release
   needs a module-to-IIFE wrapping step, and it cannot be fetched in the development
   environment. The own renderer (ADR-03) covers the required feature set (capsules and
   boxes, Lambert shading, blob shadows, instancing).
3. Audio libraries (Tone.js, WebAudioFont, soundfont-player), parser libraries (midi-file,
   @tonejs/midi, alphaTab, opensheetmusicdisplay) and compression libraries (pako, fflate,
   JSZip) are all rejected for the same reasons: unavailable offline in development, and each
   would still need the game's own scheduler, model and limits around it.
4. Reference use is allowed, copying is not: a public specification or a library's documented
   behavior may be consulted to understand a format; no third-party source text is pasted
   into `src/`. Every line in `src/` is original to this project.
5. The About screen (SCR-About) lists "Third-party code: none" and "Fonts, sounds, models:
   none; all content is original and synthesized".
6. Optional external resources remain exactly three and are all network services, never
   code: the public STUN server (ADR-07, off by default), the optional relay (ADR-07) and a
   user-loaded SoundFont file (ADR-04, Deferred P2). None is fetched without an explicit user
   action.

Alternatives considered:

| Alternative | Browser compat | Mobile perf | File size | License | Maint | Security | Func compl | Offline | Single-file | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Embed three.js (r160 UMD) for rendering | 5 | 4 | 2 | 5 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 37 |
| Embed Tone.js for audio | 4 | 3 | 2 | 5 | 3 | 4 | 3 | 5 | 4 | 33 |
| Embed alphaTab for GP and MusicXML | 4 | 3 | 1 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 5 | 5 | 3 | 30 |
| Load libraries from a CDN at runtime | 4 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 5 | 1 | 1 | 29 |
| Embed pako or fflate for inflate | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 41 |
| No third-party code at all (chosen) | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 43 |

Notes: fflate scores well but cannot be obtained in the development environment and an RFC
1951 inflate is about 300 lines (M-11). alphaTab is MPL-2.0 and over 1 MB because it is an
engraver, which the spec explicitly separates from event import (B 15.3).

Consequences: easier - licensing review is trivial; offline and `file://` behavior is
deterministic; no supply-chain risk. Harder - every parser, the renderer, inflate and the
synthesizer are own code with own tests (Parts 6 and 12 size the test minimums
accordingly); timbral fidelity is limited to synthesis (ADR-04). Limits the UI must
disclose: "All instrument sounds are synthesized" on SCR-About, SCR-Settings (audio section)
and SCR-ImportInspect.

Verification: FT (static scan of the shipped file: no `<script src`, `<link`, `@import`,
`http://`, `https://` outside the About text and the STUN constant; a grep gate in
`tools/build.mjs`); XT (offline open: network disabled, every mode but Multiplayer works);
LT (license inventory review, P 20).

### 2.3 ADR-03 Rendering: own WebGL renderer with a 2D Abstract tier

Context: B 12.1-12.7, 20.2, 21.3, E 6.1, 6.2, I 4.1-4.4, 12.1, P 7.1-7.3, 17. The spec
requires a scene graph, camera system, rig, event-driven animation, quality tiers, capability
detection, resource disposal and graceful fallback down to a non-3D visualization, and asks
for a comparison of a library against custom WebGL (resolved in ADR-02).

Decision:

1. Context acquisition order in M-18: `canvas#view.getContext('webgl2', attrs)`, then
   `getContext('webgl', attrs)`, then `getContext('experimental-webgl', attrs)`; if all
   return null or throw, the Abstract tier is selected and `canvas#flat` (2D context) is
   shown instead of `#view`. `attrs = {alpha:false, antialias:<tier>, depth:true,
   stencil:false, premultipliedAlpha:false, preserveDrawingBuffer:false,
   powerPreference:'high-performance', failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat:false}`.
2. Four quality tiers: `High`, `Balanced`, `Low`, `Abstract`. Parameters (the full table is
   9.3; these values are normative):

| Parameter | High | Balanced | Low | Abstract |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Resolution scale (of CSS px x devicePixelRatio) | 1.0 (DPR capped at 2) | 0.75 (DPR capped at 2) | 0.5 (DPR capped at 1.5) | n/a (2D canvas at DPR capped 2) |
| MSAA (`antialias` attr) | on | on | off | n/a |
| Lights | 1 directional + ambient + 4 point | 1 directional + ambient + 2 point | 1 directional + ambient | n/a |
| Blob shadows | on | on | off | n/a |
| Capsule segments (radial x height) | 16 x 8 | 10 x 6 | 6 x 4 | n/a |
| Particles cap (perfect sparks, beat pulses) | 256 | 96 | 0 | 0 |
| Performers animated per frame | 5 | 5 | 3 (others idle pose) | 0 (visualizer only) |
| Highway | 3D lanes in `#view` | 3D lanes | 3D lanes, no glow | 2D lanes in `#flat` |
| Animation update rate | every frame | every frame | every 2nd frame | n/a |

3. Initial tier selection at boot (M-29 reads `Caps`): WebGL2 present and not a touch device
   (`navigator.maxTouchPoints === 0`) and `min(innerWidth, innerHeight) >= 600` -> High;
   WebGL2 present otherwise -> Balanced; WebGL1 only -> Low; no WebGL -> Abstract. A stored
   setting `video.tier` other than `auto` overrides the pick and disables auto-downgrade.
   URL parameter `?tier=<name>` (M-29) overrides both for that session.
4. Auto-downgrade: M-18 keeps a 300-frame ring of frame times; when the p95 over the last
   5 s exceeds 33 ms the tier drops by one step (`High -> Balanced -> Low -> Abstract`),
   at most once per 10 s, with a toast "Graphics quality lowered to <tier> to keep the music
   smooth". There is no automatic upgrade; the user can raise the tier in SCR-Settings. The
   check is suspended during the first 3 s after a mode enter and while a dialog is open.
5. Shading: flat or Lambert per material, one directional light, ambient term, up to 4
   point lights (High), simple linear fog, per-instance color. No shadow maps; shadows are
   blob quads with a radial gradient texture generated at init on a 64 x 64 canvas. No
   post-processing passes.
