#### 6.30.9 Implementation notes and browser quirks

- Type the data exactly as written; the bar checks (`|`) and the count table catch typing
  errors. Do not "fix" musical content without updating the count table and the LEDGER.
- Note names use `#` and `b` only (no double accidentals); `Bb1` is MIDI 34, `C6` is 84.
- `Model.Track.create` assigns default ids with `uid()`; the expander passes explicit ids, so
  determinism does not depend on `uid()`.
- The expander runs inside the Catalog's `expand` closure on first use, which happens in the
  user's click handler for Play; 50 ms is inside the time-to-first-playable budget (5 s desktop).

### 6.31 M-31 SelfTest (`src/90-selftest.js`, `src/91-test-*.js`, `src/92-test-*.js`, `FLM.SelfTest`)

#### 6.31.1 Responsibilities and non-goals

Responsibilities (test build only; ADR-11): the in-page test runner (`group`, `test`, async
tests, per-test timeout, slow filter, grep, skip), the assertion set, the fakes (fake clock,
fake timers, in-memory IndexedDB, in-memory localStorage, `OfflineAudioContext` helpers, input
synthesis, stubs and spies), the corpus store fed by `tools/selftest.mjs`, the performance
scenario registry used by `tools/perf.mjs`, the results object and `window.__FLM_RESULTS`,
the group leak check through `FLM.Modes.assertClean()`, and the "Run self-test" panel content
on SCR-Diagnostics.

Non-goals: no test content beyond the runner's own tests (`UT-31-*`); module tests live in
`91-test-<module>.js` and cross-module tests (IT, TT, FT, FI, PT smoke) in `92-test-<group>.js`
(Part 12). Nothing of this module exists in `FingerLickinMusic.html` (the build excludes
`9*-*.js`; the smoke check fails when `FLM.selfTest` exists in the shipped file).

#### 6.31.2 Public API

```js
FLM.Core.define('SelfTest', function (FLM) {
  return Object.freeze({
    VERSION: '1.0.0',
    /** The 36 group names of Part 3.1, in run order. */
    KNOWN_GROUPS: ['core','theory','model','transport','audio','instruments','input','mapping','rhythm','midi',
                   'zip','musicxml','guitarpro','import','project','storage','studio','render','rig','animation',
                   'stage','character','dance','net','progress','ui','screens','modes','boot','content','selftest',
                   'integration','timing','files','faults','perf-smoke'],
    /** Register a group. fn(t) runs immediately and declares tests with t.test; a second
     *  registration of the same name appends. Unknown names throw (the list above is closed). */
    group(name, fn) {},
    /** Add one test to a registered group (same as t.test inside the group callback). */
    test(groupName, name, opts, fn) {},
    /** Run groups. groups: undefined (all), a name, or an array. opts: {slow, grep, touch, timeoutMs}.
     *  Assigns window.__FLM_RESULTS and resolves to the results object (6.31.4.4). Never rejects. */
    run(groups, opts) /* -> Promise<Results> */ {},
    /** [{name, tests, slow}] for the registered groups (diagnostics panel). */
    groups() {},
    results() /* -> last Results or null */ {},
    progress() /* -> {running:boolean, group:string|null, index:int, total:int, passed:int, failed:int} */ {},
    RESULT_SHAPE: /* frozen description of the results object (6.31.4.4) */ {},
    /** Isolated runner with its own registry (used by UT-31 tests to test the runner). */
    createRunner() /* -> {group, run, groups} */ {},

    assert: { eq, deepEq, near, within, ok, throws, rejects },   // also available as t.eq etc.
    fakes: {
      FakeClock /* class; clock(start) returns new FakeClock(start) */, FakeIndexedDB /* class; indexedDB(opts) returns an instance */,
      clock(startSec /* = 0 */) /* -> FakeClock */ {},
      timers() /* -> FakeTimers (install/uninstall/advance) */ {},
      indexedDB(opts) /* -> FakeIndexedDB factory */ {},
      localStorage() /* -> FakeStorage */ {},
      offlineContext(opts /* {seconds, sampleRate:48000, channels:2} */) /* -> Promise<OfflineAudioContext> */ {},
      onsets(audioBuffer, opts /* {threshold:0.05, channel:0} */) /* -> number[] seconds */ {},
      inputs: { key(code, down, tPerf), tap(lane, tPerf, holdMs), pointer(id, type, x, y, tPerf, pointerType),
                gamepad(state), midi(bytes, tPerf), event(control, type, tAudio, source) },
      stub(obj, method, impl) /* -> Spy (auto-restored after the test) */ {},
      spy(fn) /* -> Spy */ {}
    },
    corpus: { load(entries), has(file), get(file) /* -> {bytes:Uint8Array, recipe, format, expect} */, list(), loaded() },
    perf:   { register(name, fn), run(name, opts) /* -> Promise<{name, durationMs, metrics, notes}> */, list() }
  });
});

/** The t object passed to group callbacks. */
TestContext {
  test(name /* 'UT-NN-nn sentence' */, opts /* ?{slow:boolean, timeoutMs:number, touch:boolean} */, fn /* async ok */),
  before(fn), after(fn),               // once per group run
  beforeEach(fn), afterEach(fn),
  skip(reason) /* throws the Skip signal */,
  eq(actual, expected, msg), deepEq(actual, expected, msg), near(a, b, eps, msg), within(x, lo, hi, msg), ok(cond, msg),
  throws(fn, codePrefix /* ?'E-CNT-001' */, msg), rejects(promiseOrFn, codePrefix, msg) /* async */,
  fakes, corpus, options /* {slow, touch, grep} of the current run */
}
FakeClock { now() /* seconds */, advance(sec), set(sec) }
FakeTimers { install(), uninstall(), advance(ms) /* runs due timeouts, intervals and RAF callbacks in time order */, pending() }
Spy { calls: [{args, result, error}], count, last(), reset(), restore() }
```

Events: none emitted, none consumed (tests subscribe to topics they assert on, with an owner
token removed in `afterEach`).

#### 6.31.3 Internal state

```js
registry: Map<groupName, {name, tests:[{name, opts, fn}], hooks:{before:[], after:[], beforeEach:[], afterEach:[]}}>
running: null | {group, index, total, passed, failed}
lastResults: null | Results
activeStubs: Spy[]            // restored after every test
corpus: Map<file, {bytes, recipe, format, expect}>
perfScenarios: Map<name, fn>
```

Invariants: tests run strictly one at a time; `activeStubs` is empty between tests; the
registry is never modified while `running` is non-null (a `group` call during a run throws).

#### 6.31.4 Algorithms

6.31.4.1 `run(groups, opts)`

```js
async function run(groups, opts = {}) {
  const startedAt = new Date().toISOString();
  const wanted = groups === undefined ? KNOWN_GROUPS : [].concat(groups);
  const unknown = wanted.filter(g => !KNOWN_GROUPS.includes(g));
  const order = KNOWN_GROUPS.filter(g => wanted.includes(g) && registry.has(g));
  const res = {version: FLM.SelfTest.VERSION, build: FLM.VERSION + ' ' + (FLM.BUILD && FLM.BUILD.date) + ' test',
    userAgent: navigator.userAgent, startedAt, finishedAt: null,
    options: {groups: groups === undefined ? null : wanted, slow: !!opts.slow, grep: opts.grep || '', touch: !!opts.touch},
    known: KNOWN_GROUPS.slice(), unknown, groups: [], tests: [], total: 0, passed: 0, failed: 0, skipped: 0, pageErrors: []};
  if (FLM.Modes.current().mode !== 'menu') await FLM.Modes.leave('user');
  for (const g of order) await runGroup(registry.get(g), opts, res);
  res.finishedAt = new Date().toISOString();
  lastResults = res; window.__FLM_RESULTS = res;
  return res;
}
```

`runGroup(group, opts, res)`:

1. `t0 = performance.now()`; run `before` hooks (a throwing hook fails every test of the group
   with message `before hook: <message>` and skips to step 4).
2. For each test in registration order: skip silently (not counted) when `test.opts.slow &&
   !opts.slow`, when `opts.grep` is set and `(group + '/' + name).toLowerCase()` does not
   contain it, or when `test.opts.touch === true && !opts.touch`; otherwise `runTest`.
3. `runTest`: `beforeEach` hooks; `limit = test.opts.timeoutMs || opts.timeoutMs ||
   (test.opts.slow ? 60000 : 10000)`; `outcome = await Promise.race([Promise.resolve().then(() =>
   test.fn(t)), timeout(limit)])` where `timeout` rejects with `Error('timeout after ' + limit +
   ' ms')`; result `{group, name, pass: true, skipped: false, ms, message: ''}`, or `pass:false`
   with `message = err.message` (first 500 chars) for assertion failures and thrown errors, or
   `skipped:true, pass:true, message: reason` for `t.skip`; `afterEach` hooks run in `finally`;
   all `activeStubs` are restored, fake timers uninstalled, test-owned bus listeners removed
   (`bus.removeOwner(testOwner)`).
4. `after` hooks; leak check: if `FLM.Modes.current().mode !== 'menu'` -> `await
   FLM.Modes.leave('user')`; `leaks = FLM.Modes.assertClean()`; non-null -> append `{group, name:
   group + ' leak check', pass:false, skipped:false, ms:0, message: JSON.stringify(leaks)}`.
5. Append the group row `{name, total, passed, failed, skipped, ms}` and add to the totals.

A test that times out keeps running in the background (JavaScript cannot cancel it); the
runner marks it failed and continues; its later side effects are contained by the leak check.

6.31.4.2 Assertions

| Assertion | Pass condition | Failure message |
|---|---|---|
| `eq(a, b)` | `Object.is(a, b)` or both `NaN` | `expected <b> but got <a>` (values via `JSON.stringify`, 200 chars) |
| `deepEq(a, b)` | structural equality: same prototype class for arrays and plain objects, same own enumerable keys, recursive; typed arrays element-wise; `Map` and `Set` by entries | first differing path, e.g. `at tracks[2].events[5].tick: expected 960 got 959` |
| `near(a, b, eps)` | `abs(a - b) <= eps` | `expected <b> +/- <eps> but got <a>` |
| `within(x, lo, hi)` | `lo <= x && x <= hi` | `expected <x> in [<lo>, <hi>]` |
| `ok(c)` | truthy | `assertion failed: <msg>` |
| `throws(fn, prefix)` | `fn` throws and, when given, `String(err.code or err.message)` starts with `prefix` | `expected a throw` or `expected code <prefix> but got <code>` |
| `rejects(p, prefix)` | promise rejects (a function is called and its result awaited) with the same prefix rule | as throws |

Assertions throw `AssertionError` (a subclass of `Error` with `name = 'AssertionError'`).

6.31.4.3 Fakes

- `clock(start)`: `{now: () => s, advance(d) { s += d; }, set(v) { s = v; }}`; passed to
  `FLM.Transport.create({clock, bus})` (06a) and to judge time maps.
- `timers()`: `install()` replaces `window.setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`, `setInterval`,
  `clearInterval`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `cancelAnimationFrame` and `performance.now` with
  versions on a virtual clock starting at the real `performance.now()`; `advance(ms)` runs every
  due callback in time order (intervals re-queued, RAF callbacks at 16.667 ms steps with the
  virtual time as argument); `uninstall()` restores the originals (also done automatically after
  each test). M-01's wrappers look up the window functions at call time, so code under test goes
  through the fake (requirement noted in 6.31.9).
- `indexedDB(opts)`: an in-memory factory implementing what M-16 uses: `open(name, version)` with
  `onupgradeneeded`, `onsuccess`, `onerror`, `onblocked`; `db.createObjectStore(name, {keyPath})`,
  `store.createIndex(name, keyPath, {unique})`; `db.transaction(stores, mode)` with
  `objectStore().get/put/delete/getAll/clear`, `index().get/getAll`, `oncomplete`, `onerror`,
  `onabort`; requests settle asynchronously in microtask order; values are stored with
  `structuredClone` (so Blobs survive). Fault options: `{hangOpen:true}` (never fires success),
  `failNextWrite:'QuotaExceededError'|'AbortError'`, `quotaBytes:int` (puts beyond the total size
  fail with `QuotaExceededError`), `corruptOnRead:id` (returns a damaged record once).
- `localStorage()`: `getItem`, `setItem` (with a `quotaBytes` option throwing a DOMException
  named `QuotaExceededError`), `removeItem`, `key`, `length`, `clear`.
- `offlineContext({seconds, sampleRate = 48000, channels = 2})`: `new OfflineAudioContext(channels,
  ceil(seconds * sampleRate), sampleRate)`; `onsets(buffer, {threshold, channel})` returns the times
  where `abs(sample)` first exceeds the threshold after at least 10 ms below it, used by the
  scheduling-precision tests (onset within 1 ms of the intended time).
- `inputs`: wrappers over `FLM.Input.synthesize` (06b) so synthesized events go through the real
  handlers; `event(control, type, tAudio, source)` emits a ready-made `input.event` payload for
  judge-level tests (`tPerf` computed back through the anchor).
- `stub(obj, method, impl)`: saves `obj[method]`, replaces it with a spy that records calls and
  delegates to `impl` (or returns undefined), and restores it after the test. Decision for
  stubbing namespaces: `FLM.Core.define` freezes namespace objects only in the shipped build
  (`FLM.BUILD.test === false`); in the test build it applies `Object.seal` recursively to the
  namespace and its nested plain objects (members stay replaceable, nothing can be added), while
  the exported data tables of S-07 are deep-frozen in both builds. A stub therefore replaces
  cross-module calls (`FLM.Storage.pickFile`), never a module's internal closures; stubbing a
  frozen table throws `cannot stub frozen <method>`.

6.31.4.4 Results object

The shape of Part 3.4.4 (the contract read by `tools/selftest.mjs`):

```json
{ "version": "1.0.0", "build": "1.0.0 2026-11-02 test", "userAgent": "...",
  "startedAt": "ISO", "finishedAt": "ISO",
  "options": { "groups": null, "slow": false, "grep": "", "touch": false },
  "known": ["core", "..."], "unknown": [],
  "groups": [ { "name": "core", "total": 28, "passed": 28, "failed": 0, "skipped": 0, "ms": 120 } ],
  "tests": [ { "group": "core", "name": "UT-01-01 define registers namespace", "pass": true, "skipped": false, "ms": 1, "message": "" } ],
  "total": 28, "passed": 28, "failed": 0, "skipped": 0, "pageErrors": [] }
```

Every `tests[]` entry carries at least `{group, name, pass, ms, message}` (ADR-11); `skipped` is
added. `pageErrors` is filled by the tool, not by the runner. An unknown group name appears in
`unknown` and contributes zero tests (the tool fails the run, 3.4.1).

6.31.4.5 Corpus and performance hooks

- `corpus.load(entries)`: for each `{file, base64, fnv1a32, recipe, format, expect}`: decode base64
  to a `Uint8Array` (`atob` then byte copy), compute `fnv1a32` over the byte values (the same
  algorithm as `Core.fnv1a32` applied to bytes 0..255 instead of UTF-16 code units, matching
  `tools/make-corpus.mjs`), compare; a mismatch records the file in `corpus.errors` and every test
  of the `files` group fails with `corpus hash mismatch: <file>` (3.4.3 step 4a). `has(file)` and
  `get(file)` serve tests; tests needing the corpus call `t.skip('corpus not loaded (run
  tools/selftest.mjs)')` when `!corpus.loaded()`.
- `perf.register(name, fn)` is called by `92-test-perf-smoke.js` for every Part 9.7 scenario; `perf.
  run(name, {durationMs})` leaves any mode, runs `fn(opts)` (which enters modes and measures),
  leaves again, and resolves `{name, durationMs, metrics, notes}`; unknown names resolve `{name,
  durationMs:0, metrics:{}, notes:['unknown scenario']}`.

6.31.4.6 Self-test panel on SCR-Diagnostics (test build)

Shown only when `FLM.SelfTest` exists. Content: group checklist (all `KNOWN_GROUPS` with test
counts from `groups()`), "Include slow tests" toggle, filter field (grep), buttons "Run
selected" and "Run all", a progress line from `progress()` polled every 250 ms ("Running audio
(5 of 36), 112 passed, 0 failed"), the results table (group, total, pass, fail, skip, ms), the
failure list (`group/name :: message`), "Copy results JSON" (`JSON.stringify(results, null, 2)`
through the clipboard helper), and the notice "corpus not loaded (run tools/selftest.mjs)" when
the corpus is empty. Running: the panel calls `await Modes.leave('user')`, `r = await
FLM.selfTest(groups, {slow, grep, touch: document.body.classList.contains('touch')})`,
`Settings.set('diagnostics.selfTestLastRun', r.finishedAt, 'ui')`, then `Modes.enter(
'diagnostics', {selfTestResults: r})`, which renders the stored results. The test build also
shows the `TEST BUILD` badge on SCR-MainMenu (6.27.4.4).

#### 6.31.5 Error handling and recovery

| What can fail | Detection | State that remains valid | Retry | User data at risk | User informed how | Degraded mode | Return to known-good | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A test throws or fails | try/catch per test | runner and other tests | rerun | test data only (tests use fakes; storage tests use the fake IndexedDB) | result entry with message | n/a | next test | UT-31-02 |
| A test hangs | timeout race | runner continues | rerun | no | `timeout after <ms> ms` | n/a | next test | UT-31-05 |
| A test leaks resources | group leak check | runner | n/a | no | failed `<group> leak check` entry | n/a | `Modes.leave` before the next group | UT-31-15 |
| A stub is not restored | `activeStubs` restore in finally | original functions | n/a | no | n/a | n/a | automatic | UT-31-12 |
| Corpus bytes corrupted in transit | fnv1a32 check | other groups | rerun the tool | no | `corpus hash mismatch` failures | files group fails | regenerate corpus | UT-31-16 |
| Unknown group requested | name check | n/a | n/a | no | `unknown` list; tool exit 1 | n/a | n/a | UT-31-09 |

#### 6.31.6 Limits and performance notes

- Per-test default timeout 10 s, slow tests 60 s (3.4.6); the whole `--all` run is expected to
  finish inside the tool's 240 s watchdog on the development machine.
- The runner adds < 1 ms overhead per test; results for about 700 tests serialize to < 300 KB.
- Fake IndexedDB keeps everything in memory; tests must not store more than 50 MB (the Chromium
  tab limit is far higher; the cap keeps runs fast).

#### 6.31.7 Spec coverage

B 1.4 (validate each subsystem before integrating the next), B 4.2 (automated tests for timing
and file handling), B 25.1-25.7 (unit, integration, file-format, timing, cross-device and
performance test infrastructure), E 12 and E 13 (test infrastructure for the added sections),
I 13.1 (fault injection through fakes and `FLM.debug.inject`), I 17 (automated quality gates,
regression tests), P 20 (testing and release quality).

#### 6.31.8 Unit tests (group `selftest`, file `src/91-test-selftest.js`)

All tests use `createRunner()` so the inner runs do not touch the real registry or
`window.__FLM_RESULTS` (except UT-31-10, which saves and restores it).

| ID | Name | Setup | Assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| UT-31-01 | passing test recorded | inner group with one passing test | result `pass:true`, `skipped:false`, `ms >= 0`, `message === ''` |
| UT-31-02 | failing assertion recorded | `t.eq(1, 2)` | `pass:false`; message `expected 2 but got 1`; the next test still runs |
| UT-31-03 | thrown error recorded | test throws `Error('boom')` | `pass:false`, message `boom` |
| UT-31-04 | async test awaited | test awaits a 20 ms timer then asserts | pass; `ms >= 20` |
| UT-31-05 | timeout | test with `{timeoutMs: 50}` awaiting a never-resolving promise | fail with `timeout after 50 ms`; the run finishes |
| UT-31-06 | skip | `t.skip('no WebGL2 in headless')` | `skipped:true`, `pass:true`, message is the reason; group `skipped` count 1 |
| UT-31-07 | slow filter | one slow and one normal test; run without and with `{slow:true}` | 1 test then 2 tests reported |
| UT-31-08 | grep filter | tests 'ZZ-01 alpha' and 'ZZ-02 beta'; grep 'BETA' | only the beta test reported |
| UT-31-09 | unknown group | `run('nonsense')` | `unknown` is ['nonsense'], total 0, `known` lists 36 names |
| UT-31-10 | results shape and global | top-level `run('selftest')` with an inner flag preventing recursion | `window.__FLM_RESULTS === returned object`; keys match `RESULT_SHAPE`; group row totals equal the sum of entries |
| UT-31-11 | assertion semantics | near(0.1 + 0.2, 0.3, 1e-12), within(5, 0, 5), deepEq on nested Map and Float32Array, throws with prefix, rejects with prefix | each passes; a deepEq mismatch message names the differing path |
| UT-31-12 | stubs restored | stub `Math.max` inside a test; next test calls `Math.max` | original behavior in the next test; `activeStubs` empty |
| UT-31-13 | fake clock with transport | `Transport.create({clock: fakes.clock(), bus: new Emitter()})`, load a 120 BPM song, play, advance 1 s | `Math.floor(positionAt(clock.now()))` equals 1,824 (06a anchors `play` at `now + 0.05`: (1.00 - 0.05) s x 1,920 ticks/s) |
| UT-31-14 | fake IndexedDB basics and faults | open v1 with upgrade creating a store and index; put, get, index getAll; then `failNextWrite` | values round-trip; the failing put fires `onerror` with name `QuotaExceededError` and the transaction aborts |
| UT-31-15 | group leak check | inner group whose test creates a `Core.timers.setInterval` with a foreign owner and does not clear it | an extra failed entry `<group> leak check` with `timers` in its message |
| UT-31-16 | corpus hash check | `corpus.load([{file:'a.mid', base64:'TVRoZA==', fnv1a32: 0}])` | `corpus.errors` contains a.mid; `has('a.mid') === false` |

#### 6.31.9 Implementation notes and browser quirks

- Fake timers require that `FLM.Core.timers` and `Core.now()` call `window.setTimeout`,
  `window.requestAnimationFrame` and `performance.now` at call time instead of caching them at
  load; this is a requirement on M-01 (6.1) recorded here so the 06a implementation honors it.
- `performance.now` is a method on `Performance.prototype`; the fake assigns an own property on
  the `performance` instance and deletes it on uninstall (works in Chromium, Firefox and Safari).
- `OfflineAudioContext` in headless Chromium renders faster than real time, which makes the audio
  scheduling tests deterministic; real-time drift tests (TT, 10 min) are `slow` and use the real
  context with the autoplay flag of 3.4.2.
- `structuredClone` exists in all target browsers; the fake IndexedDB falls back to a JSON round
  trip for plain data where it does not (tests that store Blobs then skip with a reason).
- The runner never calls `alert`, `confirm` or `prompt` (the tool records dialogs as failures).

## 7. User interface and navigation

This part fixes everything the player sees and touches: the visual rules, the three
complexity levels, where each setting appears, the navigation model, the responsive
layouts, every screen (`SCR-*`) and dialog (`DLG-*`) with element ids, layouts, states and
exact texts, the HUD, onboarding and the tutorial, the accessibility implementation, and
the text catalog. Module APIs named here belong to Part 4 and Part 6; screen controller
logic is M-27 (Part 6.27), widgets and the screen stack are M-26 (Part 6.26). Design tokens
are Part 3.2.2 and are referenced, never redefined.

Conventions used in this part:

- Element ids. A screen root is `#scr-<slug>` where `<slug>` is the screen name after
  `SCR-` in lower case (`#scr-mainmenu`); a dialog root is `#dlg-<slug>`. Child elements use
  a fixed per-screen prefix: `fl` FirstLaunch, `mm` MainMenu, `qp` QuickPlay, `ins`
  Instrument, `fp` FreePlay, `st` Studio, `lib` Library, `imp` ImportInspect, `dn` Dance,
  `mp` Multiplayer, `ch` Characters, `set` Settings, `hlp` Help, `ab` About, `dg`
  Diagnostics, `tut` Tutorial, `res` Results, `ps` Pause, `hud` HUD, `pad` touch pads.
  Ids are unique in the document at any time (a screen's DOM exists only while mounted).
- Texts in double quotes are exact user-facing strings. A text with a code (`E-...` error,
  `S-...` status) is reproduced in the catalog of 7.11, which governs when the two differ.
  Placeholders are `{name}`. Labels of buttons and fields are given in the element tables
  and are exact as well.
- "Back" means the screen's back action. It is triggered by the on-screen Back button
  (`g-back` icon, label "Back"), `Escape` (outside gameplay), gamepad button 1 in menus,
  and the browser back button (7.4). Each screen states what Back does.
- Keyboard maps list keys by `KeyboardEvent.code`. Gameplay keys are the M-07 maps (Part 6.7,
  remappable); every other key in this part is a fixed UI key handled by M-26 or M-27.
- Sizes are CSS px at `--ui = 1` unless given as tokens; tokens scale with `--ui` (3.2.2).

### 7.1 Visual identity

#### 7.1.1 Direction

Finger Lickin Music looks like a small club stage seen from the mixing desk: a near-black
room (`--c-bg`), graphite panels (`--c-panel`, `--c-panel-2`) and one warm spotlight amber
(`--c-accent`) that marks the single thing to do next. Color is information, not
decoration: amber means "primary action or selected", cyan (`--c-accent-2`) means
"informational", green, yellow and red mean status, and the four lane colors appear only
where a lane or dance direction is meant, always together with its glyph (circle, triangle,
square, diamond; arrows for dance). The 3D stage carries the energy (lights pulse on
`sched.beat`, performers move on `sched.noteOn`); the interface around it stays flat,
quiet and legible so the music and the note highway dominate (P 2.1). The logo is the game
name set in `--fs-6` `--fw-bold` with the four lane glyphs in a row beneath it at `--fs-4`;
it appears on SCR-FirstLaunch, SCR-MainMenu and SCR-About only.

#### 7.1.2 Tokens and component rules

All colors, sizes, radii, shadows, durations and z-layers come from the Part 3.2.2 token
block; the semantic usage table of Part 3.2.2 is binding. The component classes below are
written into the `S02 widgets` block of `shell.html` by Phase 1 and built by `FLM.UI.Widgets`
(M-26). Every interactive component has the six visual states of P 2.3.

Spacing and alignment rules: panels pad `--sp-4` (`--sp-3` on `body.compact`); stacked
controls are separated by `--sp-3`; groups by `--sp-5`; touch targets keep at least `--sp-2`
(8 px) between hit areas; every row of controls aligns on a 4 px grid; labels sit above
their control on `body.compact` and to the left (fixed 11rem column) otherwise. No element
uses margins to create visual borders; dividers are `--border` lines.

Track color palette (the "palette" of Part 5.1.2; tracks only, never lanes or status): index
0-7 = `#7aa2f7`, `#9ece6a`, `#e0af68`, `#f7768e`, `#bb9af7`, `#2ac3de`, `#ff9e64`,
`#c0caf5`. A track's color always appears next to its name text, never alone.

#### 7.1.3 Iconography

Every icon is a `<symbol>` in the `#glyphs` sprite of `shell.html` (Part 3.2.5), viewBox
`0 0 24 24`, used as `<svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#g-..."/></svg>` inside
a labeled control (the control carries the accessible name; icons are never the only label
for a control without `aria-label`). Two drawing classes keep the visual weight consistent
(P 21): line icons use `class="icon"` with `fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width:
2; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round`; solid icons use `class="icon solid"`
with `fill: currentColor; stroke: none`. The lane glyphs and arrows of Part 3.2.5 use
`class="glyph"` (solid, with the high-contrast outline). Sub-elements marked `dot` inside a
line icon are filled (`.icon .dot { fill: currentColor; stroke: none }`).

| `g-fam-ethnic` | Ethnic | `<circle cx="7" cy="17" r="4"/>` plus `M10 14 L19 5` and `<circle cx="19.5" cy="4.5" r="2"/>` |
| `g-fam-percussive` | Percussive | `M4 8 A8 3 0 0 0 20 8 A8 3 0 0 0 4 8 V16 A8 3 0 0 0 20 16 V8` |
| `g-fam-soundfx` | Sound Effects | `M4 9 H8 L13 5 V19 L8 15 H4 Z M16 8.5 A5 5 0 0 1 16 15.5 M18.5 6 A8.5 8.5 0 0 1 18.5 18` |
| `g-fam-drums` | Drum kit (channel 10) | `M6 13 A6 2.5 0 0 0 18 13 A6 2.5 0 0 0 6 13 V18 A6 2.5 0 0 0 18 18 V13 M3 5 L10 7 M14 7 L21 5` |

The symbols are written in source order of the two tables after the Part 3.2.5 glyphs. The
WebGL highway does not use the sprite (Part 3.2.5 atlas rule).

#### 7.1.4 Typography use

| Element | Size token | Weight | Other |
|---|---|---|---|
| Game title (logo) | `--fs-6` | `--fw-bold` | `--lh-tight` |
| Screen title (`h1` of each screen) | `--fs-5` | `--fw-bold` | one per screen, `--lh-tight` |
| Section title inside a screen (`h2`) | `--fs-4` | `--fw-bold` | |
| Body text, buttons, inputs, list titles | `--fs-3` | `--fw-medium` for buttons and list titles, `--fw-regular` for body | `--lh-body` |
| Labels, list secondary lines, units, table cells | `--fs-2` | `--fw-regular` | `--c-text-muted` (never the only carrier of required information) |
| Captions, diagnostics values, build footer | `--fs-1` | `--fw-regular` | diagnostics in `--font-mono` |
| Codes (invite codes, error codes, file hashes) | `--fs-2` | `--fw-regular` | `.code` (`--font-mono`), selectable |
| HUD score, combo number | `--fs-5` (score), `--fs-6` (combo) | `--fw-bold` | `.num` tabular numerals |
| HUD judgment word | `--fs-6` (`--fs-6` x 1.25 via `transform: scale` when `accessibility.largeJudgmentText`) | `--fw-bold` | `--j-*` color |
| HUD labels (accuracy, section) | `--fs-4` | `--fw-medium` | `.num` for numbers |

Capitalization: sentence case everywhere ("Song library", "Import music"), except the
fixed proper names of modes and menu entries of B 6.2 as listed in 7.6.2 ("Quick Play",
"Instrument Mode", "Free Play", "Studio", "Song Library", "Import Music", "Dance Mode",
"Multiplayer", "Characters", "Settings", "Help and Controls", "About"), the judgment words
"Perfect", "Great", "Good", "Miss", the compatibility words and the tier names. The same
thing is always called by the same word (P 1, P 2.2): "track" (never "channel" in UI
text), "song" for built-in and imported arrangements, "project" for saved Studio work,
"take" for a recording, "chart" for a playable part, "difficulty", "profile" (mapping
profile), "section", "loop", "count-in".

#### 7.1.5 Motion rules

| Motion | Duration and easing | Reduced motion |
|---|---|---|
| Screen push and pop | content fades from 0 to 1 opacity and moves 12 px horizontally (push from the right, pop from the left), `--t-slow`, `--ease` | opacity only, 0 ms (instant) |
| Dialog open and close | backdrop fade, dialog scale 0.98 -> 1, `--t-base` | instant |
| Sheet expand and collapse | height transition `--t-base` | instant |
| Button press | scale 0.97, `--t-fast` | instant (state still visible through color) |
| Toast in and out | fade plus 8 px rise, `--t-base` | fade only, instant |
| HUD judgment word | appears at full opacity, scale 1.15 -> 1 over `--t-fast`, fades out after 450 ms over `--t-base` | no scale, same visibility time, fade instant |
| Combo number on change | no animation (number changes in place) | same |
| Pad pressed state | instant color change (class `pressed`), no transition | same |
| Beat indicator (HUD) | 80 ms flash on `sched.beat` | kept (gameplay information) |
| Camera moves, particles, panel slides | JS-driven per Part 6.20 and 6.21 | disabled (Part 3.2.2 motion rule) |
| Loading spinner | ring rotation 1 turn per 900 ms, shown after 300 ms | static ring with the text label only |

No CSS animation runs while nothing changes: infinite animations exist only for the
spinner and the indeterminate progress bar, and both are removed from the DOM when hidden.
Screen transitions never delay input: the incoming screen is interactive at frame 0.

#### 7.1.6 Hierarchy rules

1. Each screen has exactly one `.btn.primary` (or one primary card) visible at a time; it is
   the next step of the current task ("Play", "Start", "Record", "Import", "Save").
2. Secondary actions are `.btn`; destructive actions are `.btn.danger` and always lead to a
   confirmation dialog that states the consequence (7.7).
3. The screen title (`h1`) names the current task; the current song or project name is
   shown under it in `--fs-2` (B 6.3 "current mode" and "current song or project").
4. Status (save state, connection, storage notices, audio state) is shown with an icon,
   a status word and a semantic color, in a fixed place per screen (top bar right).
5. Advanced controls live behind a disclosure ("More options", "Advanced") or in the
   Settings category "Advanced" and are never on the first visible screenful of
   SCR-QuickPlay (I 11.1).
6. Informational labels are never styled like buttons: no border, no hover change, no
   pointer cursor.

#### 7.1.7 Forbidden

- Gradients of any kind on UI surfaces, text or the HUD (`linear-gradient`,
  `radial-gradient` are not used in `S02` to `S05`; the blob-shadow texture of the 3D stage
  is a renderer texture, not UI).
- Glow: no colored `box-shadow` with blur, no `text-shadow` other than the HUD readability
  shadow `0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.8)` on `#hud` text, no `filter: drop-shadow` or `blur`,
  no `backdrop-filter`.
- Decorative borders, double borders, ornaments, background images and patterns.
- More than one accent-colored element competing on one screen (rule 7.1.6.1).
- Color as the only carrier of meaning (7.10); emoji or non-ASCII symbols in UI text.
- Animations that run continuously without a musical event or a loading state (7.1.5).
- Fake progress: percentages that are not measured (B 20.4, P 21).

### 7.2 Complexity levels (I 11.1)

The three levels are structural, not a global switch: each level is a set of places, and a
player moves to the next level by opening it. Nothing is hidden permanently; nothing
advanced is on the first screenful of the Quick Start path.

| Level | Where it lives | What it exposes | What it never shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quick Start | SCR-MainMenu entry "Quick Play"; SCR-QuickPlay in `level:'quick'`; SCR-Dance select state; SCR-FirstLaunch "Play a demo song" | Song list, part list (instrument tracks and "Dance"), difficulty, the Play button; master volume in the top bar | Profiles, chart preview, judgment presets, practice tools, calibration values, any number field |
| Customize | SCR-QuickPlay "More options" disclosure (open by default when entered from "Instrument Mode", `level:'customize'`); SCR-Pause practice panel; SCR-Settings categories Audio, Controls, Gameplay, Video, Accessibility, Calibration; SCR-Characters; SCR-FreePlay settings panel | Mapping profile, control layout, backing tracks, target track level, visualization on or off, speed and loop practice, count-in, chart preview per difficulty, audio and input settings, camera, appearance | Track editing, chart generation parameters, raw diagnostics |
| Advanced | SCR-Studio; SCR-ImportInspect "Tracks" and "Chart" tabs; SCR-Settings category "Advanced"; SCR-Diagnostics (reached from Settings > Advanced or `?diag`) | Multitrack editing, piano roll, quantize, mixer, markers, per-track chart generation with profile and difficulty preview, polyphony cap, chord window, stats overlay, log level, diagnostics export, self-test (test build) | n/a |

Rules: (1) the Quick Start path from the main menu to sound is at most two activations after
the audio unlock (Quick Play, Play: the default selection of Part 1.7 is preselected);
(2) the "More options" disclosure remembers its open state per session only (not persisted);
(3) every Customize control that changes scoring comparability carries the badge "Not
comparable" next to its value when set off-default (7.10.1).

has consistent behavior wherever it appears"). Keys are Part 5.11.

SCR-Settings has nine categories in this order: Audio, Controls, Gameplay, Video,

### 7.4 Navigation model

#### 7.4.1 Screens, modes and the stack

The screen stack (`FLM.UI.Screens`, M-26) holds mounted screens in `#overlay`; the root is
always SCR-MainMenu (depth 1). Each mode of Part 4.7 pushes its root screen above the menu
on enter; SCR-Pause and SCR-ImportInspect sub-states are screens pushed above their mode
screen; dialogs are not stack entries (they live in a dialog layer inside `#overlay` and
are counted by `UI.dialogCount()`). Only the top screen receives input; covered screens keep
their DOM (hidden with `hidden`) so their filters, selection and scroll are preserved.

| Operation | Effect on the stack | Effect on history | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `push(id, params)` | mounts and shows `id` above the top; the previous top gets `hidden` and records its focused element | `history.pushState({flm:1, seq:depth-1, screen:id}, '')` | mode enter, opening a sub-screen (SCR-Pause, SCR-ImportInspect from Library) |
| `replace(id, params)` | unmounts the top, mounts `id` at the same depth | `history.replaceState` with the same `seq` | a mode swapping its own root screen: SCR-Multiplayer lobby -> the multiplayer play layout at the countdown and back to the lobby after the song (Part 4.7.2 step 12) |
| `pop()` | runs the top screen's back guard (7.4.3); on pass unmounts it, shows the one below and restores its focus | internal pops call `history.back()` once with the suppress counter incremented (7.4.2) | Back button, `Escape`, gamepad B |
| `popTo(id)` | pops without guards down to `id` (guards already ran in the leave sequence) | `history.go(-(n))` for the n entries removed, suppressed | `Modes.leave` (Part 4.7.2 step 10) |
| `back()` | `pop()` unless the top screen overrides back (gameplay screens open SCR-Pause instead, SCR-Pause resumes) | as `pop` or a `pushState` for SCR-Pause | the global back entry point, also the `popstate` handler |

Mode changes always go through `FLM.Modes.enter` and `leave` (Part 4.7); a screen never
pushes another mode's root screen directly. Leaving a mode ends at SCR-MainMenu and the
next mode's root is pushed fresh, so the stack never holds two mode screens.

#### 7.4.2 Browser back and forward

1. At boot (M-28 `init`, Part 4.3 B10) the current history entry is replaced with
   `{flm:1, seq:-1, sentinel:true}` and one entry `{flm:1, seq:0, screen:'SCR-MainMenu'}`
   is pushed, so the first browser back at the menu stays inside the page.
2. Every `push` adds one entry with `seq = depth - 1`; `replace` replaces the top entry.
3. `popstate` handler: if the suppress counter is > 0, decrement it and return. Otherwise
   `target = event.state && event.state.flm ? event.state.seq : -1` and `top = depth - 1`:
   - `target < top`: call `UI.Screens.back()` once. If the back is refused (guard
     cancelled, or the top screen handled it as pause or resume), re-push the entry for the
     current top so the browser history matches the stack again. A jump of several entries
     at once (long-press history menu) is processed as one `back()`; the remaining entries
     are re-synchronized by pushing the stack's entries above the new top.
   - `target > top` (browser forward into an entry whose screen was already unmounted):
     forward is not replayable; call `history.go(top - target)` with the suppress counter
     incremented, which returns the browser to the current entry. Nothing else happens.
   - `target === top`: nothing.
   - `target === -1` (sentinel reached at SCR-MainMenu): push `{seq:0}` again and show toast
     S-GEN-01 "Press back again to leave Finger Lickin Music."; a second sentinel hit within
     2 s does not re-push, so the browser leaves the page (with the unload guard of 7.4.3
     when a project is dirty).
4. Gameplay screens (SCR-Instrument, SCR-Dance, SCR-Tutorial play steps, multiplayer play):
   browser back pauses (pushes SCR-Pause) instead of leaving; on SCR-Pause browser back
   resumes (same as `Escape`). Quitting gameplay is an explicit "Quit" button.
5. Fallback (Part 1.6): when `history.pushState` throws (some `file://` contexts), M-28
   switches to hash navigation for the session: each push sets `location.hash =
   '#/' + seq + '/' + screen` and a `hashchange` listener applies rule 3 with `seq` parsed
   from the hash. The internal stack works identically either way.

#### 7.4.3 Unsaved-changes guard points

`FLM.UI.confirmUnsaved(info)` shows DLG-UnsavedChanges with `FLM.Project.guard.describe()`
text and resolves to `'save'`, `'discard'` or `'cancel'`. The guard runs at these points and
nowhere else:

| Guard point | Condition | Choices and outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Back from SCR-Studio (any trigger) | `Project.isDirty()` | Save (saves, then leaves when `project.saved` arrives; on `project.saveFailed` the leave is cancelled and DLG-SaveFailed shows), Discard (leaves; the checkpoint ring keeps the last autosave), Cancel (stays) |
| Back from SCR-FreePlay | the transient Free Play project holds a take not yet saved or opened in Studio | Save opens the project name field then saves; Discard drops the transient project; Cancel stays |
| SCR-Library "Open" of another project, "New project" in Studio | current project dirty | as Studio |
| SCR-ImportInspect "Play now" or "Open in Studio" | a project is open and dirty (both actions make the imported song the current project) | DLG-ImportReplace (7.7), not DLG-UnsavedChanges; "Save to Library" only adds a catalog entry and never asks |
| SCR-Settings "Data and backup" > "Import settings" | always | DLG-ImportSettings (7.7) |
| Page unload (`beforeunload`) | `Project.isDirty()` and not recording | the listener sets `event.returnValue = ''` (browser's own prompt; custom text is not shown by browsers); `pagehide` also triggers the synchronous autosave of Part 4.7.4 |
| Mode leave caused by an error (`returnToMenu`) | any | no dialog: the leave autosaves (Part 4.7.2 step 13) and the project stays in memory |

Characters (SCR-Characters) never asks: changes are applied as they are made (Part 1.2).
Recording in progress is never interrupted by a guard dialog: Back while recording first
stops the take (S-STU-04 "Recording stopped. The take was kept.") and then applies the
guard.

#### 7.4.4 Focus restoration

1. On `push`, the covered screen stores the id of its focused element (or its scroll
   container plus row index for lists). On `pop`, that element regains focus; if it no
   longer exists, the screen's initial focus target is used.
2. Each screen names its initial focus target in 7.6 ("Initial focus"); a screen that names
   none focuses its first focusable control after the Back button. The target is focused
   when the push transition starts (same frame), with `preventScroll: true`.
3. Dialogs: `UI.Focus.trap(dialog)` on open (Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside; focus starts
   on the dialog's default button, which is never a destructive one); on close focus returns
   to the invoking element via `UI.Focus.restore()`, or to the screen's initial focus
   target when the invoker was removed.
4. Gameplay: when play starts, `document.activeElement.blur()` runs (no text field keeps
   focus, B 6.4) and focus moves to the gameplay surface `#view` (`tabindex="-1"`), so
   `Escape` and the lane keys reach M-07.
5. The focus ring is the Part 3.2.4 `:focus-visible` ring; `.focus-ring` is added by M-26
   to the focused element after keyboard or gamepad navigation so the ring is also visible
   on browsers where programmatic focus does not trigger `:focus-visible`.

#### 7.4.5 Listener discipline

Screens attach every DOM listener through `FLM.Core.dom.on(el, type, fn, opts, owner)` with
the screen's owner token, and every bus subscription with the same token; `unmount` calls
`Core.dom.offOwner(owner)` and `bus.removeOwner(owner)` and removes the screen's DOM. M-26
installs exactly one document-level `keydown` listener (UI navigation) and one
`pointerdown` capture listener (audio unlock, Part 4.3 B15) at `UI.init`; screens register
key handlers with M-26 instead of adding their own document listeners. Repeated navigation
therefore cannot accumulate listeners; `Modes.assertClean()` (Part 4.7.3) checks the
counts after every leave (P 3 "repeated navigation does not duplicate event listeners").

Screen-level single-key shortcuts (for example `Space` play and stop in SCR-Studio) are
ignored when the key code is bound to a live control in the current `FLM.Input` context
(checked by M-27 through `FLM.Input.getMap()` and `FLM.Input.context()`), so a remapped
gameplay key never triggers a UI action as well.

Gamepad in menus: while a gamepad is connected (`input.device`) and the mode is not a
gameplay mode, M-27 polls `navigator.getGamepads()` every 50 ms with a `Core.timers`
interval owned by `'ui-gamepad'` and translates edges to UI navigation: d-pad (buttons
12-15) moves focus like the arrow keys, button 0 activates, button 1 is Back, button 9
(start) activates the screen's primary button. The interval stops on disconnect and when a
gameplay mode is entered (M-07 owns the pad there).

### 7.5 Responsive rules

#### 7.5.1 Layout families

The layout family is computed by M-26 from the viewport and published in `ui.layout`. The
classes are those of Part 3.2.3 plus one media query.

| Family | Condition | Class and query | Layout pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phone portrait | `min(innerWidth, innerHeight) < 600` and portrait | `body.compact.portrait` | one column; full-screen gameplay; settings and editors in sheets or tabs; pads along the bottom |
| Phone landscape | `min(...) < 600` and landscape | `body.compact.landscape` | two columns where useful (list plus detail); gameplay with pads at the bottom or right |
| Tablet | `min(...) >= 600` and `innerWidth < 1024` | neither `compact` nor the wide query | two columns; panels as side drawers |
| Desktop | `innerWidth >= 1024` and `min(...) >= 600` | `@media (min-width: 1024px)` with `body:not(.compact)` | multi-panel: navigation column, stage or editor center, inspector right (B 6.4) |

Viewports the layouts are checked at (Part 2.13 LT list): 360 x 640, 390 x 844, 844 x 390,
768 x 1024, 1024 x 768, 1366 x 768, 1920 x 1080. At every one of them and at `--ui` 0.8 to
1.5: no horizontal page scroll (`html, body { overflow: hidden }` plus scroll containers that
scroll vertically only), no clipped text, no overlapping controls (P 2.2). Scroll containers
set `overflow-y: auto; touch-action: pan-y; overscroll-behavior: contain` because `body` has
`touch-action: none` (Part 3.2.4).

#### 7.5.2 Touch targets

- On `body.touch` every interactive control is at least `var(--touch-min)` (56 px) on both
  sides with at least `--sp-2` (8 px) between hit areas (brief section 6). The visible shape
  may be smaller (a 24 px toggle thumb) when the hit area is padded to 56 px.
- On pointer-only layouts menu controls are at least 44 x 44 px (Part 2.13 decision 6).
- Gameplay pads: minimum height from `input.padSize` (small 56, medium 72, large 88 px),
  width as computed below, never below 56 px.
- Nothing essential depends on hover (B 21.1): every `.hover-only` element (tooltips) has a
  tap or focus equivalent.

#### 7.5.3 Pad placement

Pads are four `div.pad` children of `#touch` with ids `pad-0` to `pad-3` (lanes 0-3, or
dance directions 0-3 in SCR-Dance). `UI.TouchPads.layout(mode)` computes rectangles from
the viewport, the safe areas and the settings, then calls `FLM.Input` to refresh its cached
rects (`Input.layoutChanged()`, Part 6.7.4 D.2) through M-27.

| Orientation and `input.padLayout` | Area | Arrangement | Highway area |
|---|---|---|---|
| Portrait (any setting) | bottom 28 % of the viewport height, but at least the pad minimum height + 16 px, inside the safe areas | one row of four equal pads, 8 px gaps, 8 px side margins; lane 0 at the left | the full width above the pad area; hit line 12 px above the pads' top edge |
| Landscape, `bottom` | bottom 24 % of the height (same minimum) | one row of four pads split into two pairs: lanes 0-1 in the left 40 % of the width, lanes 2-3 in the right 40 %, 20 % center gap | centered column, 40 % of the width, above the pad row; hit line 12 px above the pads |
| Landscape, `right` | right 24 % of the width, full height minus the top bar | 2 x 2 grid: top row lanes 0 and 1, bottom row lanes 2 and 3, 8 px gaps | left 76 % of the width, highway centered there; hit line at 80 % of the height |
| Dance, any orientation | as the instrument row above, with `layout:'pads'` rendering a 2 x 2 diamond (up top, left and right middle, down bottom) inside the same area when `session.dance.layout === 'pads'` | arrows layout: one row left, down, up, right | as instrument |

Each pad shows its glyph (`g-lane0`..`g-lane3`, or the arrow) at 40 % of the pad height,
centered, plus a small label: the current note name or chord name in Free Play (from
`Mapping.profileTable`), nothing in chart play. Background `--lane-N` at the opacity of
`input.padOpacity`, border 2 px `--lane-N`; class `pressed` (set by M-26 on `input.event`
press, removed on release) raises opacity to 1 and inverts the glyph color to `--c-bg`. The
highway and HUD never place anything under the pads; the pads never cover the hit line.

Pads are shown when `Caps.maxTouchPoints > 0` (body class `touch`) or when
`onboarding.inputMode === 'touch'`, and hidden in the keyboard layout chosen at first launch
(`desktop`); SCR-Pause offers "Show touch pads" either way.

#### 7.5.4 Rotate recommendation

Modes that recommend landscape on phones: `instrument` and `quickplay` play (four lanes plus
stage), `multiplayer` play, `studio` (piano roll width). `dance`, `freeplay` and every panel
mode are designed for portrait and never recommend rotation. Rule: when one of the
recommending modes is entered and `body.compact.portrait` holds, `#rotate` is shown with its
Part 3.2.5 text ("Landscape recommended" / "This mode works best with the device sideways.
You can keep playing in portrait." / button "Continue in portrait"). It is shown before play
starts (gameplay waits with the count-in until the panel is dismissed or the device is
rotated), at most once per mode per session, and never during active play. Rotating to
landscape hides it automatically. Nothing is ever blocked: every mode is fully usable in
portrait (B 6.4).

#### 7.5.5 Safe areas, UI scale and text entry

- Safe areas: `#overlay`, `#hud` and `#rotate` pad with the `--safe-*` tokens (Part
  3.2.4); pads are placed inside `env(safe-area-inset-*)`; the top bar of every screen has
  `padding-top: var(--safe-top)` included in its 56 px height on notched devices.
- UI scale: `video.uiScale` sets `--ui` (0.8-1.5, step 0.05) through `UI.Layout.setScale`;
  all rem-based tokens follow. At 1.3 and above on `body.compact`, multi-column grids
  (menu landscape grid, Library two-pane, Characters options grid) collapse to one column
  and the HUD hides the section name line (kept in the progress bar tooltip and the
  screen-reader live region).
- Text entry is limited to: project name, track name, marker label, character name, preset
  name, player display name, invite and answer codes (paste), relay URL (Online edition),
  library search. None is required to start any mode; every name has a default. Text
  fields use `maxlength` from the data limits (track 80, project 80, marker 80, character
  24, display name 24, search 60), `autocomplete="off"`, `autocapitalize="sentences"`
  (names) or `"off"` (codes), `spellcheck="false"`, `enterkeyhint="done"`. During gameplay
  no text field exists in the DOM (B 6.4); Studio text fields commit on Enter or blur and
  are blurred when recording starts.
- Long names: a single-line CSS ellipsis (`white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis`) everywhere in lists, track headers and top bars, with the full
  text in `title` and in the accessible name. Text drawn into the canvas or the HUD uses
  `UI.truncate(text, maxChars)`, which cuts at `maxChars - 3` and appends "..." (ASCII):
  HUD song title 32, performer label 16, lobby name 24, results song title 48. Names never
  wrap into a second line inside fixed-height rows (P 21).

### 7.6 Screens

#### 7.6.0 Shared screen frame (B 6.3)

Every screen except SCR-FirstLaunch and the gameplay screens has the same frame:

| Element id (per screen prefix `xx`) | Type | Content | Accessible name |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xx-top` | `header.topbar`, height 56 px plus `--safe-top` | left to right: Back, title block, status block, volume button | landmark `banner` |
| `xx-back` | icon button `g-back` with visible label "Back" on non-compact layouts | Back action of the screen | "Back to {previous screen name}" |
| `xx-title` | `h1` plus `p.subtitle` | screen name; subtitle = current song or project name ("No project open" when none) | heading |
| `xx-status` | `div` with up to four status chips | audio chip (`g-mute` plus "Sound off" when not unlocked or suspended; hidden when running), save chip in Studio ("Saved" `--c-ok`, "Unsaved changes" `--c-warn`, "Saving..." neutral, "Not saved" `--c-error`), connection chip in Multiplayer ("Connected" / "Reconnecting" / "Offline"), input chip (icons of the active sources: keyboard, touch, gamepad, MIDI; a source appears after its first event or connect) | `role="status"`, each chip has text |
| `xx-volume` | icon button `g-volume` (`g-mute` when the value is 0 %) opening a popover with the master volume slider (`audio.masterVolume`) | | "Master volume, {n} percent" |

Gameplay screens replace the frame with the HUD (7.8) and a pause button. Error
notifications are toasts in `#toast` (7.11.4) on every screen; dialogs are centered in
`#overlay`. The stats overlay (`video.showStats`) is a fixed 4-line box top-right inside
`#hud` (FPS, p95 frame ms, active voices / cap, sync offset when connected) in `--fs-1`
`--font-mono`.

#### 7.6.1 SCR-FirstLaunch

Purpose: the seven steps of B 6.1 for a first visit (`onboarding.firstLaunchDone === false`):
identity, capability check, audio activation by gesture, rendering capability, input
configuration, mode choice, explanation of unavailable features. Returning users never see
it (P 4).

Entry: Boot step B14 (Part 4.3). Re-entry: SCR-Settings > Data and backup > "Show first-launch
setup again" (sets the flag false and enters `menu` with this screen).

Elements (three panels in one screen; only one panel is visible at a time; a step dots
indicator `fl-steps` shows 1 of 3, 2 of 3, 3 of 3 as text plus dots):

| Id | Type | Label or content | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fl-logo` | logo block | "Finger Lickin Music" plus the four lane glyphs | step 1, identity |
| `fl-tagline` | `p` | "Play, record and perform music with four buttons." | |
| `fl-checks` | list of 4 rows | "Storage", "Settings", "Sound engine", "Graphics"; each row shows a state word: "Checking", "Ready", "Limited" (with a one-line reason below), never a percentage | driven by `boot.stage` for B5-B8 (Part 4.3 last paragraph) |
| `fl-start` | primary button | "Start" | the audio unlock gesture (`Audio.unlock()` inside the click handler); disabled with text "Checking..." until B8 completed |
| `fl-start-hint` | `p` | "Starting turns on sound. Nothing plays until you choose a mode." | |
| `fl-skip` | text button | "Skip setup" | sets `onboarding.firstLaunchDone = true`, `onboarding.inputMode = 'auto'`, unlocks audio (it is a gesture), enters SCR-MainMenu |
| `fl-input` | segmented, 3 options | "Keyboard", "Touch", "Gamepad" (gamepad disabled with reason "Press a button on the controller first" until `input.device` reports a gamepad) | step 2; preselected: Touch when `Caps.maxTouchPoints > 0` and no keyboard event has occurred, else Keyboard; writes `onboarding.inputMode` (`desktop` for Keyboard and Gamepad, `touch`) |
| `fl-input-preview` | `div` | Keyboard: the four lane keys drawn as key caps "A S K L" with their glyphs; Touch: four live pads (the real `#touch` pads in the portrait layout) with the text "Place up to four fingers on the pads"; Gamepad: "Buttons A, B, X, Y play the four lanes." | pressing keys or pads lights the matching glyph (uses `input.event` with Input in context `instrument`; no sound) |
| `fl-touch-result` | `p` | after a touch probe: "Your device registered {n} simultaneous touches." and, when n < 4, "Chords on more than {n} pads at once may not register on this device." | the probe of Part 2.19 OQ-1: the maximum count of concurrently pressed pads during this step; stored for Diagnostics |
| `fl-next` | primary button | "Continue" | step 2 -> 3 |
| `fl-choices` | three cards | "Learn the basics" (subtitle "Interactive tutorial, about 3 minutes", recommended badge), "Play a demo song" (subtitle "Neon Boulevard, keys part, beginner"), "Go to the main menu" | step 3; each card sets `onboarding.firstLaunchDone = true` before acting |
| `fl-unavailable` | `div.notice.info` list | header "Not available in this browser" plus one line per entry of `Caps.degraded` with the Part 4.3 gate reason text; hidden when the list is empty | step 3, B 6.1 step 7 |
| `fl-tier` | `p` | "Graphics: {tier}" with the tier name and, for Abstract, "3D stage unavailable in this browser; using the flat visualizer." | step 3, B 6.1 step 4 |

Layouts:

```text
Desktop (centered column 32rem)          Phone portrait                 Phone landscape
+--------------------------------+      +--------------------+      +---------------------------------+
|        FINGER LICKIN MUSIC      |      | FINGER LICKIN MUSIC|      | LOGO       | Storage    Ready   |
|          o  ^  []  <>           |      |   o  ^  []  <>     |      | tagline    | Settings   Ready   |
|  Play, record and perform ...   |      | tagline            |      |            | Sound      Ready   |
|  Storage ........... Ready      |      | Storage     Ready  |      |            | Graphics   Ready   |
|  Settings .......... Ready      |      | Settings    Ready  |      |            | [ Start ]          |
|  Sound engine ...... Ready      |      | Sound       Ready  |      |            | Skip setup         |
|  Graphics .......... Limited    |      | Graphics    Ready  |      +---------------------------------+
|     WebGL2 unavailable ...      |      |                    |
|          [  Start  ]            |      | [      Start     ] |
|          Skip setup             |      | Skip setup         |
+--------------------------------+      +--------------------+
```

Step 2 and step 3 use the same column; in phone landscape the three choice cards sit in one
row, in portrait they stack.

States:

| State | Trigger | What shows |
|---|---|---|
| Loading | boot stages B5-B8 running | `fl-checks` rows "Checking"; `fl-start` disabled "Checking..." |
| Ready | `boot.ready` | rows "Ready" or "Limited" with reason; `fl-start` enabled "Start" |
| Audio blocked | `Audio.unlock()` resolved `ok:false` | DLG-AudioBlocked (7.7) over the screen; on success the screen advances to step 2 |
| Error | a hard capability failure | never reached: Boot shows `#fatal` instead (Part 4.3 B4) |
| Disabled | n/a | "Gamepad" option disabled with its reason until a pad is seen |
| Empty | `Caps.degraded` empty | `fl-unavailable` hidden |

Keyboard: `Enter` activates the focused button (initial focus `fl-start`, then `fl-input`,
then the first card); arrows move inside the segmented control and between cards; `Escape`
does nothing (there is nothing behind this screen). Touch: tap. Gamepad: per 7.4.5.
Exit paths: "Learn the basics" -> `tutorial`; "Play a demo song" -> `quickplay` play with
the Part 1.7 default selection (`origin:'menu'`); "Go to the main menu" and "Skip setup" ->
SCR-MainMenu. Accessibility: `fl-checks` is `role="list"` with each state word in the row
text; `aria-live="polite"` on the list announces "Ready"; the steps indicator text is
"Step 1 of 3".

#### 7.6.2 SCR-MainMenu

Purpose: the root (B 6.2, P 3): reach every mode, see what is unavailable and why, continue
recent work, see the daily challenge, recover an unsaved project after a crash.

Entry: Boot B14 for returning users; every mode leave ends here.

Elements:

| Id | Type | Label | Disabled reason (exact) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mm-title` | logo block (small) | "Finger Lickin Music" | |
| `mm-continue` | card, shown only when `flm.v1.lastSession` exists and its target still exists | "Continue: {project or song name}" with subtitle "{mode name}, {relative time}" ("Studio, 2 hours ago") | |
| `mm-recover` | `div.notice.warn` with buttons "Recover" and "Discard", shown when `flm.v1.recovery` exists | S-STO-01 "An unsaved project ({name}) was kept after the last session ended unexpectedly. Recover it?" | |
| `mm-audio-banner` | `div.notice.info`, shown until `audio.unlocked` | S-AUD-01 "Tap or press a key to enable sound." | |
| `mm-storage-notice` | `div.notice.warn` for the Part 6.16 notices D1-D4 (dismissible; returns after reload) | text from `Storage.state().notice` | |
| `mm-list` | `nav` with 12 entry buttons in this order | "Quick Play", "Instrument Mode", "Free Play", "Studio", "Song Library", "Import Music", "Dance Mode", "Multiplayer", "Characters", "Settings", "Help and Controls", "About" | see the next table |
| `mm-entry-<n>` | `.btn` with icon, label and a subtitle line | subtitles: "Pick a song and play", "Choose part, profile and practice options", "Play freely in any key", "Record and arrange tracks", "Built-in songs, imports and projects", "MIDI, MusicXML, Guitar Pro, audio", "Step to the beat", "Play with 2 to 4 people", "Customize your band", "Sound, controls, display", "Controls and how each mode works", "Version, limits and licenses" | |
| `mm-daily` | card | "Daily challenge" plus `{song title}`, `{instrument or Dance}`, `{difficulty}`, goal text ("Reach 90.0 % accuracy", "Reach a 40 combo", "Score 75 % of the maximum") and state "Completed today" with `g-check` when done | |
| `mm-project` | `p` in the footer | "Open project: {name}" or nothing | |
| `mm-version` | `p` footer | "Version {VERSION} ({edition}) - {build date}" | |
| `mm-stage` | the idle band on `canvas#view` behind the menu (desktop and tablet: right 60 % of the screen; phone: hidden behind an opaque menu background to save power) | | `aria-hidden` (decorative) |

Disabled entries (B 6.2, P 3 "unavailable online features explain their requirements"):

| Entry | Disabled when | Reason line |
|---|---|---|
| Quick Play, Instrument Mode, Dance Mode | `Project.Catalog.list()` is empty and no imported song exists | S-GEN-02 "No built-in songs were loaded. Import a song to play." |
| Multiplayer | `RTCPeerConnection` missing and no relay URL is configured | E-CAP-005 "Multiplayer needs WebRTC, which this browser does not provide." |
| every other entry | never | n/a |

While audio is locked, entries stay enabled; choosing a mode that needs audio opens
DLG-AudioBlocked first (Part 4.7).

```text

+-----------------------------------------------+    +------------------+    +----------------------------------+
| FINGER LICKIN MUSIC             [Sound off]   |    | FINGER LICKIN    |    | FLM  [Tap to enable sound]       |
| [i Tap or press a key to enable sound]        |    | [i enable sound] |    | [Continue: Song A]  [Daily]      |
| [Continue: My song - Studio, 2 h ago]         |    | [Continue ...]   |    | Quick Play     | Instrument Mode |
| > Quick Play          |                       |    | Quick Play       |    | Free Play      | Studio          |
|   Instrument Mode     |   (idle 3D band)      |    | Instrument Mode  |    | Song Library   | Import Music    |
|   Free Play           |                       |    | Free Play        |    | Dance Mode     | Multiplayer     |
|   Studio              |   [Daily challenge]   |    | ... (scrolls)    |    | Characters     | Settings        |
|   ... 12 entries      |                       |    | [Daily]          |    | Help           | About           |
| Version 1.0.0 (Standalone) - 2026-..          |    | Version ...      |    | Version ...                      |
+-----------------------------------------------+    +------------------+    +----------------------------------+
```

States: Loading never applies (the menu is built after `boot.ready`); Empty: no continue
card, no recovery notice; Error: notices as above; Disabled: as the table. Initial focus:
`mm-continue` when shown, else "Quick Play" (P 3 "Quick Play is easy to find"); the entry of
`onboarding.lastMode` is marked with the subtitle prefix "Last used - ".

Keyboard: `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` move through the entries (wrapping), `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`
move between columns in the landscape grid and to the daily card, `Enter` or `Space`
activates, `Home`/`End` jump to the first and last entry; `Escape` does nothing (root).
Touch: tap; the list scrolls vertically in portrait. Exit paths: each entry enters its mode
(Part 1.2 menu map); "Continue" enters the recorded mode with the recorded project or song;
the daily card enters `instrument` or `dance` with `origin:'daily'`. Accessibility:
`mm-list` is a `nav` with `aria-label="Main menu"`; disabled entries keep focus and expose
the reason through `aria-describedby`; the daily card's name is "Daily challenge: {goal},
{song}, {state}".

#### 7.6.3 SCR-QuickPlay

Purpose: the shortest path from the menu to playing (B 7.1, I 11.1, P 4): song, part (an
instrument track or Dance), difficulty, Play. Entered as "Quick Play" it opens at the Quick
Start level (`level:'quick'`); entered as "Instrument Mode" it opens with More options
expanded (`level:'customize'`, title "Instrument Mode").

Entry: SCR-MainMenu "Quick Play" and "Instrument Mode"; SCR-Library "Play"; SCR-ImportInspect
"Play now"; SCR-Results "Back" when `origin` is `quickplay` or `instrumentmode` (selection
restored); the daily card (prefilled and locked).

| Id | Type | Label or content | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qp-filter` | tabs | "All", "Built-in", "Imported", "Projects" | remembered in the session only |
| `qp-songs` | list | row: title (truncated), second line "{style or artist} - {m:ss} - {BPM} BPM", source badge "Built-in", "Imported" or "Project", best result "Best {accuracy} %" when a personal best exists | songs from `Project.Catalog.list()` plus project songs from the index |
| `qp-parts` | list | one row per track with notes: family icon, track name, GM program name, "{n} notes", badge "Recommended" for `Import.recommendTrack`; a final row "Dance" with the four arrow glyphs and subtitle "Step to the beat with four directions" | tracks without notes are listed disabled with "No notes in this track"; audio tracks are not listed |
| `qp-difficulty` | segmented | instrument: "Beginner", "Intermediate", "Advanced", "Expert"; Dance: "Easy", "Normal", "Hard"; each segment has a second line with the note count once the chart exists ("214 notes") | charts are generated with `generateAsync` when the part is chosen (all difficulties, sequentially) |
| `qp-play` | primary button | "Play" | disabled with "Preparing chart..." until `chart.ready` for the chosen difficulty |
| `qp-more` | disclosure button | "More options" / "Fewer options" | |
| `qp-profile` | segmented (inside More options) | "Lanes" (A), "Intervals" (B), "Chords" (C), "Scale" (D), "Instrument" (E), "Rhythm" (F); drums tracks offer only "Rhythm" and show "Drum tracks use the Rhythm profile" | changes the generated chart (`profile` argument) |
| `qp-backing` | toggle | "Backing tracks" (on: the other tracks play; off: only your part and the metronome) | |
| `qp-target` | segmented plus slider | `gameplay.targetTrackMode` and `gameplay.accompanimentVolume` (7.3) | |
| `qp-visual` | toggle | "3D band" (off: the highway is drawn on a plain background and performers are not built) | B 7.1 "performance visualization" |
| `qp-speed` | slider | "Speed" 25-200 %, step 5, default 100 %; badge "Not comparable" when not 100 % | `Transport.setSpeed` at start |
| `qp-countin` | toggle plus segmented | `gameplay.autoCountIn`, `audio.countInBars` | |
| `qp-judgment` | segmented | `gameplay.judgmentPreset` (7.3); badge "Not comparable" on Relaxed and Strict | |
| `qp-stray` | toggle | `gameplay.strayPressPenalty` | |
| `qp-notespeed` | slider | "Note speed" (7.3) | |
| `qp-preview` | `canvas` 2D (height 160 px) plus `p` | chart preview of 8 bars from the first note (`ChartGenerator.preview`): four lanes with glyphs, holds as bars, chords joined by a line; under it `ChartGenerator.describe(chart)` ("Expert: 412 notes, 38 chords, 25 holds; 61 of 473 source notes not charted") | P 11 "automatic charts can be previewed" |
| `qp-listen` | button | "Listen" / "Stop" | plays the arrangement from the preview's first bar for 8 bars through `Transport.main` |
| `qp-calibrate` | button | "Calibrate..." | opens DLG-Calibration |
| `qp-keys` | `p` | keyboard layouts: "Keys: A S K L" with glyphs plus link "Change keys" (opens SCR-Settings Controls); touch layouts: pad layout and pad size segmented controls (7.3) | |
| `qp-daily` | `div.notice.info` (daily origin only) | "Daily challenge: {goal}. Song, part and difficulty are set by the challenge." | song, part and difficulty controls disabled with that reason; judgment preset fixed to Standard and speed to 100 % |

Purpose: the four-button chart play of one track while the arrangement plays (B 7.2, B 7.5,

| Disabled | n/a | none |

Keyboard: lanes `KeyA` `KeyS` `KeyK` `KeyL` (remappable), `Escape` pause, `KeyP` stop all
sound (pauses first, then soft panic), `ShiftLeft`/`ShiftRight` sustain (only audible for
instruments with sustain; does not affect scoring). `KeyQ`/`KeyE` have no effect in chart
play. Touch: the pads; tap `ins-pause`. Gamepad: per Part 6.7 table; start = pause.
Multitouch gestures (pinch, swipe) are suppressed on `#touch` and `#view`. Exit paths: song
end -> SCR-Results; SCR-Pause Restart, Quit; multiplayer host end -> results. Accessibility:
the canvas is `aria-hidden`; HUD announcements per 7.8.6; the pause button's name is "Pause
(Escape)".

#### 7.6.5 SCR-FreePlay

Purpose: play without a chart (B 7.3, P 9): instrument, key, scale or chromatic, profile,
octave, register, note length, velocity, sustain, metronome, tempo, quantized or unquantized
recording, record and replay.

Entry: SCR-MainMenu "Free Play"; tutorial step 4 (instrument choice) uses the same panel
component. Settings come from `session.freePlay` and are written back on change.

Elements:

| Id | Type | Label or content | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fp-instrument` | select pair | "Family" (16 GM families plus "Drum kit"), "Instrument" (programs of the family, "1 Acoustic Grand Piano" ... numbered 1-128 for display, 0-based internally); badge "Synthesized" (`--c-accent-2`) | changing it releases held notes first (`LiveMapper.releaseAll`) so nothing sticks (P 9) |
| `fp-key` | select | "Key": C, C# / Db, D, D# / Eb, E, F, F# / Gb, G, G# / Ab, A, A# / Bb, B | |
| `fp-scale` | select | "Scale": Major, Natural minor, Harmonic minor, Melodic minor, Major pentatonic, Minor pentatonic, Blues, Chromatic, then user scales, then "New custom scale..." | |
| `fp-lock` | toggle plus status line | "Scale lock"; status: "Scale lock on: {key} {scale}" or "Chromatic: every note is available" | turning it off selects Chromatic and remembers the previous scale; turning it on restores it (B 7.3 last bullet) |
| `fp-scale-editor` | inline panel | 12 toggle buttons "1", "b2", "2", "b3", "3", "4", "#4", "5", "b6", "6", "b7", "7" (root always on), name field (1-24 chars), "Save scale", "Cancel" | `Theory.defineScale`; persisted under `settings.userScales` (Part 6.2); max 64 |

| `fp-octave` | number with steppers | "Octave" 2-6 | `KeyQ` down, `KeyE` up; the clamp result is shown |
| `fp-register` | number with steppers | "Register" -7..7 | enabled for profile D only; disabled reason "Register applies to the Scale profile" |
| `fp-slots` | 4 rows (profile C) or 4 selects (profile B) | C: "Root" select, then per lane "Degree" (I-VII), "Chord" (major, minor, dim, aug, sus2, sus4, 7, maj7, m7), "Inversion" (root, 1st, 2nd, 3rd); B: per lane "Interval" 0-24 semitones with names ("Unison", "Major third", "Perfect fifth", "Octave") | hidden for other profiles |
| `fp-length` | segmented plus slider | "Note length": "Hold" (as long as pressed) or "Fixed"; slider 50-2,000 ms, step 10 (fixed only) | |
| `fp-velocity` | slider | "Velocity" 1-127; note "Touch pressure and MIDI velocity are used when the device reports them." | |
| `fp-sustain` | toggle | "Sustain"; note "Or hold Shift" | latched sustain sends CC 64 |
| `fp-metronome` | toggle plus slider | "Metronome", volume | |
| `fp-tempo` | number with steppers | "Tempo" 20-300 BPM, step 1 | `Transport` tempo override |
| `fp-meter` | select | "Time signature": 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 5/4, 6/8, 7/8, 12/8 | |

| `fp-record` | primary button `g-record` | "Record" / "Stop" | count-in per `audio.countInBars` |
| `fp-takeplay` | button `g-play` | "Play take" / "Stop" | |
| `fp-takedel` | danger button `g-trash` | "Delete take" | no dialog: undo toast S-FP-03 "Take deleted." with "Undo" (8 s) |

| `fp-lanes` | four lane labels above the pads (desktop: key caps) | glyph, key letter ("A"), and the note or chord the lane plays now ("C4", "F major") from `Mapping.profileTable` | updates immediately on any key, scale, octave or profile change (P 9) |
| `fp-chord` | large text | last `label` action ("C major", "Perfect fifth", "E4") | `aria-live="polite"` when screen-reader labels are on, throttled to 1 per s |

States:

| State | Trigger | What shows |
|---|---|---|
| Idle | default | record bar "No take yet" |
| Count-in | Record pressed | beat numbers over the performer; Record label "Stop" |

| Take ready | stop with notes | "Take: {n} notes, {m:ss}"; Play take and Open in Studio enabled |

Keyboard: lanes (`KeyA` `KeyS` `KeyK` `KeyL`), `Digit1`-`Digit6` profiles, `KeyQ`/`KeyE`
octave, `ShiftLeft`/`ShiftRight` sustain, `KeyP` stop all sound, `Escape` stops recording
or take playback when active, otherwise Back; UI keys (7.4.5 rule): `KeyR` record and stop,
`Space` play and stop the take. Touch: the four pads (with note labels), simultaneous
presses form chords (B 8.4). Exit paths: Back (guard 7.4.3) -> menu; "Open in Studio" ->
studio. Accessibility: each pad's accessible name is "Lane {n}, {note or chord}"; the
profile control announces the profile name.

#### 7.6.6 SCR-Studio

Purpose: the multitrack workstation (B 7.4, B 16, I 5): tracks, instruments, recording with
count-in, overdub, loop recording, piano roll, quantize, undo and redo, mixer, tempo, meter,
key and scale, section markers, the arrangement overview, save and export. MIDI-event
editing and audio rendering are visibly distinct: the Export menu separates "MIDI file"
and "Project file" (editable events) from "Audio mix" (rendered sound), and the record
button's tooltip says "Records notes, not sound" (B 7.4 last bullet, B 11.5).

Entry: SCR-MainMenu "Studio" (opens `session.lastProjectId`, else a new empty project named
"Untitled project"); SCR-Library "Open in Studio"; SCR-FreePlay "Open in Studio"; tutorial
step 7. On open, DLG-RecoverCheckpoint appears when `Studio.Session.open` returns a newer checkpoint
(Part 6.17.4 A step 8).

| Stage | `st-stage` | collapsible panel "Band" | small 3D view of the project's performers | hidden by default on phones |

States:

| State | Trigger | What shows |
|---|---|---|
| Loading | project opening | skeleton rows and S-STU-01 "Opening project..." |
| Empty project | no tracks | `st-roll` empty state "This project has no tracks yet." with primary "Add track" |
| Empty track | selected track has no notes | roll empty state "No notes on this track. Press Record, or choose Draw and tap the grid." |
| Saved | `project.saved` | chip "Saved"; toast S-STO-02 "Project saved." on manual saves only |
| Unsaved | `project.changed` dirty | chip "Unsaved changes" |
| Saving | save in flight | chip "Saving..."; Save button busy |
| Save failed | `project.saveFailed` | chip "Not saved" and DLG-SaveFailed (or DLG-ProjectTooLarge for size) |
| Read-only | lock held elsewhere | banner S-STO-05 "This project is open in another tab. Close it there to edit here." with "Take over"; every edit control disabled with that reason |
| Count-in, Recording | Recorder states | `st-rec` "Stop recording"; chip "Recording" `--c-error`; the armed track row shows "Recording" text; beat numbers during the count-in over the roll |
| Take review | `studio.take` | `st-take` panel |
| Recording aborted | track deleted or audio lost | toast S-STU-03 "Recording aborted: the track was deleted." or DLG-ResumeAudio plus toast S-STU-04 "Recording stopped. The take was kept." |
| Limit | 32 tracks, 100,000 events | `st-addtrack` disabled with E-PRJ-020 text; recording auto-stop toast S-STU-05 "Recording stopped at 100,000 notes (track limit)." |
| Error | command refused | toast with the E-PRJ text (7.11) |

Keyboard (editor focus; the 7.4.5 rule skips any key bound to a live control while "Play
with keys" is on or a take is recording):

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `Space` | play or stop |
| `KeyR` | record or stop recording |
| `Home`, `End` | playhead to start, to end |
| `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight` | move the selection by one grid step (playhead by one bar when nothing is selected) |
| `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown` | move the selection by one semitone; with Shift by one octave |
| `Alt+ArrowLeft`, `Alt+ArrowRight` | shorten or lengthen the selection by one grid step |
| `Delete`, `Backspace` | delete the selection |
| Ctrl/Cmd+`KeyZ`; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+`KeyZ` or Ctrl+`KeyY` | undo; redo |
| Ctrl/Cmd+`KeyC`, `KeyX`, `KeyV` | copy, cut, paste at the playhead on the selected track |
| Ctrl/Cmd+`KeyA` | select every note of the selected track |
| Ctrl/Cmd+`KeyS` | save |
| `Alt+KeyQ` | quantize the selection with the last quantize settings |
| `Alt+KeyL` | loop on or off |
| `Alt+KeyM`, `Alt+KeyS` | mute, solo the selected track |
| `Equal`, `Minus` | zoom in, zoom out (horizontal) |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab` | move between top bar, transport, overview, tracks, roll, mixer |
| `Escape` | close the open popover or menu; otherwise clear the selection; otherwise Back |

Touch (piano roll): tap a note selects it (tap with a second finger held adds to the
selection); tap empty space deselects (Select) or adds a note of one grid step at the tapped
pitch (Draw); drag a note moves it (snapped when Snap is on); drag its right edge (24 px hit
zone) resizes; one-finger drag on empty space draws a selection rectangle (Select); two-finger
drag scrolls, pinch zooms horizontally; long-press (500 ms) on a note opens a menu "Delete",
"Velocity...", "Copy". Overview: tap seeks; drag on the ruler sets the loop.

Exit paths: Back (guard 7.4.3) -> menu; "Play this track" -> instrument with `origin:'studio'`;
"Characters..." -> customize (project stays loaded); export items stay in Studio.
Accessibility: regions are `section` elements with `aria-label` ("Transport", "Arrangement
overview", "Tracks", "Piano roll", "Mixer"); the piano roll exposes the selection through a
visually hidden live text "{n} notes selected, from bar {b}"; each note is not a DOM element
(canvas), so keyboard editing covers every pointer operation (P 15).

export, delete (Part 1.2).

Entry: SCR-MainMenu "Song Library"; SCR-ImportInspect "Save to Library"; Back from a mode
launched here restores `session.libraryFilter` (query, sort, scroll; P 21).

| `lib-sort` | segmented | "Recent", "Name" | |
| `lib-tabs` | tabs | "All", "Built-in", "Imported", "Projects" | |
| `lib-list` | list | row: title, second line by kind: built-in "{style} - {m:ss}", imported "{format} - {tracks} tracks - {m:ss}", project "{tracks} tracks - modified {relative time} - {size}"; badges "Built-in", "Imported", "Project", compatibility badge for imports ("Supported" `--c-ok`, "Partial" or "Conversion" `--c-warn`) | |
