Layouts: desktop and tablet two panes (list 45 %, detail 55 %); phone portrait list only,
the detail opens as a sheet; phone landscape two panes. States: Empty all (only when the
built-in songs failed to load and nothing was imported or saved): S-GEN-02; Empty tab: "No imported songs yet." with "Import Music", "No saved projects
yet." with "Open Studio"; Loading: skeleton rows while `Storage.listProjects()` resolves;
Error: index damaged is rebuilt silently (Part 6.16.5); a project that fails to load shows
the E-PRJ or E-STO text in DLG-OpenFailed (7.7) with "Open backup" when a `.bak` exists;
Disabled: Delete for built-ins (absent, not disabled).
Keyboard: `Ctrl/Cmd+KeyF` or `Slash` focuses search; arrows move in the list; `Enter` opens
the detail (phone) or activates Play (desktop); `Delete` on a deletable row opens the delete
dialog; `Escape` closes the sheet, else Back. Touch: tap row, sheet with actions. Exit paths:
Play, Open in Studio, Dance, Import, Back -> menu. Accessibility: the list announces "{n}
items" after filtering through a polite status line.

#### 7.6.8 SCR-ImportInspect

Purpose: B 7.5, B 15.1 steps 1-7, I 6.1, I 6.2, P 11: pick a file, watch real progress,
inspect what was detected before anything changes, choose the playable part, preview and
change the generated chart, then confirm or cancel. The current project is untouched until
a confirm action (Part 4.6 S-12).

Entry: SCR-MainMenu "Import Music", SCR-Library "Import Music", SCR-QuickPlay empty states,
tutorial step 6, and a file dropped anywhere on `#app` while a panel mode is active (the drop
enters `import` with the file).

Phases of the screen: Picker, Progress, Report, Error.

Picker elements:

| Id | Type | Label or content |
|---|---|---|
| `imp-drop` | drop zone (`Storage.enableDrop`, class `drop-active` while dragging) | "Drop a music file here" (pointer layouts only; hidden on `body.touch`) |
| `imp-pick` | primary button `g-import` | "Choose file" (calls `Storage.pickFile` inside the click handler) |
| `imp-accepted` | `p` | S-IMP-01 "Accepted: MIDI (.mid, .midi), MusicXML (.xml, .musicxml, .mxl), Guitar Pro 3, 4 and 5 (.gp3, .gp4, .gp5), and audio files (.wav, .mp3, .ogg, .flac) where this browser can decode them. Guitar Pro 6 and 7 files (.gpx, .gp) cannot be imported." |
| `imp-compat` | link button | "Compatibility details" (opens SCR-About at the compatibility table) |
| `imp-limits` | `p` (`--fs-2`) | S-IMP-02 "Limits: 25 MB per file (100 MB for audio), 1,000,000 events, 128 tracks read and 32 kept." |

Progress elements: `imp-stage` (`h2`) with the stage word "Reading file", "Identifying
format", "Reading music data", "Arranging tracks", "Inspecting", "Preparing chart" (from
`import.progress.stage`); `imp-bar` progress bar, determinate only when `fraction` is
non-null, else indeterminate (never a fabricated percentage, B 20.4); `imp-bytes`
"{done} of {total} MB read" while reading; `imp-cancel` button "Cancel" (`Import.cancel()`;
the screen returns to Picker with toast E-IMP-011 "Import cancelled.").

Report elements (tabs `imp-tabs`: "Summary", "Tracks", "Chart", "Warnings ({n})"):

| I 6.1 field | Id | Content (exact form) |
|---|---|---|
| File | `imp-file` | "{fileName} - {size}" plus `.code` hash "{fileHash}" in the detail line |
| Detected format and version | `imp-format` | "{Format name} {version}" ("Standard MIDI File, format 1", "MusicXML 4.0 (compressed .mxl)", "Guitar Pro 5.10", "Audio (WAV, 44,100 Hz, stereo)") plus status badge "Supported", "Partial" or "Conversion" with the word always visible |
| Songs in the file | `imp-sequence` | format 2 or multi-song files only: select "Sequence {i} of {n}: {title}, {tracks} tracks, {notes} notes" (rebuilds the report for the chosen index) |
| Duration | `imp-duration` | "{m:ss} ({bars} bars)" |
| Tempo | `imp-tempo` | "{bpmStart} BPM" plus "{changes} tempo changes ({bpmMin}-{bpmMax} BPM)" when changes > 0; when `source === 'default'`: "120 BPM (the file has no tempo; default used)" |
| Time signatures | `imp-meters` | "4/4 from bar 1; 3/4 from bar 17; ..." (first 50; "and {n} more" when truncated); default: "4/4 (the file has no time signature; default used)" |
| Key signatures | `imp-keys` | "G major from bar 1; ..." or "Not specified in the file" |
| Tracks and instruments, event counts | `imp-tracks` (Tracks tab table) | columns: "Track", "Instrument" (GM name or "Drums"), "Channel" (1-16 for display), "Notes", "Events", "Range" ("E2-G5"), "Max chord", "Notes per bar", "Warnings", "Playable" ("Yes" or the reason), badge "Recommended"; overflow files show a checkbox column "Keep" and the counter "{k} of 32 selected" (selection per Part 6.14.4.6) |
| Unsupported features and conversion warnings | `imp-warnings` (Warnings tab) | grouped "Errors ({e})", "Warnings ({w})", "Notes ({i})"; each row: severity icon plus word, the warning message, location ("Track {name}, bar {b}"), and "x{count}" when coalesced; "{n} more warnings were not listed." when `warningsDropped > 0` |
| Which track will be playable | `imp-playable` | "Playable part: {track name} (recommended)" or the `unplayableReason` text |
| Whether a simplified four-button mapping is needed | `imp-simplify` | from `chordComplexity`: "Largest chord: {n} notes at once." plus one sentence: all false -> "Every difficulty can represent this part without simplification."; some true -> "Four-button play simplifies this part at {list of difficulties}. The original notes are kept and still play."; null -> "Simplification is computed when you choose a part." |
| Informational notes | `imp-notes` | the report's `notes` sentences (Part 6.14.4.7), each as a `notice.info` line |
| Audio start offset (audio files) | `imp-sync` | number "Audio start offset" -30,000..30,000 ms, step 10, help "Positive values start the audio later than the first beat." (E 3.4) |

Chart tab (I 6.2 preview and mapping change): `imp-part` select (playable tracks;
recommended first), `imp-difficulty` segmented (four difficulties), `imp-profile` segmented
"Lanes", "Intervals", "Chords", "Scale", "Instrument", "Rhythm" labeled "Mapping" (changing
it regenerates the chart; the source is never altered), `imp-preview` canvas (as `qp-preview`,
8 bars, with "Earlier" and "Later" buttons stepping 8 bars), `imp-describe` (describe text),
`imp-listen` button "Listen" / "Stop" (preview playback of the candidate song from the
preview's first bar; Part 4.7 import row), and the fixed line S-IMP-03 "The original
arrangement is kept unchanged. The chart is generated from it and can be changed at any
time."

Actions (always visible at the bottom of the Report phase): `imp-playnow` primary "Play now"
(disabled with the unplayable reason when `playable` is false), `imp-save` "Save to
Library", `imp-studio` "Open in Studio", `imp-discard` "Cancel".

Layouts:

```text
Desktop                                                     Phone portrait
+---------------------------------------------------------+ +--------------------------+
| < Back  Import Music                     [Vol]           | | < Import Music    [Vol]  |
| song.mid - 48 KB              Standard MIDI File, fmt 1  | | song.mid  [Supported]    |
|                               [Supported]                | | Summary|Tracks|Chart|Warn|
| Summary | Tracks | Chart | Warnings (3)                  | | 3:12 (96 bars)           |
| Duration 3:12 (96 bars)    | Playable part: Lead (rec.)  | | 120 BPM, 2 changes       |
| Tempo 120 BPM, 2 changes   | Largest chord: 6 notes ...  | | 4/4 from bar 1           |
| Time 4/4 from bar 1        | Notes: Instruments are      | | G major from bar 1       |
| Key G major from bar 1     |  synthesized; timbres ...   | | Playable: Lead (rec.)    |
|                                                          | | ...                      |
| [Play now]  [Save to Library]  [Open in Studio]  Cancel  | | [Play now]               |
+---------------------------------------------------------+ | Save | Studio | Cancel   |
                                                            +--------------------------+
```

Phone landscape: summary list left, tab content right; actions in a bottom bar.

States:

| State | Trigger | What shows |
|---|---|---|
| Empty | Picker phase | drop zone, Choose file, accepted formats |
| Loading | import running | Progress phase |
| Success | `import.done` | Report phase; initial tab Summary; focus on `imp-playnow` (or `imp-studio` when not playable) |
| Success with warnings | report with warnings | Warnings tab label shows the count; status badge "Partial" or "Conversion" |
| Error | `import.failed` | Error phase: `g-error` icon, title "This file could not be imported", the code's text from 7.11 (E-IMP-001 to E-IMP-016; for E-IMP-006 the adapter sentence, including the Part 1.5 Guitar Pro 6 and 7 sentence), the code in `.code`, and the action buttons of Part 6.14.5 ("Choose another file", "Retry", "Compatibility details") |
| Disabled | not playable | Play now disabled with the reason; for audio files the Part 1.5 audio sentence |
| Replace confirmation | Play now or Open in Studio with a dirty open project | DLG-ImportReplace (7.7) |

Keyboard: `Enter` on Choose file opens the picker; `Tab` through tabs and actions; arrows
switch tabs; `Escape` during Progress cancels (same as Cancel), in Report opens nothing and
performs Back (equivalent to Cancel; the candidate is discarded and its audio buffer
released). Touch: tap; tables scroll horizontally inside their own container (the only
horizontal scroll allowed, `touch-action: pan-x pan-y` on the table wrapper). Exit paths:
Play now -> quickplay prefilled with the chosen part, difficulty and profile; Save to
Library -> library with the song selected; Open in Studio -> studio with `Project.fromSong`;
Cancel or Back -> the previous screen with the current project unchanged. Accessibility:
the Progress phase uses `aria-live="polite"` for the stage word; the error title is an
`h2` with `role="alert"`; the Tracks table has `scope="col"` headers.

#### 7.6.9 SCR-Dance

Purpose: Dance Mode as its own experience (B 7.6, B 14, I 7, P 12): song, difficulty,
layout, practice speed and loop, optional life bar, custom chart import and export; then
play with a distinct HUD and avatar choreography.

Entry: SCR-MainMenu "Dance Mode" (select state); SCR-QuickPlay part "Dance" (play state
directly); SCR-Library "Dance"; tutorial step 7; daily card.

Select state elements:

| Id | Type | Label or content |
|---|---|---|
| `dn-songs` | list | as `qp-songs`, plus "Custom chart" badge for songs with an imported dance chart |
| `dn-difficulty` | segmented | "Easy", "Normal", "Hard" with step counts ("96 steps") |
| `dn-layout` | segmented | "Arrows" (four arrows in a row) or "Pads" (2 x 2 diamond) |
| `dn-speed` | slider | "Practice speed" 50-100 %, step 5 (`session.dance.practiceSpeed`); badge "Not comparable" below 100 % |
| `dn-section` | select plus toggle | "Practice section": "Whole song" or a section label; toggle "Loop section" |
| `dn-lifebar` | toggle | "Life bar (song can be failed)" (`gameplay.lifeBar`, default off) |
| `dn-judgment` | segmented | `gameplay.judgmentPreset` |
| `dn-notespeed` | slider | "Step speed" (same key as note speed) |
| `dn-choreo` | toggle | "Dancing avatar" (off: the avatar stays idle; scoring is unaffected) |
| `dn-import` | button | "Import chart (.flmdance.json)" |
| `dn-export` | button | "Export chart" (exports the selected difficulty's chart) |
| `dn-validation` | `div.notice` | chart validation result before play: "Chart checked: {n} steps, {holds} holds, {jumps} jumps." or the error list from `Dance.validate` ("Step at bar 12 beat 3 repeats the same direction twice; the second was removed.", "Overlapping holds on Left at bar 20 were shortened.") with severity words |
| `dn-play` | primary button | "Dance" |

Play state (distinct dance HUD, I 7): steps rise from the bottom of the highway toward four
receptors at the top (the dance highway runs upward, the instrument highway downward, so the
two modes are distinguishable at a glance); the avatar is shown large and centered behind the
lanes; HUD layout: receptor row (arrows with outlines) at 18 % height; judgment word under the
receptors; combo as "{n} combo" centered at 60 % height; score bottom-left; accuracy
bottom-right; progress bar along the bottom edge; life bar (when on) along the top edge as a
bar plus the text "Life {n} %"; step counter "Step {k} of {n}" under the progress bar on
non-compact layouts; section name top-left. Element ids: `dn-receptors`, `dn-life`,
`dn-pause` (as `ins-pause`), plus the shared `hud-*` ids of 7.8.

```text
Phone portrait (Arrows)              Phone portrait (Pads)
+--------------------------+         +--------------------------+
|[||] Life 72 %  =======   |         |[||]  Chorus              |
|  <    v    ^    >        |         |      <  v  ^  >          |
|      GREAT               |         |       PERFECT            |
|   (avatar dancing)       |         |   (avatar)               |
|      24 combo            |         |      31 combo            |
|   ^         <            |         |        [ ^ ]             |
|        v         >      |         |   [ < ]       [ > ]      |
| 12,300          96.1 %   |         |        [ v ]             |
| [ < ][ v ][ ^ ][ > ]     |         | 12,300          96.1 %   |
+--------------------------+         +--------------------------+
```

States: Select: Empty songs (S-GEN-02); Loading "Preparing steps..." while
`DanceChartGenerator` runs; Error: validation errors that cannot be resolved disable
`dn-play` with "This chart has errors that must be fixed: {first error}"; imported chart for
another song shows the Part 5.14.2 notice "This chart was made for '{title}'; steps will be
aligned to the current song's ticks."; Disabled: speed fixed at 100 % in the daily
challenge. Play: Count-in, Playing, Paused (SCR-Pause), Failed (life bar empty: S-DNC-01
"Out of energy. Try again, or turn off the life bar for practice." then results with
`endedBy:'fail'`), Finished ("Song complete" then results). Missing choreography never
blocks scoring: when the avatar cannot be built (Abstract tier or `dn-choreo` off) the HUD
plays alone (E 7).

Keyboard: select state as SCR-QuickPlay; play state `ArrowLeft` `ArrowDown` `ArrowUp`
`ArrowRight` and alternates `KeyD` `KeyF` `KeyJ` `KeyK` (remappable), `Escape` pause, `KeyP`
stop all sound. Touch: the four dance pads (row or diamond per `dn-layout`), simultaneous
presses for jumps. Gamepad: per Part 6.7 dance table. Exit paths: Dance -> play state; play
end -> results; Back (select) -> origin. Accessibility: receptors and pads carry direction
names ("Left", "Down", "Up", "Right") as accessible names and glyphs.

#### 7.6.10 SCR-Multiplayer

Purpose: B 7.7, B 17, I 10, P 13: understand what is shared, create or join a room by
invite and answer codes (room code through the relay in the Online edition), set name and
character, ready up, let the host pick the experience, song and charts, play, see results,
read synchronization quality.

Entry: SCR-MainMenu "Multiplayer"; SCR-Results "Back to lobby" after a multiplayer song.

Phases (one screen, `net.state` drives the phase): Start, Hosting, Joining, Connecting,
Lobby, Countdown (then the SCR-Instrument or SCR-Dance play layout with the multiplayer HUD),
Reconnecting, Ended.

Start phase elements:

| Id | Type | Label or content |
|---|---|---|
| `mp-privacy` | `section.panel` (expanded on the first visit of the session, then collapsed to a one-line summary with "Show details") | heading "What is shared" and S-NET-01 (the privacy statement, 7.11.3) |
| `mp-how` | `section.panel` collapsed | heading "How this works": the edition sentence of Part 1.4, S-NET-02 (the two-device note of Part 1.5), S-NET-03 (late join note of Part 1.5) |
| `mp-name` | text field | "Your name" (1-24 chars, default "Player") |
| `mp-character` | select with preview icon | "Your character" (roster presets and the project's characters) |
| `mp-create` | primary card | "Create room" with subtitle "You host: you choose the song and others join you" |
| `mp-join` | card | "Join room" with subtitle "Paste the invite code you received" |
| `mp-roomcode-create`, `mp-roomcode-join` | cards (Online edition only, relay reachable) | "Create room with a room code", "Join with a room code" |
| `mp-stun` | toggle | "Connect across networks (STUN)" with S-NET-04 "Uses Google's public STUN server (stun.l.google.com) to find a route between networks. Off by default; same-network play works without it." |

Hosting phase: `mp-invite` read-only `textarea.code` (4 rows, selectable) with the invite
code, `mp-invite-copy` primary "Copy invite code" (S-NET-05 "Invite code copied." toast),
`mp-invite-share` "Share" (only when `navigator.share` exists), instruction S-NET-06 "Send
this code to the player who joins. Then paste their answer code below.", `mp-answer` text
area "Paste the answer code", `mp-connect` "Connect", `mp-gathering` status "Preparing
invite..." (ICE gathering, up to 3 s) and, when STUN is on and failed, S-NET-07 "STUN server
not reachable; connections may only work on the same network." For a third and fourth
player the lobby shows `mp-invite-more` "Invite another player", which repeats this phase
for one more peer.

Joining phase: `mp-invite-in` text area "Paste the invite code", `mp-make-answer` primary
"Create answer", then `mp-answer-out` read-only code with "Copy answer code" and S-NET-08
"Send this answer code back to the host. You will join as soon as the host connects."
Relay join: `mp-roomcode` field "Room code" (6 characters, uppercase letters and digits,
`autocapitalize="characters"`), "Join".

Lobby elements:

| Id | Type | Label or content |
|---|---|---|
| `mp-room` | `h2` | "Room {roomCode}" (relay) or "Room hosted by {name}" (P2P) plus the player count "{n} of 4 players" |
| `mp-players` | list | per player: slot number, name, character icon, part ("Keys", "Drums", "Same chart" in Synchronized Play), state word "Ready" (`g-check`) or "Not ready", "Host" badge, latency "{rtt} ms", sync word "Good", "Fair" or "Poor" |
| `mp-experience` | three cards (host chooses; guests see the choice) | "Synchronized Play" - "Everyone plays the same chart; scores are compared."; "Cooperative Band" - "Each player plays a different part of the same song."; "Collaborative Studio" disabled with the Part 1.5 sentence "Collaborative Studio is not in this version. Synchronized Play and Cooperative Band are available." |
| `mp-song` | select (host) or text (guests) | built-in songs and songs every player has (matched by `sourceHash`); guests without the song see E-NET-007 |
| `mp-difficulty` | segmented (host) | four difficulties (Synchronized Play: one for everyone; Cooperative Band: each player picks their own) |
| `mp-part` | select | Synchronized Play: the host's chosen track for everyone; Cooperative Band: each player picks a free track ("Taken by {name}" for taken tracks) |
| `mp-ready` | toggle button | "Ready" / "Not ready" |
| `mp-start` | primary button (host only) | "Start"; disabled with "Waiting for every player to be ready" or "At least 2 players are needed" |
| `mp-diag` | collapsible `section` | heading "Connection quality": per peer "Round trip {rtt} ms", "Clock offset {offset} ms", "Jitter {jitter} ms", "Samples {n}", "Missed updates {m}", "Dropped messages {d}", "Rejected messages {r}", and the quality word with its rule "Good: under 20 ms sync error; Fair: under 50 ms; Poor: above 50 ms" (I 10.2) |
| `mp-leave` | danger button | "Leave room" (no dialog; results of a finished song stay in the history) |

Countdown and play: the host's `start` arrives with `tStartShared`; the lobby shows
"Starting in {s}" counted from shared time, then the play layout of SCR-Instrument (or
SCR-Dance) with `ins-peers` and `ins-sync` (7.6.4). Pause: any player's pause request is
sent to the host; only the host's pause and resume apply (SCR-Pause shows "Paused by {name}";
guests see "Waiting for the host to resume" instead of Resume).

States:

| State | Trigger (`net.state`) | What shows |
|---|---|---|
| Empty | `idle` | Start phase |
| Loading | `creating`, `inviting`, `connecting` | the phase's status line ("Preparing invite...", "Connecting...") with an indeterminate bar after 300 ms |
| Success | `lobby` | Lobby; toast S-NET-09 "{name} joined." per new peer |
| Reconnecting | `reconnecting` | banner S-NET-10 "Connection lost. Trying to reconnect for up to 60 seconds..." with "Leave room"; in play the transport pauses for everyone (host authority) |
| Ended | `ended` | host left: DLG-NetError variant with E-NET-009, then SCR-Results with the results so far, then the Start phase; reconnection timeout: E-NET-015 |
| Error | `error` | DLG-NetError with the code's text and "Retry" (repeats the phase) and "Back" |
| Disabled | no WebRTC | the menu entry is disabled (7.6.2); relay controls hidden in the Standalone edition and toast "Relay rooms need the Online edition build. Invite codes still work." when `?online=` is given (Part 1.4) |
| Song in progress | a guest connects while the host plays | S-NET-03 "A song is in progress. You will join the room when it ends." |

Keyboard: `Tab` order follows the phase top to bottom; `Ctrl/Cmd+KeyC` in a code field
copies; `Enter` in the paste field submits; `Escape` is Back (Start phase -> menu; Hosting
and Joining -> Start phase with the pending connection closed; Lobby -> asks nothing and
leaves through `mp-leave` semantics). Touch: long-press on a code field selects it; the
Paste buttons call `navigator.clipboard.readText()` where permitted, otherwise the field is
focused with the hint "Long-press and choose Paste". Exit paths: Leave room or Back ->
menu (connection closed, Part 4.7.2 step 12); Start -> play; results -> lobby.
Accessibility: code fields have `aria-label="Invite code"` and `"Answer code"`; the player
list is a live region announcing joins, leaves and ready changes politely.

#### 7.6.11 SCR-Characters

Purpose: the character editor (B 13, I 8, P 8): presets, every option of the catalog, a
seeded randomize, instrument and stage slot, animation style, stage theme, with an immediate
3D preview on the same renderer and rig as the stage and no scene reload (I 8 performance
requirement).

Entry: SCR-MainMenu "Characters"; SCR-Studio "Characters..."; SCR-Multiplayer "Your
character" link "Edit". Characters edited here are the open project's characters when a
project is open (`project.characters`), else the settings roster.

Elements:

| Id | Type | Label or content |
|---|---|---|
| `ch-roster` | list (horizontal on phones) | five slots "Slot 1" to "Slot 5", each the character's name and family icon of its instrument, "Empty" when unused |
| `ch-preview` | `canvas#view` region (or `#flat` portrait in Abstract) | the edited character alone with its instrument, idle loop plus the preview phrase gestures |
| `ch-previewsound` | toggle | "Preview sound" (plays the instrument's M-30 preview phrase at -12 dB, looped) |
| `ch-tabs` | tabs | "Presets", "Body", "Skin", "Hair", "Face", "Clothes", "Accessories", "Role", "Stage" |
| `ch-presets` | card grid | the 8 built-in presets plus saved presets, each with its name |
| `ch-body` | segmented | "Slim", "Average", "Broad"; slider "Height" 90-110 %, step 1 (badge "Changes proportions" on these two rig-affecting options) |
| `ch-skin` | swatch grid | 8 swatches named "Skin tone 1" ... "Skin tone 8" |
| `ch-hair` | segmented plus swatches | styles "None", "Short", "Medium", "Long", "Curly", "Mohawk"; color swatches with names |
| `ch-face` | segmented | "Face 1" ... "Face 4" |
| `ch-clothes` | three groups | Top: "Tee", "Shirt", "Hoodie", "Jacket", "Tank", "Dress"; Bottom: "Jeans", "Shorts", "Skirt", "None"; Shoes: "Sneakers", "Boots", "Bare"; each with color swatches |
| `ch-accessories` | toggle chips | "Hat", "Glasses", "Headphones", "Scarf", "Wristband" (up to 5) |
| `ch-role` | selects | "Name" (text 1-24), "Plays" (the open song's tracks or "Nothing (idle)"), "Stage position" (5-slot mini map, the occupied slots marked with names), "Animation style" segmented "Calm", "Normal", "Energetic" |
| `ch-stage` | card grid | "Default" plus unlocked themes ("Neon", "Club", "Sunset"); locked themes show "Unlock: {condition}" (P 21 no unexplained gaps) |
| `ch-random` | button | "Randomize" (seeded; stays within valid combinations, P 8) |
| `ch-savepreset` | button | "Save as preset" (name field 1-24) |
| `ch-export`, `ch-import` | buttons | "Export character (.flmchar.json)", "Import character..." |
| `ch-reset` | button | "Reset to preset" |
| `ch-compat` | `p` notice line | automatic compatibility notes: S-CHR-01 "A hat covers long hair; the hair is shown short under the hat.", S-CHR-02 "Headphones replace the hat; only one can be worn.", S-CHR-03 "A dress replaces the bottom piece." (shown while the combination is active) |

Layouts: desktop: roster column left, preview center (55 %), option tabs right; phone
portrait: preview top 45 %, roster strip, tabs and options below in a scroll container;
phone landscape: preview left half, options right half.

States: Empty roster slot (tap creates a character from preset 1); Loading: none (options
are local data; the preview rebuilds one performer within a frame budget, Part 6.21);
Success: changes apply immediately, `character.changed`, and are persisted on change (toast
none; the roster row updates); Error: an imported character file that fails validation shows
the E-IMP-013 text or "This character file is not valid." (S-CHR-04) and nothing changes;
Disabled: stage themes not yet unlocked; "Plays" when no song or project is open ("Open a
project or choose a song to assign instruments").
Keyboard: arrows in grids and segmented controls, `Enter` applies, `Tab` between regions,
`Escape` Back. Touch: tap; the preview can be rotated by a one-finger horizontal drag (the
only gesture on the canvas here; vertical drags scroll the options). Exit paths: Back ->
previous screen (menu, studio or multiplayer lobby) with changes kept. Accessibility:
every swatch has a color name; the preview canvas has `role="img"` with a generated
description ("{name}: average build, short dark brown hair, blue tee, jeans, plays Keys,
slot 2").

#### 7.6.12 SCR-Settings

Purpose: every setting in one place by category (7.3), the remap UI, calibration, data and
backup, privacy statement, advanced options. Changes apply immediately and persist on change
(no Save button; Part 1.2).

Entry: SCR-MainMenu "Settings"; links from other screens open it at a category (`params:
{category}`).

Elements: `set-cats` category list (Audio, Controls, Gameplay, Video, Accessibility,
Calibration, Data and backup, Privacy, Advanced) and `set-panel` showing the selected
category's rows (7.3 for keys, controls and ranges). Category-specific elements:

| Category | Elements beyond the 7.3 rows |
|---|---|
| Audio | `set-fidelity` note under the instrument quality row: "All instruments are synthesized in real time. Loading SoundFont (.sf2) sound banks is not supported in this version." (Part 1.5); `set-test` button "Play test sound" (a C major chord on piano, 1 s) |
| Controls | `set-remap` table: one row per control: "Lane 1" to "Lane 4" (with glyphs), "Dance left", "Dance down", "Dance up", "Dance right", "Pause", "Stop all sound", "Octave down", "Octave up", "Sustain", "Profile 1" to "Profile 6"; each row shows up to 3 key chips (key name such as "A", "Arrow Left", "Left Shift"), a chip's `g-close` removes it (refused for the last key with S-INP-01 "Each control needs at least one key."), and "Add key" starts capture: the row shows S-INP-02 "Press a key for {control}. Escape cancels." and the next keydown is offered to `Input.remap`; a conflict opens DLG-RemapConflict; "Reset controls to defaults" button. `set-gamepad`: read-only table of the gamepad map with S-INP-03 "Gamepad buttons are fixed in this version." `set-midi`: toggle "Use MIDI devices" (disabled with the Part 1.5 MIDI sentence when unavailable), device list, lane note pickers. `set-pads`: pad layout, size, opacity, and "Touch pads": "Automatic", "Always show", "Never show" (writes `onboarding.inputMode` `auto`, `touch`, `desktop`); "Touch input": "Automatic", "Pointer events", "Touch events" (`input.touchApi`) |
| Gameplay | rows of 7.3; comparability badges |
| Video | rows of 7.3; current tier line "Running: {tier} ({reason})" |
| Accessibility | rows of 7.3 plus a live sample: a four-lane strip with glyphs that reflects high contrast and glyph settings |
| Calibration | current values with units; `set-wizard` primary "Run calibration" (DLG-Calibration); "Reset calibration" |
| Data and backup | "Export settings (.flmsettings.json)"; "Import settings..." (DLG-ImportSettings); "Show first-launch setup again"; "Clear performance history" (DLG-ConfirmClear); "Reset all settings" (DLG-ConfirmReset); storage line "Storage: {mode words}" and the current storage notice; S-STO-03 "Browser storage is not a permanent backup. Export projects you want to keep." (I 5.3) |
| Privacy | S-SET-01 (7.11.3): what is stored locally and that nothing is sent anywhere outside multiplayer; link "Multiplayer privacy" showing S-NET-01 |
| Advanced | rows of 7.3; button "Open diagnostics" |

Layouts: desktop two panes (categories 16rem, panel); phone portrait categories as a list,
the panel pushed as a sub-view inside the screen (Back returns to the list, not to the
menu); phone landscape two panes.
States: Loading none; Success: every change shows its new value immediately, no toast;
Error: an invalid value typed into a number field is clamped on commit and the field shows
the clamped value with S-SET-02 "Adjusted to the allowed range ({min} to {max})." for 3 s;
Disabled: rows unavailable in this browser show their Part 4.3 gate reason; Empty: none.
Keyboard: arrows in the category list, `Enter` opens, `Tab` into the panel, sliders with
arrows (one step), `PageUp`/`PageDown` (ten steps), `Home`/`End` (min, max); during key
capture every key is captured except `Escape` (cancels) and `Tab` (cancels and moves on).
Touch: tap; sliders drag; number steppers. Exit: Back -> previous screen (or the category
list on phones). Accessibility: each row's label is the accessible name; values announce
with units ("Input offset, plus 12 milliseconds").

"Press any key, pad or controller button" showing the last control as "{physical} -> {control
name} in {context}" (Input in a display-only binding; no sound, Part 1.2); `hlp-bindings`
read-only tables per context with "Change" links to SCR-Settings Controls; `hlp-tutorial`

  tracks, speed, practice loops and chart preview."
- "Free Play: no chart and no score. Choose an instrument, key and scale and play anything;
  record takes and send them to the Studio."
- "Studio: build songs track by track. Record with a count-in, overdub, edit notes in the
  piano roll, mix, and export MIDI, project files or an audio mix."
- "Dance Mode: step on four directions in time with the music. It has its own charts,
  difficulties and score, separate from instrument play."
- "Multiplayer: 2 to 4 players on their own devices, connected by invite codes. Play the
  same chart competitively or different parts as a band."

Profiles tab: one table per profile from `Mapping.profileTable(profile, {key: C major,
octave 4})` with the profile descriptions "Lanes: each button plays one note of the scale.",
"Intervals: buttons add intervals above a root note.", "Chords: each button plays a chord of
the key.", "Scale: buttons walk up and down the scale four notes at a time.", "Instrument:
patterns suited to the selected instrument (power chords on guitar, root and fifth on
bass).", "Rhythm: drum sounds on every button." Tips tab: calibration, touch, gamepad
(Firefox note "A controller appears after you press one of its buttons."), MIDI (Part 1.5
sentence), local two-player (Part 1.5 sentence), and the OQ-1 sentence S-INP-04 "If chords
do not register on a touch screen, choose Settings > Controls > Touch input: Touch events."
Layouts: tabs on top, content scrolls; desktop shows the tester beside the tables.
States: static content; Disabled: gamepad and MIDI rows show their reasons. Keyboard:
arrows switch tabs; every key pressed while the Controls tab is open goes to the tester
except `Escape` (Back) and `Tab`. Exit: Back -> previous screen.

#### 7.6.14 SCR-About

Purpose: edition, version and build, honest limits, compatibility, licenses, privacy
summary (B 3.6, B 5.4, B 26.8, P 18).

Elements (one scrolling page with an in-page index `ab-index`):

| Id | Content |
|---|---|
| `ab-version` | "Finger Lickin Music {VERSION}" and "Build {date}" and "Test build" when `FLM.BUILD.test` |
| `ab-edition` | the Standalone or Online edition sentence (Part 1.4, 7.11.6) |
| `ab-context` | "Opened from: {This device (file) or a web server (https) or a web server (http)}"; S-GEN-03 "Single file, no build needed to play."; S-GEN-04 "Opening the file directly or over HTTPS gives the full feature set; plain HTTP disables MIDI input." |
| `ab-limits` | the "Limits of this version" block (7.11.6) |
| `ab-compat` | table from `Import.COMPATIBILITY`: "Format", "Files", "Status" (Supported, Partial, Conversion, Unsupported, always as words with the badge color), "Preserved", "Not preserved or approximated" |
| `ab-browsers` | the five target browsers with the claim text; until Phase 15 every row reads "Not yet verified" (Part 1.6 policy 2) |
| `ab-licenses` | "Third-party code: none." / "Fonts, sounds, models: none; all content is original and synthesized." / "Built-in songs are original compositions for this game." / the game license line from Part 10.3 |
| `ab-privacy` | S-SET-01 short form and S-NET-01 link |
| `ab-credits` | "Finger Lickin Music is part of the HTML-Games collection." |

Layout: single column `max-width: 44rem` on every family. States: static; the compatibility
table scrolls horizontally on phones inside its wrapper. Keyboard: `Tab` through index links
and Back; arrows scroll. Exit: Back. Accessibility: the index is a `nav`; tables have
captions.

#### 7.6.15 SCR-Diagnostics

Purpose: development and support diagnostics (B 24, I 3.5, I 13.2, P 19): timing, audio,
rendering, storage, input and network metrics, the error list, the log tail, export.

Entry: SCR-Settings > Advanced > "Open diagnostics"; `?diag` (the overlay plus this screen
from the menu footer link "Diagnostics", shown only with `?diag`).

Elements: sections `dg-build`, `dg-caps`, `dg-timing`, `dg-audio`, `dg-render`, `dg-storage`,
`dg-input`, `dg-net`, `dg-errors`, `dg-log`, each a two-column key and value table in
`--font-mono` `--fs-1`, refreshed once per second while visible:

| Section | Rows |
|---|---|
| Build | version, edition, build date, test build, URL parameters in effect |
| Capabilities | every `Caps` flag "yes" or "no"; the degraded list with reasons |
| Timing | audio state, sample rate, base and output latency, latency estimate (with "estimated" when derived), anchor offset, anchor method, anchor spread (ms), scheduler lookahead 120 ms and tick 25 ms, stall count and the last stall gap, last drift check result |
| Audio | active voices / cap, peak active, stolen, dropped, channel strips, audio nodes, metronome state |
| Render | tier and reason, FPS, p50 and p95 frame ms, draws, triangles, context losses, resolution scale |
| Storage | mode, notice, quota usage of quota ("unknown" when not available), projects in the index, last save result and time |
| Input | sources seen, held controls, gamepads (id, mapping), MIDI inputs, touch probe maximum (OQ-1) |
| Network | state, role, transport, per peer RTT, offset, jitter, quality, messages in, out, dropped, rejected |
| Errors | last 50: time, code, class, count, user message |
| Log | last 100 entries with level filter "Info" or "Debug" |

Buttons: `dg-export` primary "Export diagnostics" (downloads `.flmdiag.json`), `dg-copy`
"Copy diagnostics", `dg-include` toggle "Include song content" (off by default; S-GEN-05
"Diagnostics never include songs, projects or recordings unless you turn this on."),
`dg-overlay` toggle "Show stats overlay", `dg-tone` "Test tone" (440 Hz, 0.5 s),
`dg-selftest` "Run self-test" (test build only; absent in the shipped build) with a results
table "Group", "Test", "Result" ("Pass" or "Fail"), "ms", "Message" and the summary line
"{passed} of {total} passed".
Layout: one column of sections on phones; two columns on tablet and desktop, the log full
width at the bottom. States: Loading: values show "-" until the first refresh; Error: a provider that throws
shows "unavailable" for its rows; Disabled: self-test absent in the shipped build.
Keyboard: `Tab` through sections and buttons. Exit: Back.

#### 7.6.16 SCR-Tutorial

Purpose: the interactive tutorial of I 11.3 (seven steps, each skippable and repeatable,
keyboard and touch variants); step content and criteria are in 7.9.2.

Entry: SCR-FirstLaunch "Learn the basics"; SCR-Help "Start the tutorial"; SCR-MainMenu
daily card area shows "Learn the basics" while `onboarding.tutorialDone` is false.

Elements: `tut-step` (`h1`) "Step {n} of 7: {title}"; `tut-dots` seven step markers with
state words for screen readers ("done", "current", "skipped", "not started");
`tut-instruction` the instruction text for the active input variant; `tut-goal` progress
text ("2 of 3 notes played"); `tut-feedback` per-attempt feedback; `tut-repeat` "Repeat
step"; `tut-skip` "Skip step"; `tut-next` primary "Next" (appears on success; auto-advance
after 1.5 s unless focus is on a button); `tut-exit` "Leave tutorial"; step-specific content
(instrument choices, record bar, file picker button, mode cards) and the highway and HUD for
step 3. Layout: instruction panel top (desktop: left column 30 %), stage and highway center,
pads bottom on touch. States: per step Waiting, Success ("Nice!" plus the criterion met),
Retry ("Not yet: {hint}"), Skipped; Disabled: step 2 on devices reporting fewer than 2 touch
points shows "This device cannot press two pads at once; this step is skipped." and is
marked skipped. Keyboard: the gameplay keys of the step plus `Escape` (opens a small menu
"Resume", "Repeat step", "Skip step", "Leave tutorial"). Exit paths: step 7 choice -> studio
or dance (`origin:'tutorial'`); "Leave tutorial" -> menu (progress kept; `tutorialDone`
stays false unless step 7 was reached).

#### 7.6.17 SCR-Results

Purpose: the performance summary (B 9.4, I 2.4, I 9, P 5.2): score, accuracy, combo,
counts, completion, section feedback that explains where to improve, personal best,
unlocks, retry.

Entry: `chart.finished` (Part 4.7.1 step 12); multiplayer end.

Elements:

| Id | Content |
|---|---|
| `res-head` | "{song title}" (truncated 48), "{part or Dance} - {difficulty} - {profile name}" and "Speed {n} %" when not 100 % |
| `res-score` | score (`--fs-6`, `.num`, thousands separators) |
| `res-accuracy` | "Accuracy {aa.aa} %" (two decimals of percent) |
| `res-combo` | "Max combo {n}" |
| `res-counts` | four rows "Perfect {n}", "Great {n}", "Good {n}", "Miss {n}" with the words always shown |
| `res-completion` | "Completed {n} %" (`completion`), plus "Hold breaks {n}" when > 0 and "Extra presses {n}" when `stray > 0` |
| `res-timing` | "Average timing: {n} ms late", "{n} ms early" or "on time" (when abs mean < 5 ms); "Early {e}, late {l}"; and, when abs mean >= 15 ms, the hint S-PLAY-02 "You are consistently {early or late}. Calibration can correct this." with the button "Calibrate..." |
| `res-sections` | one row per section: label, accuracy bar with the percentage text, "{judged} notes"; the worst section (Part 6.9.4 F) is marked "Practice this" with `g-warn` and the word |
| `res-best` | "New personal best! +{delta}" (`--c-ok`), "Personal best: {score}", or "Not counted for personal bests: {reasons}" where reasons come from the non-comparable settings ("relaxed timing", "speed 80 %", "song not finished", "extra-press penalty", "calibration changed during the song") |
| `res-unlocks` | list of `progress.unlock` items: "Achievement: {title}" and "Unlocked: {title}" with their descriptions |
| `res-daily` | daily origin only: "Daily challenge complete!" or "Daily goal: {goal}. You reached {value}." |
| `res-players` | multiplayer only: table "Rank", "Player", "Score", "Accuracy", "Max combo" from the host's authoritative final `scoreUpdate`; S-NET-11 "Scores are calculated by the host." |
| `res-retry` | primary "Retry" |
| `res-practice` | "Practice {section}" (enters the same mode with the section looped and speed 75 %) |
| `res-back` | "Back" (to the origin screen with its state restored) or, in multiplayer, "Back to lobby" |

Layout: desktop two columns (summary left, sections and unlocks right) over a dimmed idle
stage; phones one column with the buttons in a bottom bar. States: Loading: none (the
summary exists at entry); Success as above; Error: if `Progress.record` fails to persist,
S-PRG-01 "Your result could not be saved to the history." and the screen still shows the
result; Empty: a run with zero judged notes (quit at once) shows "No notes were played."
and no best line. Keyboard: `Enter` Retry (initial focus), `Tab` to others, `Escape` Back.
Exit paths: Retry (full leave and enter, Part 1.2); Practice; Back. Accessibility: the
summary is announced once on entry through the polite region: "Score {n}, accuracy {a}
percent, max combo {c}".

#### 7.6.18 SCR-Pause

Purpose: pause without side effects (P 5.2 "pausing does not register additional notes"),
practice tools (I 6.3), view options, restart, quit.

Entry: `Escape`, `ins-pause` or `dn-pause`, gamepad start, browser back, and every
interruption of Part 4.7.4 that pauses (reason line set). The Judge is inactive while this
screen is up (Part 6.9.4 B.1); held controls were released by `Input.releaseAll`.

Elements:

| Id | Type | Label or content |
|---|---|---|
| `ps-reason` | `p` | empty for user pauses; otherwise S-PLAY-03 "Paused because the game went to the background.", S-PLAY-04 "Paused because the controller disconnected.", S-PLAY-05 "Paused because playback stalled.", S-PLAY-06 "Paused because sound was interrupted.", S-NET-12 "Paused by {name}." |
| `ps-resume` | primary button | "Resume"; multiplayer guests: replaced by the text "Waiting for the host to resume" |
| `ps-restart` | button | "Restart" |
| `ps-practice` | disclosure "Practice" | target track mode, accompaniment volume, "Speed" 25-200 % (step 5), "Speed up after each clean pass" (+5 % per pass with no miss, up to 100 %), "Section" select plus "Loop section" toggle, "Restart from section" (instrument and dance; disabled in multiplayer with "Practice tools are not available in multiplayer") |
| `ps-view` | disclosure "View" | camera preset, camera motion, effects level, note speed |
| `ps-pads` | disclosure "Touch pads" | "Show touch pads" toggle, layout, size |
| `ps-calibrate` | button | "Calibration..." (DLG-Calibration; changing values marks the run not comparable, toast "Calibration changed; results not comparable") |
| `ps-volume` | slider | master volume |
| `ps-panic` | button `g-panic` | "Stop all sound" (soft panic; `Space` and `KeyP` do the same while paused) |
| `ps-quit` | button | "Quit" (to the origin; the run is not recorded) |

Behavior: Resume shows a countdown over the highway of three beats at the current tempo
(each at least 400 ms) with the numbers "3", "2", "1"; the transport stays paused during it
and resumes exactly at the paused position (no drift, B 7.5); lane presses during the
countdown are ignored (the Judge stays inactive until `resume`). Practice changes apply on
Resume (a speed change re-anchors the transport, Part 4.5.1). Restart runs the full leave
and enter sequence with identical parameters (P 5.2).
Layout: a centered dialog-like panel (`.dialog` styling, but a stack screen) over the frozen
stage; phones: full-width bottom panel with Resume first. States: Paused; Disabled as noted.
Keyboard: `Escape` Resume (also browser back), `Enter` activates the focused button (initial
focus Resume), arrows move between buttons; no other single-key shortcut exists on this screen
besides `Escape`, `Space` and `KeyP`. Exit paths: Resume, Restart, Quit. Accessibility:
`role="dialog"` semantics with `aria-labelledby` the heading "Paused".

### 7.7 Dialogs

Rules for every dialog (`FLM.UI.dialog(id, params)`, M-26):

- Root `#dlg-<slug>`, `role="dialog"` (`role="alertdialog"` for DLG-SaveFailed, DLG-NetError
  and the returnToMenu variant of DLG-Unsupported), `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby`
  the title and `aria-describedby` the body. Focus is trapped and restored (7.4.4).
- The title names the affected operation; the body states the consequence of each choice
  in plain words (P 21 "confirmation dialogs describe consequences accurately"); no dialog
  says "Are you sure?".
- Buttons: at most three plus a close icon only where a Cancel exists. Desktop: right-aligned
  row, primary rightmost; phones: full-width stack, primary on top. The default-focused
  button is never destructive. `Escape` triggers the button marked "Escape" below (none for
  dialogs that must be answered).
- Gameplay is paused before any dialog opens over a gameplay screen; M-07 ignores gameplay
  inputs while `ui.dialog` reports an open dialog (Part 4.4).
- A dialog resolves with the id of the chosen button or `'dismissed'` (mode leave, Part
  4.7.2 step 10).

| Dialog | Title | Body (exact) | Buttons (default focus marked *, Escape marked E) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DLG-UnsavedChanges (Studio, Library open, New project) | "Unsaved changes" | "{project} has {n} unsaved changes since {last save time, or 'it was created'}. If you leave without saving, these changes are lost. The last autosave ({autosave time}) can still be restored when you open the project again." (the autosave sentence is omitted when no checkpoint exists) | "Save and leave"* (primary), "Leave without saving" (danger), "Cancel" E |
| DLG-UnsavedChanges (Free Play variant) | "Keep this take?" | "Your Free Play take ({n} notes) has not been saved. Save it as a project to keep it, or leave without it." | "Save as project"* (opens the name field, then saves), "Leave without saving" (danger), "Cancel" E |
| DLG-SaveFailed | "Save failed" | "{E-STO text from 7.11.2}" followed by "Your work is still open here, and no saved copy was overwritten." | "Export to file"* (primary), "Try again", "Manage projects" (opens DLG-ManageProjects), close icon E |
| DLG-ProjectTooLarge | "Project too large for this browser" | "This project needs {size}, but this browser can only keep {limit} per project here because {reason}. Export it to a file to keep it; the project stays open." Reasons: "the browser database is not available" or "projects with recordings need the browser database"; `limit` = "2 MB" | "Export to file"* (primary), "Close" E |
| DLG-ManageProjects | "Free up space" | "Delete projects you no longer need, then save again. Export a project first if you want to keep a copy." followed by the list (name, size, modified) with a "Delete" button per row that turns into "Confirm delete" for 4 s | "Close"* E |
| DLG-SaveConflict | "Newer copy found" | "A newer copy of this project was saved by another tab or session. Overwrite it, or save this one under a new name?" | "Save as copy"* (primary), "Overwrite" (danger), "Cancel" E |
| DLG-RecoverCheckpoint | "Restore autosave?" | "An autosaved version from {time} is newer than the last save. Restore it?" | "Restore"* (primary), "Keep current" E |
| DLG-OpenFailed | "Project could not be opened" | "{E-PRJ or E-STO text}" followed by "Nothing in your library was changed." | "Open backup" (only when a `.bak` exists; primary then), "OK"* E |
| DLG-ImportReplace | "Close the open project?" | "{project} has unsaved changes. Continuing with the imported song closes it. Save it first to keep the changes." | "Save and continue"* (primary), "Continue without saving" (danger), "Cancel" E |
| DLG-AudioBlocked | "Turn on sound" | "Your browser keeps sound off until you tap or press a key on this page. {mode name} needs sound." After a failed attempt the body adds S-AUD-03 "Sound did not start. Check that this tab and the device are not muted, then try again." | "Turn on sound"* (primary; its click handler calls `Audio.unlock()`), "Cancel" E (rejects the mode enter with E-AUD-002, Part 4.7) |
| DLG-ResumeAudio | "Sound was interrupted" | "Another app, a call or the lock screen interrupted the sound. {The song is paused at {m:ss}. or Recording stopped; the take was kept.}" | "Resume sound"* (primary; calls `ctx.resume()` in the gesture), "Stay paused" E |
| DLG-DeleteTrack | "Delete track?" | "Delete \"{track}\" with its {n} notes{, {c} charts}{ and {k} recorded takes}? Undo brings it back." plus, when it is the record target during recording, "Recording on this track stops and the current take is discarded." | "Delete track" (danger), "Cancel"* E |
| DLG-DeleteItem (Library) | "Delete from library?" | "Delete \"{name}\" from this browser, including its backups and autosaves? Files you exported are not affected. This cannot be undone." | "Delete" (danger), "Export first" (opens DLG-Export for the item), "Cancel"* E |
| DLG-Calibration | "Calibration" | wizard, 7.7.1 | per step |
| DLG-RemapConflict | "Key already in use" | "{key} is already used for {control} ({context}). Use it for {new control} instead? {control} keeps its other keys." When the other control has no other key: "{control} has no other key, so {key} cannot be moved. Choose another key, or give {control} a second key first." | "Use for {new control}"* (primary; hidden in the no-other-key case), "Choose another key" (restarts capture), "Cancel" E |

Keep this screen open."; a file name field (default per Part 5.14) | "Export"* (primary), "Cancel" E; while rendering: indeterminate progress, "Rendering..." and only "Cancel" |
| DLG-ImportSettings | "Replace settings?" | "Replace your settings with the ones in {file}? Controls, calibration, volumes and display settings change. Projects and performance history are not affected." | "Replace settings" (primary), "Cancel"* E |
| DLG-ConfirmReset | "Reset all settings?" | "Controls, calibration, volumes and display settings return to their defaults. Projects, characters and performance history are kept." | "Reset settings" (danger), "Cancel"* E |
| DLG-ConfirmClear | "Clear performance history?" | "All {n} results, personal bests and daily challenge records on this device are deleted. Achievements and unlocked items are kept. This cannot be undone." | "Clear history" (danger), "Cancel"* E |

#### 7.7.1 DLG-Calibration wizard

Goal (I 2.3, I 3.5, B 8.5): measure the two offsets of Part 5.12 without technical terms,
and preview the third. Width `min(96vw, 40rem)`. The wizard uses the metronome click on
`Transport.main` (Part 1.2 settings row) and reads taps from `input.event` (Input context
`instrument`, any lane control counts as a tap; the pads are shown on touch devices). It
never claims an exact hardware measurement (I 3.5); the result is a calibration.

| Step | Title and instruction (exact) | Procedure | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "1. Listen and tap" - "Close your eyes if it helps. Tap any lane key or pad on every click you hear. The first four clicks are for getting into the rhythm." | 12 clicks at 90 BPM (667 ms apart), accent on every 4th; the screen shows only a counter "Click {k} of 12" (no flashing, so only hearing is measured); taps are matched to the nearest click within +/- 300 ms; taps on clicks 1-4 are ignored | `A` = median of `(tap.tAudio - click.audioTime) * 1000` over the matched taps of clicks 5-12 (at least 6 needed) |
| 2 | "2. Watch and tap" - "Now there is no sound. Tap when the circle flashes on the line." | 12 flashes of the hit-line circle at 90 BPM drawn at the scheduled audio time (no audio); same matching and ignoring rules | `V` = median of `(tap.tAudio - flash.audioTime) * 1000` |
| 3 | "3. Note speed" - "Notes should reach the line exactly when you hear them. Choose a speed that is comfortable to read." | a 4-lane highway preview loops 8 notes with clicks, using the new values; slider "Note speed" (7.3) | `visualLeadMs` |
| Summary | "Your calibration" - "Sound delay: {audioLatencyMs} ms. Tap timing: {inputOffsetMs, with sign} ms. Note speed: x{s}." plus "Browser estimate of the sound delay: {estimate} ms." from `Audio.latency()` and two number fields to adjust both values manually | `audioLatencyMs = clamp(round(A - V), 0, 500)`, `inputOffsetMs = clamp(round(V), -200, 200)`; the judge offset therefore equals `A` (Part 5.12) and the highway delays notes by `audioLatencyMs` | "Save"* (writes the three keys with `source:'wizard'`), "Back", "Cancel" E |

Quality checks per step: fewer than 6 matched taps -> S-CAL-01 "Not enough taps were
counted. Tap on each click, then try again." with "Try again"; interquartile range of the
deltas above 40 ms -> S-CAL-02 "Your taps were uneven, so the result may be off. Try again
for a steadier result." with "Try again" and "Use anyway". Step buttons: "Start" (primary,
starts the clicks after a 1 s pause), "Skip this step" (keeps the current value), "Back",
"Cancel" E. During steps 1 and 2 `Escape` cancels the run of that step only. Opening the
wizard while a song is paused (SCR-Pause) is allowed; saving marks that run not comparable
(Part 6.9.5).

### 7.8 HUD and gameplay feedback

#### 7.8.1 HUD elements

`FLM.UI.HUD` builds these children of `#hud` once per `show(kind)` and updates them in one
DOM write batch per animation frame (Part 2.13 decision 2); score text is coalesced to at
most 30 updates per second (Part 4.4 `score.update`).

| Id | Kinds | Content | Position (portrait / landscape and desktop) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hud-progress` | instrument, dance | bar of `tick / durationTicks`, tick marks at section starts, loop region shaded `--c-accent-2` 30 % | top edge, full width / top edge over the highway column |
| `hud-section` | instrument, dance | current section label (from `sched.marker`), `--fs-4` | under the progress bar, left |
| `hud-score` | instrument, dance | score with thousands separators and the multiplier "x{m}" when m > 1 | top-right / top-right |
| `hud-accuracy` | instrument, dance | "{aa.aa} %" | under the score |
| `hud-judgment` | instrument, dance | judgment word and timing word (7.8.2) | 45 % height over the highway |
| `hud-combo` | instrument, dance | "{n} combo" when n >= 4 | under the judgment |
| `hud-performers` | instrument | one chip per performer: family icon, track name (16 chars), activity mark (filled circle while the track has sounding notes, hollow ring otherwise) | bottom-left above the pads / bottom-left |
| `hud-beat` | all gameplay kinds when `accessibility.flashOnBeat` | four squares (numerator squares) for the beats of the bar; the current beat filled, the downbeat square larger | top-left under the section |
| `hud-chord` | freeplay | last chord or note label | center |
| `hud-rec` | freeplay, studio | "Recording {m:ss}" with `g-record` and the word | top-center |
| `hud-life` | dance with life bar | bar plus "Life {n} %" | top edge |
| `hud-peers` | multiplayer | 7.6.4 `ins-peers` | left column |
| `hud-sync` | multiplayer | 7.6.4 `ins-sync` | top-right under the accuracy |
| `hud-sr` | all | visually hidden `aria-live="polite"` region (7.8.6) | n/a |

The instrument and dance HUDs differ in layout and content (7.6.9): the dance HUD puts the
receptors at the top, the combo at 60 % height, score and accuracy at the bottom corners and
has the life bar; the instrument HUD has the hit line at the bottom, the performers row and
no life bar (I 7 "a distinct gameplay HUD").

#### 7.8.2 Judgment feedback and non-color cues

Every judgment is shown in three redundant ways: the word, a shape at the lane's hit point,
and the color (B 22 "non-color-only indications of success and failure").

| Judgment | Word (`hud-judgment`, `--j-*` color) | Shape at the hit line of each lane of the note | Timing word |
|---|---|---|---|
| perfect | "Perfect" | a full ring around the lane glyph, 100 % size, 150 ms | none |
| great | "Great" | a ring at 75 % size | "Early" or "Late" when `abs(deltaMs) > perfect window` |
| good | "Good" | a ring at 50 % size | "Early" or "Late" |
| miss (head) | "Miss" | an X (`g-close` shape) over the lane glyph; the missed note turns to `--c-text-dim` and continues off the line | none |
| miss (hold tail) | "Hold break" | the hold tail turns to `--c-text-dim` from the break point | none |
| stray press (no note) | no word | the pad and lane glyph flash with a dashed outline (no ring) | none |

Rules: the newest judgment replaces the previous word immediately (no queue); a chord shows
one word (the chord's judgment, Part 6.9.4 B.8); while a hold is held its tail is drawn at
full lane color and the word "Hold" shows under the combo; `gameplay.showJudgmentText` off
hides words but keeps shapes; `accessibility.largeJudgmentText` scales the word to 125 %;
the screen-reader region does not read individual judgments (7.8.6).

#### 7.8.3 Combo display rules

- The combo appears at 4 consecutive hits ("4 combo") and updates in place on each hit.
- Every 50th combo shows the milestone word "{n} combo!" for 1 s (scale pulse 1.0 -> 1.1
  over `--t-fast` without reduced motion).
- A miss after a combo of 10 or more shows "Combo lost at {n}" in `--fs-2` for 800 ms under
  the judgment; below 10 the combo simply disappears.
- The score multiplier is shown as "x2", "x3", "x4" next to the score (Part 6.9.4 E.4) and
  returns to nothing at x1.
- Combo text never covers the four lanes' lower 20 % (the area where notes are judged).

#### 7.8.4 Section and failure feedback

- At each section boundary (`sched.marker`) the finished section's accuracy is shown at the
  side of the highway for 2 s as "{label}: {accuracy rounded to an integer} %"; it never
  overlaps the lanes.
- Failure feedback is informative, not punitive (P 5.2): the word "Miss" without sound
  effects or screen shake; after 8 misses in a row the hint S-PLAY-07 "Too fast? Pause to
  slow down, loop this section, or try an easier difficulty." appears once per play-through
  for 3 s at the side.
- Dance with life bar: the bar drains per miss (Part 6.23 failure rule); at 20 % it shows
  the word "Low"; at 0 the song ends with S-DNC-01.
- Song end: "Song complete" (S-PLAY-01) for 1.5 s, then SCR-Results.

#### 7.8.5 Pause and restart

- Pausing (any trigger) freezes the highway at the paused tick, hides `hud-judgment` and
  `hud-combo` milestones, and pushes SCR-Pause; the Judge is inactive (Part 6.9.4 B.1), and
  held controls were released with `source:'system'` (Part 4.7.4), so no press during the
  pause is judged or counted as a stray (P 5.2).
- Resume uses the three-beat countdown of 7.6.18.
- Restart and Retry run the full leave and enter sequence; `HUD.reset()` sets the score to
  0, hides the combo and judgment, empties the progress bar, clears the section label and
  the peers' values, and the new Judge starts from a fresh `load` (Part 6.9.3 invariant 5),
  so no stale scoring state is reused.

#### 7.8.6 Screen-reader announcements

When `accessibility.screenReaderLabels` is on, `hud-sr` announces, politely and at most one
message per 2 s: the count-in start ("Get ready"), section changes ("Chorus"), combo
milestones every 50, pause and resume, the song end, and in multiplayer joins, leaves and
the start countdown. Individual judgments are not announced (they would flood the reader);
the results screen announces the full summary.

### 7.9 Onboarding and tutorial

#### 7.9.1 First launch (B 6.1) and returning users

| B 6.1 step | Where | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Display the game identity | SCR-FirstLaunch step 1 | logo and tagline appear at frame 0 of the screen |
| 2 Check browser support | SCR-FirstLaunch `fl-checks` | the four boot stages B5-B8 of Part 4.3 shown as discrete states; hard failures never reach this screen (`#fatal`) |
| 3 Request audio activation by gesture | `fl-start` (also `fl-skip`) | the click handler calls `Audio.unlock()`; failure opens DLG-AudioBlocked; no sound plays before the gesture (P 4 "audio activation is explained only when necessary": the hint line is the only explanation) |
| 4 Determine rendering capabilities | step 3 `fl-tier` | the tier chosen at B8 is named; Abstract is explained |
| 5 Offer desktop or mobile input configuration | step 2 `fl-input` | Keyboard, Touch or Gamepad with a live preview and the touch probe (OQ-1) |
| 6 Allow choosing a gameplay mode | step 3 `fl-choices` | tutorial, demo song, or menu |
| 7 Explain unavailable functionality without blocking | step 3 `fl-unavailable` | reasons listed; every available mode stays reachable |

Persistence: `onboarding.firstLaunchDone` and `onboarding.inputMode` are written
immediately (Part 5.11 rule: `onboarding.*` writes are not debounced) when a step 3 choice
or "Skip setup" is made; `onboarding.audioHintSeen` when DLG-AudioBlocked was shown once.
Returning users (flag true) go straight to SCR-MainMenu (Part 4.3 B14) with the sound banner
until their first gesture (B15); completed onboarding is never forced again (P 4). Permissions
are requested only on demand: MIDI only from the Settings toggle, clipboard read only from a
Paste button, never at launch (P 4).

#### 7.9.2 Tutorial steps (I 11.3)

The tutorial runs on the `tut-basics` song (Part 1.7; segments and the recording loop in
Part 6.30) with profile A in C major on Acoustic Grand Piano, beginner windows. Instructions
use the player's actual bindings: `{lane0}` and similar placeholders are filled with the
current key names from `Input.getMap()` ("A", "Arrow Left"), so a remapped player sees
their own keys (P 4 "teaches the actual controls"). The variant (keyboard or touch) follows
the last input source used (`input.event.source`), switching live; gamepad uses the keyboard
text with button names ("A button") substituted.

| Step | Title | Keyboard instruction | Touch instruction | Success criterion | Retry hint |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "Play a note" | "Press {lane0} to play a note. Press it three times." | "Tap the circle pad three times." | 3 presses of lane 0 that produced a `sched.noteOn` with `live:true` | "Press {lane0} (or tap the circle pad)." |
| 2 | "Two notes at once" | "Press {lane0} and {lane1} at the same moment to play two notes together. Do it twice." | "Tap the circle and triangle pads together, twice." | 2 presses where two different lanes are pressed within 50 ms of each other (`Rhythm.CHORD_TOLERANCE_MS`); the chord label shows the interval name | "Press both at the same time; they were {n} ms apart." |
| 3 | "Follow the rhythm" | "Notes slide down to the line. Press the matching key when a note reaches it." | "Notes slide down to the line. Tap the matching pad when a note reaches it." | the 8-note chart of segment 3 (quarter notes, lanes 0, 1, 2, 3, 0, 1, 2, 3, after a 1-bar count-in) played with at least 6 notes not missed | "Wait until each note touches the line, then press." The step loops automatically up to 3 times; after the third failure "Skip step" becomes the primary button |
| 4 | "Change the instrument" | "Pick another instrument, then play a note with it." | same | three cards "Piano", "Clean guitar" (27), "Square lead" (80) plus "More instruments" (the `fp-instrument` selects); success when the chosen program differs from the starting one and one note sounds with it | "Choose a different instrument first." |
| 5 | "Record a short take" | "Press Record. After four clicks, play anything for four bars. It stops by itself." | "Tap Record. After four clicks, tap the pads for four bars. It stops by itself." | a `complete` take with at least 4 notes in the 4-bar loop; the take then plays back once automatically | "Nothing was recorded. Play after the four clicks." |
| 6 | "Import a song" | "If you have a MIDI, MusicXML or Guitar Pro file, choose it now. No file? Skip this step." | same | a successful `import.done`; the summary shows format and track count, with "Add to Library" (registers the song) and "Continue"; an import error shows its text and the step stays open | "That file could not be imported. Try another, or skip this step." |
| 7 | "Studio or Dance" | "Build songs track by track in the Studio, or play the dance game." | same | choosing "Open the Studio", "Try Dance Mode" or "Finish"; any choice sets `onboarding.tutorialDone = true` | n/a |

Every step has "Repeat step" (restarts the step from its setup state, clearing its counters)
and "Skip step" (marks it skipped and moves on); the tutorial can be left at any point with
"Leave tutorial". Steps 1-3 use the Rhythm Judge only in step 3; steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 use the
Free Play mapper. Step 5 uses a transient project that is discarded at the end unless the
player chooses "Open the Studio" in step 7, in which case the take becomes the first track
of the new Studio project. Tutorial state (step results) is kept for the session; only
`tutorialDone` persists.

| High-contrast indicators (B 22, I 15) | `html.high-contrast` token overrides (Part 3.2.2): pure black surfaces, white outlines on lane glyphs and notes (`--lane-outline`), 2 px borders, no shadows; lane glyphs forced on | SCR-Settings Accessibility; Part 3.2.2 |
| Non-color lane and direction identification (B 22 last paragraph, I 15, P 15) | glyph shapes on notes, pads, receptors, chart previews and key labels (Part 3.2.5); judgment words plus shapes (7.8.2); status chips with words; compatibility badges with words | everywhere lanes or status appear |
| Visual feedback for audio events (B 22) | beat indicator (`hud-beat`), performer activity marks, metronome indicator in Free Play and Studio, hit rings | HUD, SCR-FreePlay, SCR-Studio |
| Reduced motion (B 22, I 15, P 12, P 15) | `video.reducedMotion` System, On, Off; `html.reduced-motion` and the media query zero the motion tokens; JS reads the class to disable camera motion, particles, judgment scaling and panel slides; highway scroll, hit feedback and the beat indicator stay (Part 3.2.2 motion rule) | SCR-Settings Accessibility; M-20, M-21, M-26 |
| Adjustable visual effects (B 22, I 15) | `video.effectsLevel` Off, Reduced, Full; `video.cameraMotion`; tiers | SCR-Settings Video, SCR-Pause |

| Keyboard navigation for menus (B 22, I 15) | every screen operable with `Tab`, arrows, `Enter`, `Space`, `Escape`, `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown` as listed per screen; gamepad navigation in menus (7.4.5) | M-26, M-27 |
| Accessible labels (B 22, P 15) | every control has a visible label or `aria-label`; icon buttons always have `aria-label`; canvases have `aria-hidden` or `role="img"` with a description; live regions as listed | all screens |
| Focus visibility and dialog focus (I 15, P 15) | `:focus-visible` ring 2 px `--c-focus` with 2 px offset, `.focus-ring` fallback; focus trap and restore (7.4.4) | M-26 |
| Clear error messages (B 22, P 15) | every message names the operation and the next step (7.11.1 rule 2) | 7.11 |
| Disabled controls explain why (P 15) | `aria-disabled` plus the reason line and `aria-describedby`; activating opens DLG-Unsupported with the reason | all screens |
| Configurable control sizes (I 15) | `input.padSize` 56, 72, 88 px; UI scale for menus | SCR-Settings Controls |
| Simplified visualization for low-powered devices (I 15) | `video.tier` Low and Abstract; "3D band" off in SCR-QuickPlay | SCR-Settings Video |
| Consistency across modes (I 15 last paragraph) | accessibility settings are global keys read by M-26, M-20, M-21 and M-07 in every mode; no mode has its own copy | Part 5.11 |
| Settings persist (P 15) | written on change through `Storage.saveSettings` | M-16 |

#### 7.10.1 Comparability flag (P 5.3)

A run is comparable only when the judgment preset is Standard, the speed is 100 %, the
extra-press penalty is off, calibration was not changed during the run, and the song was
finished (Part 5.13 `comparable`, Part 6.9.4 G). The UI makes this visible in three places:
the badge "Not comparable" next to any off-default value in SCR-QuickPlay, SCR-Dance and
SCR-Pause; the SCR-Results line "Not counted for personal bests: {reasons}"; and the history
list (comparable runs only feed personal bests and the daily challenge). Multiplayer forces
Standard windows and 100 % speed for every player (Part 5.16 `ready` validation) and shows
S-NET-13 "Multiplayer uses standard timing windows and normal speed so scores are
comparable." in the lobby when a player's local setting differs. Accessibility adjustments
are never hidden or disallowed in single-player; they are labeled.

### 7.11 Text catalog

#### 7.11.1 Rules

1. Home in code: every string of this catalog lives in one frozen table `FLM.Core.Text`
   (data block at the end of `src/01-core.js`) with `get(code, params) -> string`,
   `has(code) -> boolean` and `all() -> object`. Reason: M-01 is the only module every other
   module may reference (Part 4.2 R-DEP), and `ErrorReporter.report` fills `userMessage`
   from the catalog at report time (Part 4.9). Module tables such as `FLM.Import.ERRORS`
   hold codes and classes and read their text from `Core.Text`, so a string exists once.
   `get` replaces `{name}` placeholders from `params`; a missing parameter becomes an empty
   string and is logged once; an unknown code returns E-GEN-000 text with the code.
2. Every error text says what failed and what the player can do next (I 11.4, P 15 "error
   messages identify the affected operation"); dialogs add the code in `.code` under the text;
   toasts for `E-*` codes show the code in `--fs-1` after the text; `S-*` texts never show a
   code.
3. No text exposes stack traces, file paths, internal ids, byte offsets beyond the
   `{detail}` the parsers already limit, or anything from the user's files other than the
   file name and titles (P 19 "avoid exposing sensitive information"). Imported text
   (titles, track names, warning details) is always inserted with `textContent` (ADR-12).
4. Number formats (fixed, independent of the browser locale so screenshots and tests are
   stable): integers with "," thousands separators ("12,450"); accuracy with two decimals
   ("97.42 %"); other percentages as integers ("75 %"); times by `Core.formatTime` ("3:12",
   "-0:02" during count-in); sizes "{n} KB" below 1 MB (integer) and "{n.n} MB" above;
   milliseconds as integers with "ms"; signed offsets with an explicit sign ("+12 ms",
   "-8 ms"); BPM with at most one decimal ("120 BPM", "73.5 BPM").
5. ASCII only; the ellipsis is "..." and the multiplication sign is "x".
6. Warning texts `W-*` are owned by the modules that produce them (Part 6.3, 6.10 to 6.14,
   Part 5.6) and are shown verbatim in SCR-ImportInspect and SCR-Diagnostics; they are not
   repeated here.

UI of 4.9 and this part. Codes marked "log" have no user text (they are defects or internal
