## 12. Testing and acceptance plan

This part turns B 25 (testing strategy), B 26 (acceptance criteria), E 2 to E 7, E 9, E 11
and E 13 (edge cases, recovery rules, release gate), I 13 and I 13.1 (reliability and fault
injection), I 17 (automated quality gates), I 19 (measurable quality targets) and P 20
(testing and release quality) into named tests with fixed IDs. Sections 12.1 to 12.7 hold the
automated levels; 12.8 to 12.11 (cross-device, live manual, release gate, evidence) and 12.12
to 12.13 (acceptance tests per requirement) follow in the same part. Every test here is
planned: nothing is written, run or passing at plan time, and no result may be recorded
before the test has run against the build named in its row.

### 12.1 Strategy and tooling

#### 12.1.1 Test levels

| Level | IDs | Defined in | Code location and runner group | How it runs | Gate class (Part 9.1.1) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | `UT-<MM>-<nn>` | Part 6 module sections; compiled in 12.2 | `src/91-test-<module>.js`, group `<module>` (file suffix of the module, Part 3.1) | in-page runner M-31; headless through `node tools/selftest.mjs --group <module>` | [U] |
| Integration | `IT-001`.. | 12.3 | `src/92-test-integration.js`, group `integration`; touch rows also run in the touch context as `integration@touch` | `node tools/selftest.mjs --group integration` (corpus injected, Part 3.4.3 step 4a) | [U] |
| File format | `FT-001`.. | 12.4 | `src/92-test-files.js`, group `files`, test name `<ID> files.<subgroup>.<file name>` | `node tools/selftest.mjs --group files` (corpus injected) | [U] |
| Timing | `TT-001`.. | 12.5 | `src/92-test-timing.js`, group `timing`; long rows registered `{slow:true}` | `node tools/selftest.mjs --group timing` and `--slow` for the slow rows | [U] |
| Performance | `PT-001`.. | 12.6 | scenarios of Part 9.7.3 driven by `tools/perf.mjs` (in-page part in `src/92-test-perf-smoke.js`); each PT row also has a short smoke check in group `perf-smoke` | `node tools/perf.mjs --scenario <name>` (default and slow sets, Part 9.7.1); smoke checks in every `selftest.mjs --all` | [H], [HD], [D], [B] as the row states |
| Fault injection | `FI-001`.. | 12.7 | `src/92-test-faults.js`, group `faults`; faults armed through `FLM.debug.inject` (Part 10.9) | `node tools/selftest.mjs --group faults` (corpus injected; touch rows as `faults@touch`) | [U] |
| Cross-device and browser | `XT-001`.. | 12.8 (Part 12b) | none (manual protocol) | owner on physical devices and browsers | [D] |
| Live manual | `LT-001`.. | 12.9 (Part 12b) | none (manual protocol) | tester with headphones and the shipped file | [D] |
| Acceptance | `AT-<R-ID>` | 12.12 and 12.13 (Parts 12c, 12d) | references the IDs above | by the referenced tests, or review | as referenced |
| Build checks | (no ID) | Part 3.3.4 | `tools/build.mjs` | every build: lint rules (S-01, S-04, S-05, S-07 regexes), size limits, `node --check` | [B] |
| Corpus check | (no ID) | Part 3.6.2 | `tools/make-corpus.mjs --check` | when a T section touches the generator or `test-corpus/` | [B] |
| Relay self-test | (no ID) | Part 3.7.6 | `server/relay.mjs --selftest` | Phase 13 gate and later gates | [U] |
| Smoke of the shipped file | (no ID) | Part 3.4.5 | `node tools/selftest.mjs --smoke` | every phase gate from Phase 1; Phase 16 on both editions | [B] |

B 25.1 lists the minimum unit-test topics; their coverage by module is in 12.2.32. B 25.2 to
B 25.4 and B 25.6 map to 12.3 to 12.6; B 25.5 maps to 12.8; B 25.7 maps to 12.12 and 12.13.

#### 12.1.2 Runner conventions (binding for every automated test)

1. Name. The runner test name is the ID, one space, then the title of its row (for example
   `IT-014 recording to project save and reload`); FT names follow Part 8.9.1
   (`FT-001 files.midi.midi-mono-simple.mid`). `--grep` matches either part. The ID in the
   name is how 12c and 12d, STATUS.md and the final report find a result.
2. Isolation. Each test starts from the `menu` mode with `Modes.assertClean()` null and ends
   with `Modes.leave('user')` when it entered a mode, `FLM.Core.Faults.clearAll()`, and an
   `assertClean()` that must return null (a non-null result fails the test, Part 9.5 rule 2).
   No test depends on another test's side effects or on run order.
3. Determinism. Random choices use `new FLM.Core.Prng(seed)`; the seed is the one named in
   the row, otherwise 1. Clock-sensitive rows use `FLM.SelfTest.fakes.clock()` or the
   offline engine of Part 6.5.4.10 (`createEngine({context: OfflineAudioContext, clock})` with
   `scheduler.tickOnce(audioNow)`); only rows that say "real clock" use the live
   `AudioContext` (headless Chromium starts it with `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required`,
   Part 3.4.2).
4. Storage. Rows that persist use the real M-16 with `FLM.SelfTest.fakes.indexedDB` and
   `FLM.SelfTest.fakes.localStorage` unless the row says "real storage"; real-storage rows
   delete every key and record they wrote (the headless context starts empty, Part 3.4.2).
5. Input. Gameplay presses come from `Input.synthesize` (source `synthetic`) or, in touch
   rows, from real dispatched Pointer Events; "chart bot" means the synthesized presses of
   Part 9.1.1 item 12, which judge perfect when the input anchor and the Transport agree.
6. Network. No automated test opens a network connection. Multiplayer rows use
   `Net.createSession(deps)` instances joined by `Net.createLoopbackPair(opts)` and
   `FLM.SelfTest.fakes.rtc` (Part 6.24.8). Rows that need the relay process are marked
   Automated "no" and are run by hand at the Phase 13 and Phase 15 gates.
7. Timeouts. Per test 10 s, slow tests 60 s (Part 3.4.6); slow rows of 12.5 and 12.6 run only
   with `--slow` or in `tools/perf.mjs` sets.
8. Skips. A test may skip only for a missing capability that it names in the message
   (for example `skip: no WEBGL_lose_context`); a skip is not a pass for gating unless the
   row is marked capability-dependent and 12.8 has an XT row for the capability.
9. Exact values. Expected values in the rows are the values the code must produce, derived
   from the Part 5, 6, 8 and 9 rules cited; a mismatch is a defect in the code or a plan
   inconsistency to be resolved by a LEDGER "Decisions" line before the test is changed.

#### 12.1.3 Execution environments

| Environment | Used by | What it can show | What it cannot show |
|---|---|---|---|
| Headless Chromium desktop context (1280 x 720, DPR 1, no touch) through `tools/selftest.mjs` | UT, IT, FT, TT, FI, perf-smoke | logic, scheduling against the audio clock, file handling, recovery paths, DOM structure, WebGL2 through SwiftShader | real device timing, audible quality, GPU performance |
| Headless Chromium touch context (390 x 844, `hasTouch:true`) | groups `input`, `ui`, `integration`, `faults` (Part 3.4.2) | Pointer Event lifecycle with up to 4 concurrent touch points, pad layout | iOS Safari pointer behavior (OQ-1, 12.8) |
| `OfflineAudioContext` inside the page | TT, UT-05-15, UT-06-06, wav export rows | sample-exact onsets, drift, pitch | output latency of a device |
| `tools/perf.mjs` headless runs | PT | regression signals for jitter, drift, heap growth, serialization, import time; frame metrics recorded as info "(software GL)" | device frame rate and memory claims (Part 9.1.4 rule 2) |
| Test build on a device (SCR-Diagnostics "Run self-test" and "Run performance scenarios") | owner runs of UT to FI and PT device sets | the same tests on a real browser | nothing beyond what the tests assert |
| Physical devices and browsers by hand | XT, LT (Part 12b) | audibility, touch feel, readability, browser-specific behavior | nothing automated |

#### 12.1.4 Gating rules per T section

A T section is done only when the "clean T section" conditions of Part 3.9 hold, with these
test rules:

1. Every test ID named in the section's Verification line exists in its file under its exact
   name, runs, and passes in a headless run made after the section's last code change. A
   Verification line may name a test that a later section completes only if it is marked
   "(partial until Tpp.nn)" there; such a test is registered and must pass in the form the
   current code supports.
2. Every group touched by the section passes in full (`--group <g>` exit 0), and its test
   count is at least the count of its 12.2 table (unit groups) or of its rows here that are
   assigned to phases up to the current one (cross-module groups).
3. After any change to M-01 to M-09, the foundation guard of Part 3.9 item 3 passes.
4. A section that adds a test adds its row to this part's table and its line to
   `parts/12x-index-*.txt` in the same commit (plan patch, LEDGER "Decisions" line); IDs are
   never reused or renumbered.
5. A failing test is never deleted, weakened or marked skipped to close a section; the
   section stays open, or the requirement goes to Partial or Blocked in STATUS.md with the
   failing test named (Part 0.7 rule 3).

#### 12.1.5 Gating rules per phase

At every phase gate (Part 0.4 step 5) the session runs, in this order, and records each
summary line in the LEDGER gate entry:

1. `node tools/build.mjs` (exit 0; size warnings allowed before Phase 16).
2. `node tools/selftest.mjs --all --json <scratch path>`: every registered test passes; zero
   page errors; capability skips listed by name.
3. `node tools/selftest.mjs --smoke` on the shipped file.
4. `node tools/make-corpus.mjs --check` (from Phase 7).
5. `node tools/perf.mjs --repeat 3` default set from Phase 4 (Part 9.1.1 item 9); the slow
   set (`--slow`) at the Phase 14 and Phase 16 gates.
6. `node tools/selftest.mjs --all --slow` at the Phase 2, 4, 9, 14, 15 and 16 gates (adds the
   10-minute drift and long-session rows).
7. `node server/relay.mjs --selftest` and the Automated "no" rows of 12.3 from Phase 13.

The tests of this part become binding at the gate of the phase in their row's Phase column
(12.3 lists it in the coverage table 12.3.2; 12.4 to 12.7 in their own tables). A phase
gate cannot close while a binding test of that phase or an earlier one fails.

| Phase (B 27) | Binding from this gate (cumulative with earlier phases) |

| 1 Foundation | unit groups `core`, `ui`, `screens` (menu, settings, help, about, diagnostics rows), `modes` (menu rows), `boot`, `selftest`; PT-001, PT-002 |
| 2 Musical data and timing | groups `theory`, `model`, `transport`; the FakeClock rows of 12.5 marked Phase 2 |
| 3 Input and four-button gameplay | groups `input`, `mapping` (profiles), `rhythm`; IT and TT rows marked Phase 3; PT-009 (input part) |
| 4 Audio engine | groups `audio`, `instruments`, `content`; offline TT rows; PT rows marked Phase 4 |
| 5 3D stage and visualization | groups `render`, `rig`, `animation`, `stage`; IT, TT, PT, FI rows marked Phase 5 |
| 6 Free Play | rows marked Phase 6 |
| 7 MIDI import and playback | groups `midi`, `import`; FT subgroups `midi`, `midi-damaged`, `limits` (MIDI and audio rows), `audio`, `ident`; rows marked Phase 7 |
| 8 Rhythm-game song mode | `mapping` chart rows; rows marked Phase 8 |
| 9 Studio and multitrack recording | groups `project`, `storage`, `studio`; FT `roundtrip` (MIDI and project rows); FI storage rows; rows marked Phase 9 |
| 10 Character customization | groups `character`, `progress`; rows marked Phase 10 |

#### 12.1.6 No continuous integration

This project has no continuous-integration service, no hosted runner and no pre-merge
check (repository convention; ADR-11). Every gate above is run by the implementing session
on its own machine with the commands listed, or by the owner with the same commands or from
SCR-Diagnostics on a device. A gate is "passed" only when its commands were run on the commit
being gated and their summary lines are in the LEDGER entry; a result from an earlier commit
never carries over. Pushes happen only when the owner says so (BRIEF 8).

#### 12.1.7 Regression policy (I 17 last rule, P 20)

1. Every defect found after its feature's tests first passed is recorded in STATUS.md
   section 6 with its severity (Part 13.2) before it is fixed.
2. The fix lands together with a regression test that fails on the unfixed code and passes
   on the fixed code. The test takes the next free ID of the lowest level that can show the
   defect (a new `UT-<MM>-<nn>` after the module's last number, or the next `IT`, `FT`, `TT`,
   `FI` number), its title ends with `(regression)`, its row is appended to the matching
   table (12.2 to 12.7) and index file, and STATUS.md section 6 names it in the "Regression
   test" column.
3. "Whenever practical" (I 17): a defect that only a physical device shows gets an XT or LT
   row instead (Part 12b); the STATUS row says why no automated test exists.
4. A corpus file that exposed a parser defect stays in the corpus; when the triggering file is
   a real-world file that cannot be committed (licensing), `tools/make-corpus.mjs` gets a
   synthetic recipe reproducing the structure, with a new FT row.
5. Regression tests are never removed; a test made obsolete by a plan change is changed
   only through a LEDGER "Decisions" line that names the replacing test.

#### 12.1.8 Test data

- Corpus: the 89 committed files and the in-memory cases of Part 8.9, injected by
  `tools/selftest.mjs`; a manual run from SCR-Diagnostics skips corpus rows with the message
  `corpus not loaded (run tools/selftest.mjs)` (Part 3.4.3).
- Built-in content: the five demo songs of Part 1.7 (`demo-poprock`, `demo-piano`,
  `demo-electro`, `demo-jazz`, `demo-dance`) and the tutorial sequence (M-30).
- Generated content: songs and projects built in page from a seeded `Prng` (seed `0xF1A9`
  unless stated, Part 9.6) for stress, chord and long-session rows.
- Fakes (M-31, Part 6.31): `fakes.clock`, `fakes.indexedDB`, `fakes.localStorage`,
  `fakes.audioDecoder`, `fakes.rtc`, `fakes.stub`, `fakes.inputEvent`.
- Faults: the 14 names of Part 10.9.2, armed only through `FLM.debug.inject` in the test
  build.

### 12.3 Integration tests (IT-001..)

Integration tests run the real modules together in the test build (group `integration`,
`src/92-test-integration.js`) under the conventions of 12.1.2. "Modules" lists the modules whose
cooperation the test exercises; every row also relies on M-01 and M-31. Rows marked
Automated "no" need a process outside the page (the relay) and are run by hand at the gates
named in 12.1.5; their result is recorded like an automated one.

#### 12.3.1 Test table

| ID | Title | Modules | Setup | Steps | Expected | Pass criterion | Automated |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IT-001 | keyboard lane press to live audio | M-07, M-08, M-05, M-06, M-28 | `freeplay` mode entered through `Modes.enter('freeplay', {})`; profile A, key C major, program 0; real clock; `Audio.unlock()` resolved true | dispatch a `keydown` then, 400 ms later, a `keyup` KeyboardEvent with `code` `KeyA` on the gameplay surface; spy on `input.event`, `sched.noteOn`, `sched.noteOff` | one `input.event` press and one release (source `keyboard`, control `lane0`); one `sched.noteOn` with `live:true` and the profile A lane 0 pitch of UT-08-01; one `sched.noteOff` with `reason:'live'` at the keyup's mapped audio time | event counts exactly 1, 1, 1, 1; `performance.now()` at the `sched.noteOn` emit minus `tPerf` <= 16.7 ms; `Audio.VoiceAllocator.activeCount()` is 0 within the program's release time plus 50 ms after the keyup | yes |
| IT-002 | touch pads: four simultaneous pointers to live audio | M-07, M-26, M-08, M-05 | touch context (`integration@touch`); `freeplay`; pads shown at `input.padSize` medium; real clock | dispatch `pointerdown` for pointerIds 1 to 4 on pads 0 to 3 in one task; after 300 ms dispatch `pointerup` in the order 3, 1, 4, 2; then repeat with the browser's compatibility mouse events also dispatched | 4 presses then 4 releases (source `pointer`), each pad's pressed class set then cleared; 4 live `sched.noteOn` and 4 `sched.noteOff`; the compatibility mouse events produce no extra `input.event` | exactly 8 `input.event` per round; no control left in `Input.held()`; `activeVoices` 0 after the release tails; `assertClean()` null after leave | yes |
| IT-003 | input to scoring: 31 perfect presses | M-07, M-09, M-04, M-28 | `instrument` mode with a test chart of 31 single-lane notes on beats 1 to 31 of a 120 BPM 4/4 test song (intermediate, lane `n % 4`); calibration all zero | chart bot presses and releases each note at `Transport.audioTimeAt(note.tick)`; record the input log; afterwards replay the log through a fresh `Rhythm.Judge` on the same chart | 31 `judge.result` perfect; final `ScoreState` `{score:6400, combo:31, maxCombo:31, counts:{perfect:31, great:0, good:0, miss:0}, judged:31, total:31, accuracy:1, completion:1}`; one `chart.finished` with `endedBy:'end'` | exact integer equality (score = 100 x (10 x 1 + 10 x 2 + 10 x 3 + 1 x 4) = 6400, multiplier from the combo before each note); the replayed ScoreState is deep-equal | yes |
| IT-004 | calibration affects scoring predictably | M-07, M-09, M-27, M-21 | the IT-003 chart at expert; inputs synthesized 30 ms after each note's audio time | run 1: `inputOffsetMs 0`, `audioLatencyMs 0`; run 2: `inputOffsetMs 30`; run 3: `audioLatencyMs 30`, `inputOffsetMs 0`; settings set through `Settings.set` as SCR-Settings does | run 1: every `deltaMs` +30 and every judgment `great` (expert perfect 18 ms, great 40 ms); runs 2 and 3: every `deltaMs` 0 and `perfect`; Scheduler `at` values and the highway's hit-line crossing times identical in all three runs | per note abs(`deltaMs` - expected) <= 1 ms; the three `sched.noteOn.at` lists are equal; run 2 and run 3 ScoreStates deep-equal (S-04: calibration applied once, in the Judge) | yes |
| IT-005 | chords and simultaneous presses within documented limits | M-07, M-09, M-08 | chart with chords of 2, 3 and 4 lanes (4 of each) at 1 s spacing, intermediate | press every lane of each chord with spreads of 0, 20 and 40 ms; for the last 4-lane chord press lane 3 60 ms after lane 0 | each in-tolerance chord yields one `judge.result` after its last press with `deltaMs` equal to the worst lane; the last chord's late press is a stray and the chord is a miss when the window closes (UT-09-15 rule) | 11 chord hits plus 1 chord miss; stray count 1; no lane judged twice | yes |
| IT-006 | imported MIDI to playback: tracks, programs and notes | M-10, M-14, M-15, M-04, M-05, M-06 | corpus `midi-multitrack-band.mid`; `Import.importFile`, then `Project.fromSong` as the Play now path does; offline engine of Part 6.5.4.10 with a 20 s `OfflineAudioContext` | schedule the whole song through `scheduler.tickOnce` in 25 ms steps; render; collect `sched.noteOn` and `sched.program` | 240 `sched.noteOn` (32, 64, 48, 96 per track); programs 33, 29 and 0 on the melodic tracks; the Drums track routed to the drum kit (`isDrums:true`, channel 9); every `at` equals `audioTimeAt(tick)` at tempo 600000 | counts exact; abs(`at` - `audioTimeAt(tick)`) <= 1 ms for every note; rendered onsets of the first note of each track within one render quantum plus 1 ms | yes |
| IT-007 | imported MIDI with tempo changes plays on the tempo map | M-10, M-14, M-03, M-04, M-05 | corpus `midi-tempo-changes.mid` imported; offline engine | schedule and render the full 26.9 s | 48 click notes at the seconds given by the six-segment TempoMap; the note at model tick 45360 starts at `ticksToSeconds(45360)` | every `at` within 1 ms of `TempoMap.ticksToSeconds(tick)` plus the start anchor; `ticksToSeconds(45600)` within 1e-6 of 26.911904 | yes |
| IT-008 | polyphonic MIDI stays polyphonic in playback | M-10, M-14, M-05, M-06 | corpus `midi-poly-chords.mid`; offline engine; voice cap 64 | schedule and render; sample `Audio.VoiceAllocator.activeCount()` after every tick | five notes sound together at every bar start of bars 9 to 16 (seventh chord plus bass); no voice is stolen | maximum simultaneous `sched.noteOn` sharing one `at` is 5; `audio.voices.stolen === 0`; 240 notes started | yes |

The invariants are also asserted at other levels; 12.7.5 lists every test per invariant.

### 12.4 File-format tests (FT-001..)

Group `files`, `src/92-test-files.js`. One FT test per committed corpus file of Part 8.9.3 and
8.9.4 (89 files), one per in-memory case of Part 8.9.5 (subgroup `limits`, names starting `mem-`;
the decoded-audio case is named `mem-audio-400mb.wav`), three whole-corpus checks in `ident`, and
the writer round trips and export checks of Part 8.11 in `roundtrip`. IDs follow Part 8.9.1:
subgroups in the order `midi`, `midi-damaged`, `limits`, `musicxml`, `security`, `mxl`, `gp`,
`audio`, `ident`, `roundtrip`, and file-name order (ASCII) inside each subgroup. A new corpus file
takes the next free FT number at the end of the table (12.1.7), never a number inside a subgroup.

#### 12.4.1 Pass rules

Every corpus and `mem-` row passes only when the five assertion rules of Part 8.9.1 hold: (1) an
expected error rejects with that code, emits exactly one `import.failed` with the expected stage
and no `import.done`, lets no exception escape and leaves `Project.current()` deep-equal (S-12);
(2) an expected success matches `format`, `songs`, `tracks`, `notes`, `status` and `playable`,
contains every listed warning code and no unlisted warn or error code; (3) the import settles
within 5,000 ms; (4) two imports of the same bytes give deep-equal reports after removing ids,
`importedAt` and timings; (5) files with notes generate charts for the four difficulties that pass
`Mapping.ChartGenerator.validate`, and the Song's fnv1a32 is unchanged by generation (S-08). The
Expected column summarizes the Part 8.9 `expect` object; the manifest entry is the exact
reference. `roundtrip` and `ident` rows state their own criterion in the Expected column.

Supported publication rule (Part 8.7, BCD open issue): a format version is published as
Supported only with at least two valid-file FT rows and one malformed-file FT row passing for it;
otherwise it is published as Partial with "(not yet verified)" (Part 8.7.2 section 5).

### 12.5 Timing tests (TT-001..)

Group `timing`, `src/92-test-timing.js`. Rows marked Slow run only with `--slow` (Part 3.4.1)
and at the phase gates of 12.1.5 rule 6. Harnesses: "FakeClock transport" is
`Transport.create({clock: fakes.clock(), bus})` with the Scheduler's `pullDue` read directly;
"offline engine" is `createEngine({context: OfflineAudioContext, clock})` of Part 6.5.4.10 with
onset detection by the first sample above 0.01 after the expected time; "real clock" is the
live `AudioContext`. Every assertion uses scheduled audio times or rendered sample positions,
never wall-clock observation of sound (Part 9.1.1 item 7).

### 12.6 Performance tests (PT-001..)

Each PT row is one `tools/perf.mjs` scenario of Part 9.7.3 (plus the build-size check and one
tool-side layout scenario), with the budgets and thresholds of Part 9.1 and 9.7.7 unchanged.
Thresholds are written "desktop (mobile)". Gate classes are those of Part 9.1.1: [B] build,
[U] unit-verified, [H] headless-gated, [D] device-gated, [HD] both. Headless frame-time values
are info and carry "(software GL)"; device cells stay "not measured" until a device run
exists (Part 9.2.3). Default-set rows run at every gate from their Phase; slow-set rows at the
Phase 14 and 16 gates (12.1.5). The Smoke column is a short in-page check in group `perf-smoke`
(`src/92-test-perf-smoke.js`) that runs in every `selftest.mjs --all` so a gross regression is
caught between perf runs; a smoke pass never stands in for the PT result.

### 12.7 Fault-injection tests (FI-001..)

Group `faults`, `src/92-test-faults.js`, using the fault registry of Part 10.9 (`FLM.debug.inject`
in the test build). Every row also asserts the three E 11 outcomes of Part 10.9.3: no exception
reached `window.onerror` other than the injected one, user data equals its pre-fault snapshot
(or only the documented at-risk item changed), and the application ends in a known-good state
(`Modes.current().mode` is a valid mode and `assertClean()` is null after leaving), then
`FLM.Core.Faults.clearAll()`. "Data-safety assertion" is the row's specific check on top of that.

### 12.8 Cross-device and browser tests (XT-001..)

XT tests run the delivered file in real browsers on real devices (B 25.5, E 9, I 12, P 14,
P 18, P 20). They are planned here; every result cell starts as "not run" and is filled
only from a recorded run (12.11). The implementing session cannot reach physical devices or
non-Chromium browsers (Part 0.6, Part 0.10); it prepares the artifacts, runs the
pre-checks it can run, and lists every XT row as an owner action in the LEDGER until the
owner reports a result.

#### 12.8.1 Rules for every XT test

1. Artifact under test. The shipped `FingerLickinMusic.html` of the release candidate
   commit, built by `node tools/build.mjs`, unless a row names the test build
   (`FingerLickinMusic.test.html`, needed only for "Run self-test" and "Run performance
   scenarios" on SCR-Diagnostics, Part 7.6.15 and 9.7.5). The tester records the file's
   SHA-256 (`sha256sum`, `shasum -a 256` or `certutil -hashfile <file> SHA256`) and the
   version line of SCR-Diagnostics "Build". A result obtained with a different hash does not
   count for the release candidate.
2. Browsers. The five targets of Part 1.6: Desktop Chromium (Chrome; Edge is run as a
   second result line of the same row), Desktop Firefox, Desktop Safari, iOS Safari,
   Android Chrome. Each row runs on the current stable release and on the previous major
   release where the tester can obtain it (Part 1.6); each version is a separate result
   line. Other Chromium-based browsers are not tested (Part 1.6 rule 4).
3. Devices. Device classes are those of Part 9.2.1 (`ref-desktop`, `low-desktop`,
   `ref-android`, `low-android`, `ref-ios`, `old-ios`, `tablet`). Every result line records
   the model, OS build, browser version string (from `navigator.userAgent` as shown in the
   diagnostics export), devicePixelRatio, viewport in CSS px and `navigator.maxTouchPoints`.
4. Contexts. Every row names the contexts it runs in:

   | Context | URL form | Secure context | Used on |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | C1 | `file:///.../Finger Lickin Music/FingerLickinMusic.html` (path with spaces), and a second run after copying the file alone to another folder (for example Downloads) | browser-dependent (Part 1.6) | desktop; Android through `file:///sdcard/Download/FingerLickinMusic.html` or the Files app "Open with Chrome" (the scheme shown, `file://` or `content://`, is recorded); iOS see rule 6 |
   | C2 | `http://localhost:8080/` | yes | desktop |
   | C3 | `https://<static host>/FingerLickinMusic.html` | yes | all five browsers |
   | C4 | `http://<LAN address of the serving computer>:8080/` | no | desktop (from a second computer) and mobile |

   A row "passes for a browser" only when it passes in every listed context on every tested
   version. The `file://` and `http(s)` results are recorded in separate cells (12.11).
5. Serving for C2 and C4 uses Node built-ins only (no npm, ADR-02). From the repository
   root, with the desktop firewall allowing TCP 8080:

   ```text
   cd "Finger Lickin Music"
   node -e "const h=require('http'),fs=require('fs');h.createServer((q,s)=>{const u=q.url.split('?')[0];const f=u==='/'?'FingerLickinMusic.html':decodeURIComponent(u.slice(1));if(f.includes('..')||!fs.existsSync(f)||fs.statSync(f).isDirectory()){s.writeHead(404);s.end();return;}s.writeHead(200,{'Content-Type':f.endsWith('.html')?'text/html; charset=utf-8':'application/octet-stream','Cache-Control':'no-store'});fs.createReadStream(f).pipe(s);}).listen(8080,'0.0.0.0',()=>console.log('serving on 8080'))"
   ```

   The same server lets mobile devices download corpus files from
   `http://<LAN address>:8080/test-corpus/<file>` into their Downloads or Files storage
   before the import rows. C3 uses any static HTTPS host the owner controls (for example
   the repository's GitHub Pages site if the owner enables it); the host name is recorded.
   No row requires a server-side header (R-E9-11).
6. iOS `file://`. When the device offers no way to open a local HTML file with scripts
   running in Safari (the Files app shows only a preview), the C1 cell of an iOS row is
   recorded "n/a: platform cannot open local HTML files" (not "fail"), and the published
   claim for iOS Safari names C3 only (12.11.3 rule 4).
7. Profiles and data. The first run of a browser uses a fresh profile with no site data
   (Chrome or Edge `--user-data-dir=<new folder>`, Firefox `-P` with a new profile, Safari
   Settings > Privacy > Manage Website Data > Remove All, iOS Settings > Safari > Clear
   History and Website Data, Android Chrome Settings > Site settings > All sites > clear).
   Rows that test returning-user behavior say so.
8. Network. C1 runs with the network disconnected (airplane mode or adapter off) from
   before the file is opened, so every C1 run is also an offline run (R-E9-04, R-P18-06).
   C2, C3 and C4 need the network only to load the page; rows that test offline behavior
   disconnect after load.
9. Inspection tools. Desktop: the browser's developer tools (Console and Network panels).
   iOS: Safari Web Inspector from a Mac (Settings > Safari > Advanced > Web Inspector).
   Android: `chrome://inspect` from a desktop Chrome over USB debugging. Where no inspector
   is available, the diagnostics export (`.flmdiag.json`, SCR-Diagnostics "Export
   diagnostics") is the evidence.
10. Console rule. Every row also requires: no uncaught exception and no `#fatal` panel
    during the row, and no network request after the document itself in C2 and C3 (the
    Network panel shows exactly one request, the document) unless the row exercises
    multiplayer with the STUN toggle on or the relay.
11. Session pre-checks. The implementing session runs the Desktop Chromium rows that need
    no physical device in headless Chromium (C1 and C2) as pre-checks; their results are
    recorded "pre-check (headless)" in the LEDGER and never fill a release cell or support
    a Supported claim (Part 9.2.1, Part 1.6 policy).
12. Failure handling. A failing row opens a STATUS.md section 6 defect with the row ID,
    browser line and context; a fixed defect is re-run on the new release candidate hash
    and gains a regression test where one can be automated (I 17).

and that no mode can start; (2) press "Start" on SCR-FirstLaunch; within 1 s
SCR-Diagnostics Timing (opened afterwards) shows audio state `running`; (3) enter Quick
Play and hear the count-in clicks with the accent on beat 1; (4) reload as a returning
user, press nothing, try to start Quick Play with the pointer: the first click or tap both

reload, press a key first (desktop) or tap an empty area (mobile), then start Quick Play
by keyboard; (6) with the device volume at zero, press "Turn on sound" in DLG-AudioBlocked
and confirm the S-AUD-03 text appears only after a failed attempt, not after a success.

#### 12.8.4 Four simultaneous touches on the pads (XT-011..XT-015, OQ-1)

Covers R-P14-03, R-I12-03, R-P5.1-03, R-B26.2-02 (touch part); risk RISK-53; resolves OQ-1
(Part 2.19). Uses the old-ios and ref-ios classes for the two physical iOS devices that

Procedure: (1) fresh profile; at SCR-FirstLaunch step 2 choose "Touch" and place four
fingers on the four pads at once; record the `fl-touch-result` sentence; (2) SCR-Diagnostics
Input shows the same "touch probe maximum" and the pad surface in use (`pointer` or
`touch`); (3) Free Play, profile C (chords) and profile A (lanes): press all four pads at
once 20 times in portrait and 20 times in landscape; count lit pads and heard notes; (4)
set SCR-Settings Controls `input.touchApi` to `pointer`, repeat step 3 in portrait; set it
to `touch`, repeat; set it back to `auto`; (5) Instrument Mode on `demo-poprock` Rhythm
Guitar at expert (four-note chords) for 30 s: chord judgments appear for four-lane chords.

#### 12.8.5 Touch release lifecycle (XT-016..XT-019, E 13 item 7)

Covers R-P14-04, R-P5.1-04, R-P5.1-06, R-I12-04, R-E13-07; risk RISK-09.

Procedure: Free Play with GM program 19 (Church Organ, sustained), profile A, sustain off.
For each case below hold one pad (cases a-f) or four pads (cases g-h), perform the action,
then lift every finger; after each case SCR-Diagnostics Input "held controls" reads 0, no
note keeps sounding and no pad stays lit. Cases: (a) slide the finger onto the
neighboring pad and lift there; (b) slide the finger off all pads onto the highway; (c)

#### 12.8.9 WebGL initialization, tier and context loss (XT-035..XT-039)

Covers R-E9-15, R-P14-11, R-I12.1-01..R-I12.1-05, R-E13-06 (per browser), R-P19-05;

the context type (WebGL2, WebGL1 or 2D) and the initial tier with its reason; compare with
the expected tier of the device class (Part 9.2.1); (2) Quick Play `demo-poprock` with five
performers for 60 s: the highway is readable, performers animate, no visual corruption;

`var c = document.getElementById('view'); var gl = c.getContext('webgl2') || c.getContext('webgl'); var ext = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context'); ext.loseContext();`
(`getContext` returns the context the game already created): the HUD shows "Graphics
paused"; music, input and scoring continue; (4) after 1 s call `restoreContext()` on the same extension object: the
stage returns within 3 s; (5) repeat step 3 without restoring: the Abstract tier takes over
after 3 s with a toast naming the switch to the flat visualizer (text per the Part 10.6 code registry), the song continues to the end and SCR-Results opens;
(6) SCR-Settings Video: force each tier High, Balanced, Low, Abstract in turn for 20 s of
play each; no tier change stops, seeks or re-anchors the Transport (the beat indicator
continues without a jump).

### 12.9 Live manual tests (LT-001..)

LT tests need human perception or judgment: eyes for alignment, readability and visual
quality, ears for timbre, clicks and synchronization, hands for gestures and feel, and
reviewers for wording and documentation. They complement the automated suite (12.3-12.7)
and never replace an automated test where one exists.

#### 12.9.1 Rules for every LT test

1. Artifact and recording. The shipped `FingerLickinMusic.html` of the release candidate
   (SHA-256 recorded as in 12.8.1 rule 1), opened in context C1 on desktop and Android and
   C3 on iOS unless the row says otherwise. Each run records tester, date, device class and
   model, OS build, browser version, file hash, result ("pass", "fail: <reason>", "not
   run") and a findings list.
2. Testers. The owner, or testers the owner names. The implementing session runs no LT row
   on a physical device (Part 0.6); rows whose Device(s) cell says "screenshots allowed"
   may be pre-reviewed by the session from Playwright screenshots of the test build, recorded
   "pre-check (screenshots)", which never fills a release cell.
3. Listening conditions. Audio rows use closed-back wired headphones at a comfortable level
   in a quiet room unless the row names speakers or a Bluetooth output. Rows that compare
   with a reference player name it in the findings.
4. Video evidence. Rows that judge timing by eye use a screen recording at 60 frames per
   second (desktop) or a second phone filming at 240 frames per second (mobile); the clip
   name is written in the findings, the clip itself is kept by the owner (not committed).
5. Findings. Each finding gets a severity by Part 13.2 and, when Medium or higher, a
   STATUS.md section 6 defect. A row passes only when its pass criterion holds and no
   finding of severity High or Critical is open against it; Low and Medium findings are
   recorded and do not fail the row unless the criterion names them.
6. Default inputs. "Keyboard" means the default keys of the brief (lanes `KeyA KeyS KeyK
   KeyL`, dance arrows), "touch" means the on-screen pads at `input.padSize` medium,
   "gamepad" means a standard-mapping controller (an Xbox or PlayStation controller over
   USB or Bluetooth).
7. Content. Rows use the built-in content (`demo-poprock`, `demo-piano`, `demo-electro`,
   `demo-jazz`, `demo-dance`, `tut-basics`), files from `test-corpus/`, and, where a row
   says "real files", files the owner supplies; real files are never committed (licensing).
8. Calibration. Unless a row tests calibration, the tester runs DLG-Calibration once per
   device and output before the first timing row and keeps the result.

#### 12.9.14 Task list for the keyboard-only and touch-only passes

LT-079 and LT-083 use this list; each item is done without the excluded input:

1. Complete first-launch setup and reach SCR-MainMenu.
2. Start Quick Play with a non-default song, track and difficulty; pause, resume, quit.
3. Change master volume, note speed, UI scale and one key or pad setting in SCR-Settings.
4. Run DLG-Calibration to its summary and save.
5. In Studio: add a track, record 4 bars, select and move two notes, undo, save as a new
   project.
6. In SCR-Library: find the project by search, rename it, export it, delete a demo copy
   (and cancel once).
7. Import `midi-multitrack-band.mid` and start play from SCR-ImportInspect.
8. In SCR-Characters: change three options, save the character.
9. Open SCR-Multiplayer, create an invite, copy it, cancel.
10. Open SCR-Help, SCR-About and SCR-Diagnostics and return to the menu.

### 12.10 Release-blocking gate

The implementation must not be declared production-ready, and `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md`,
`README.md`, SCR-About and STATUS.md must not call the release complete, while any gate
row below is unresolved (E 13, B 26.8, Part 0.8 item 6). Test IDs are those of 12.3 to
12.9 (FI IDs from 12.7, hooks of Part 10.9.2) and the acceptance tests `AT-<R-ID>` of
12.12 and 12.13. Build checks are the Part 3.3.4 checks of `tools/build.mjs`, which have no
test ID.

#### 12.10.1 Gate rules

1. A gate row is resolved only when every test it lists has a recorded pass on the release
   candidate's file hash (12.8.1 rule 1) or, for in-page and tool tests, on the build of
   the release candidate commit, and every AT it lists passes.
2. A listed test that cannot run in the environment (owner device and browser tests) keeps
   the row unresolved with the reason "awaiting owner device test"; the session never
   treats "not run" as a pass and never removes a test from a row to resolve it.
3. Part 9.1.2 release-blocking budget rows (2, 14, 15, 20, 21, 22) are part of the gate
   through the PT tests named below; a failure of one of them blocks regardless of other
   results.
4. A row with a failing test produces a STATUS.md section 6 defect of severity Critical
   (Part 13.2); the row resolves only after the fix, the added regression test (I 17) and
   a full re-run of the row on the new release candidate.
5. Lower-priority features may be Deferred only per E 13 (row G-11): their status is in
   STATUS.md and `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md`, and every row G-01 to G-10 and D-01 to D-06 is
   resolved.
6. The gate decision (resolved or not, per row) is written to the Phase 16 LEDGER entry and
   to `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md` (12.11); a release that is delivered with unresolved rows is
   delivered as "not production-ready" with those rows listed.

#### 12.10.4 Gate procedure

1. Build the release candidate with `node tools/build.mjs` from a clean tree; record the
   commit hash, the file hash and the size (D-01).
2. Run `node tools/selftest.mjs --all` and `node tools/perf.mjs --slow`; store both result
   JSON files in the Phase 16 LEDGER entry (D-05).
3. Hand the owner the XT and LT run list (12.8, 12.9) for the release candidate hash, with
   the corpus files and the rule-5 serving command; transcribe the returned results.
4. Evaluate every AT of 12.12 and 12.13 named in 12.10.2 and 12.10.3.
5. Fill the two gate tables of 12.10.2 and 12.10.3 in `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md` with
   "resolved" or "unresolved: <tests not passing or not run>" per row.
6. Only when all 17 rows are resolved may the documents call the release production-ready.

### 12.11 Evidence recording

Every result of 12.3 to 12.10 is evidence only once it is written down in the places below
with its run identity. Nothing is presented as tested, measured or verified without such a
record (B 28 last paragraph, B 25.5, Part 9.2.3 rule 1).

#### 12.11.1 Where results go

| Result | Primary record | Summary copies | `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md` item (B 28 numbering) |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-page suite (`node tools/selftest.mjs --all`: UT, IT, FT, TT, FI) | the results JSON stored verbatim in the LEDGER entry of the run | STATUS.md header line "Self-test (--all)"; STATUS.md section 6 for failures | item 10 "Automated test results": pass and fail counts per category and per group, run date, commit, Chromium and Playwright versions |
| Performance (`node tools/perf.mjs`, PT) | the result JSON of Part 9.7.6 in the LEDGER entry | STATUS.md section 7 per Part 9.1 row; the `headless` row of the Part 9.2 matrix | item 9 "Performance measurements": each Part 9.1.2 row with its value or "not measured" |
| Device scenario runs (XT-065 to XT-069) | the device JSON pasted by the owner, stored verbatim in the LEDGER entry of the day | the device rows of the Part 9.2 matrix in `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`; STATUS.md section 7 | items 8 and 9 |
| XT results | one record line per XT row, browser version and context (12.11.2) in the LEDGER | the browser matrix of `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` (one row per browser version and device, one column per 12.8.18 capability, separate `file://` and `http(s)` cells); STATUS.md header line "Live and device tests (LT, XT)" | item 8 "Browser and device compatibility report" |
| LT results | one record line per LT run with its findings list in the LEDGER | STATUS.md section 6 for findings of Medium severity or higher; the same header line | item 4 "Feature-completion report" (an LT result table by area) and item 11 for open findings |
| AT results | the AT evaluation table of 12.12 and 12.13 with pass, fail or "not run" per AT and the tests it relied on | Part 15 Status column at Phase 16 (Part 0.7 rule 7) | item 2 (traceability matrix with final statuses) and item 4 |
| Release-blocking gate (12.10) | the two gate tables, filled per 12.10.4 step 5, in the Phase 16 LEDGER entry | none | item 4, closing table "Release-blocking gate"; every unresolved row repeated in item 11 |
| Format evidence | FT IDs and real-file LT results per format and version | `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` format matrix (each Supported, Partial, Conversion or Unsupported cell cites its tests) | item 5 "Supported file-format and version matrix" |
| Packaging evidence (D-01, LT-090) | commit hash, file SHA-256, byte size, the build report | STATUS.md header line "Build" | item 1 and item 14 |

#### 12.11.2 Record format

XT and LT record lines in the LEDGER use one fixed line per run (fields separated by
semicolons; no field left empty; unknown values are written "unknown"):

```text
XT-020; Desktop Firefox; Firefox <full version string>; <OS name and build>; ref-desktop <model>; DPR <n>; C1 pass; C2 pass; C3 fail: <reason>; file <sha256 first 12 hex>; <YYYY-MM-DD>; <tester>
LT-033; Audio quality; <browser and full version>; <OS name and build>; ref-ios <model>; pass; findings: <none or the list with severities>; file <sha256 first 12 hex>; <YYYY-MM-DD>; <tester>
```

A context cell or a result is one of "pass", "fail: <reason>", "n/a: <reason>" (only for
the cases 12.8.1 rule 6 and the "-" cells of 12.8.18 allow) or "not run". "pre-check
(headless)" and "pre-check (screenshots)" lines are kept in the LEDGER but are never
copied into `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` or the final report as results.

#### 12.11.3 The "not measured" and "not run" rules

1. A budget cell without a recorded measurement reads "not measured"; a test without a
   recorded run reads "not run". Neither is replaced by an estimate, an expectation, a
   value from another device or browser version, or a value inferred from the engine
   name (Part 1.6 rule 3, Part 9.2.3 rule 1).
2. Values measured in the session's headless Chromium under software GL carry the suffix
   "(software GL)" and never stand for a device (Part 9.2.1).
3. A browser stays "not yet verified" on SCR-About, in `README.md` and in
   `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` until all XT IDs of its 12.8.18 column have passing records on
   the release candidate (Part 1.6 rules 1 and 2). With some failing or not run, it is
   published Partial with the failing or untested capabilities named, or Unsupported.
4. When the platform cannot open local HTML files (12.8.1 rule 6), the claim names the
   contexts actually tested, for example "iOS Safari <recorded version>: tested over https only"
   (the placeholder is the recorded version).
5. When a floor version cannot be obtained (XT-070), the claim states the lowest
   version actually tested.
6. Requirements whose named tests include unrun XT or LT rows stay Partial in STATUS.md
   with the reason "awaiting owner device test" (Part 0.7 rule 3); the final report lists
   them under unverified behavior, separate from implemented and tested functionality and
   from future work (B 28).
7. Results are tied to a file hash. A new release candidate invalidates earlier XT and LT
   results for the rows its changes can affect; the session lists those rows for re-run
   in the LEDGER and marks the old records "superseded by <hash>"; records are never
   deleted.

#### 12.11.4 Browser versions, devices and testers

Every XT and LT record names: the browser and its full version string (as reported in the
diagnostics export), the operating system with its build, the device model and its Part
9.2.1 class, the devicePixelRatio and viewport for layout rows, the output device for
audio rows (speaker, wired, Bluetooth model), the date and the tester. `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`
and the final report reproduce the browser version, OS build, device model and date for
every published result (B 25.5 "Browser versions and actual test devices must be
recorded"). Records and screenshots contain no personal data: device names are models,
not owner-given names; diagnostics exports keep "Include song content" off (S-GEN-05);
real-world music files used in LT rows are named by type and source program only.

#### 12.11.5 Owner actions

Every XT and LT row, and every 12.10 gate row that depends on them, is listed in the LEDGER
"Owner actions" section with the release candidate hash until a result is recorded (Part
0.6). The final report's item 8 and item 11 list the rows still "not run" at delivery and
say that the corresponding behavior is unverified.

### 12.12 Acceptance tests for base specification requirements (AT, B)

One acceptance test per P0 and P1 requirement of spec part B, in matrix order (Part 15.1). Method is `auto: <UT/IT/FT/TT/PT/FI IDs>`, `manual: <XT or LT IDs>` or `review` (documentation and process obligations). A Method cell may combine forms, main form first, separated by `; `; every form in the cell is part of the acceptance test.

### 12.13 Acceptance tests for edge-case, improvement, and polish requirements (AT, E/I/P)

One acceptance test per P0 and P1 requirement of spec parts E, I and P, in matrix order (Part 15.2-15.4). Columns and Method forms are as in 12.12. A Method cell may combine forms, main form first, separated by `; ` (for example `auto: IT-012; manual: XT-030`); every form in the cell is part of the acceptance test.

#### 12.13.1 Edge cases and failure modes (E)

Each row is the acceptance test of one P0 or P1 requirement of Part 15.2 (spec part E), run on the test build (`FingerLickinMusic.test.html`) with the fault hooks of Part 10.9 and the corpus of Part 8.9 unless the row names the shipped file or a document, and its Method names the automated tests of 12.2 to 12.7, the device and live tests of 12.8 and 12.9, or a document review.

## 13. Risk register

This part is the risk register and severity classification demanded by E 12 (first bullet)
and by B 27 Phase 0 ("Identify technical risks"). It owns the `RISK-<nn>` IDs. Part 11 T
entries cite them in their "Open items" line; every phase gate re-reads this register
(0.4 step 5.2, procedure in 13.3).

At plan version 1.0.0 nothing is implemented, so every risk below is in state `open`
(13.3). The "Mitigation in design" column names the design elements that the implementation
must deliver; it does not describe existing code. A mitigation lowers no severity until the
row's verification has passed in a recorded run.

Columns of the register:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ID | `RISK-<nn>`, stable; never renumbered, reused or deleted (a retired risk keeps its row) |
| Severity | Critical, High, Medium or Low, assigned with the rules of 13.2 |
| Risk | what can go wrong, with its seed in the specification (E 1 row, E 10 item, other section) |
| Impact | the consequence for players, their work, or the delivery if the risk materializes |
| Mitigation in design | the plan elements that prevent or contain it: ADRs (Part 2), module designs (Part 6, cited `6.N` for module `M-NN`), contracts (Part 4), data rules (Part 5) |
| Early warning signal | an observable that shows the risk is materializing before users meet it: a test result, a log entry or event, a build report value, a counter |
| Phase that retires it | the phase (`Phase NN`, B 27 numbering 00-16) whose gate must show the verification passing; "re-checked" names a later phase whose gate repeats the check on more environments |
| Verification | test categories of Part 12 (UT, IT, FT, TT, PT, XT, FI, LT, AT) and, where Part 6 has already defined them, the unit test IDs; IT to LT IDs are assigned in Part 12; `review` means a documented inspection recorded in the LEDGER |

Seeds: RISK-01 to RISK-14 are the fourteen rows of E 1 in order, keeping their E 1
priority; RISK-15 to RISK-29 are the fifteen prohibited mistakes of E 10 in order (their
guards are also listed in Appendix C); RISK-30 to RISK-50 are notable cases of E 2 to E 9
not already covered by an E 1 or E 10 row; RISK-51 to RISK-77 are engineering and process
risks of this plan, including the three open questions OQ-1 to OQ-3 (RISK-53 to RISK-55).
Rows that say "decided here" add a small design element that the named module or screen
must carry; the module design and the Part 7.11 text catalog follow this register for it.

Fault names in the Verification column (`render.slowFrames`, `render.contextLoss`,
`timer.stall`, `audio.suspend`, `audio.fail`, `storage.quota`, `storage.writeFail`,
`import.truncate`, `input.disconnect`, `net.drop`, `net.delay`, `net.duplicate`,
`net.reorder`) are hooks of `FLM.debug.inject` (Part 4.8, list in Part 10.9). Invariants
`S-01` to `S-18` are those of Part 4.6.

### 13.1 Register

| ID | Severity | Risk | Impact | Mitigation in design | Early warning signal | Phase that retires it | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RISK-01 | Critical | Audio timing drifts away from gameplay (E 1 row 1, E 2.2, B 26.3): the highway, the Judge and the audio derive positions from different clocks, or rounding accumulates across loops, tempo changes and speed changes. | Rhythm scoring becomes unreliable; sound and visuals separate over a song; loops slide (E 13 item 1). | ADR-05 (integer ticks at PPQ 960; the audio clock is the only master; exact re-anchor at every loop wrap; speed applied outside the `TempoMap`); 6.4 M-04 anchor math and `pullDue`; 6.5 M-05 lookahead scheduler on `ctx.currentTime`; 6.7 M-07 `perfToAudio` with the 20-sample median anchor (Part 4.5.1); 6.9 M-09 judges `tAudio` against `audioTimeAt(note.tick)`; S-01, S-02, S-09. | TT drift above 1 ms after 10 simulated minutes; `input.anchor` jitter above 4 ms on a desktop; highway tick differing from `positionAt(audioNow)` by more than 1 tick in the frozen-RAF harness. | Phase 04; re-checked Phase 15 | UT (UT-04-05, UT-04-15, UT-04-20, UT-05-15, UT-05-16, UT-07-10); TT (10 min loop drift below 2 ms, tempo-change songs, speed changes); IT (S-01 frozen-RAF harness); XT (drift and anchor jitter per browser). |
| RISK-02 | Critical | Audio is blocked by the browser (E 1 row 2, E 2.1, B 21.2): the `AudioContext` stays `suspended` because no qualifying user activation reached `resume()`, or iOS needs the silent-buffer kick. | The game appears broken or silent; gameplay would score against a frozen clock. | ADR-04 decision 1 (one context, idempotent unlock); 6.5 M-05 unlock path with the silent-buffer kick, attached to `pointerup`, `keydown` and `click` (6.5.9); Part 4.3 steps B14-B15 (the SCR-FirstLaunch "Start" button is the gesture; menu banner "Tap or press a key to enable sound"; DLG-AudioBlocked with "Try again"); Part 4.7 gameplay modes cannot be entered before `audio.unlocked`. | `unlock()` resolving `false` in any XT run; `audio.state` still `suspended` 1,000 ms after a gesture; a tester reporting silence on first launch. | Phase 04; re-checked Phase 15 | UT (UT-05-01, UT-05-03); IT (mode entry waits for `audio.unlocked`; cancel keeps the menu); XT (unlock in all five browsers from `file://` and `https`); LT (first launch on iOS Safari and Android Chrome). |
| RISK-03 | Critical | MIDI parsing loses or misorders events (E 1 row 3, E 3.1, B 15.2). | Imported songs play incorrectly; charts and animation derive from wrong data (E 13 item 3). | ADR-06 decision 2; 6.10 M-10 bounds-checked reader, running status across meta events, VLQ of at most 4 bytes, truncated tracks keep parsed events with `W-MIDI-TRUNCATED`, format 0 channel split, format 2 as one `Song` per track; 6.3 M-03 `compareEvents` total order (Part 5.2) and `pairNotes`; the SMF writer round trip as a second check. | An FT event, track or warning list differing from the corpus expectation; any `W-MIDI-*` warning on a corpus file declared clean; a non-empty write-then-read round-trip diff. | Phase 07 | UT (UT-10-09, UT-10-10, UT-10-12 to UT-10-16, UT-10-21, UT-10-34, UT-03-04, UT-03-05); FT (whole MIDI corpus of Part 8.9 with expected events, tracks and warnings); LT (three real-world MIDI files played and compared by ear). |

| RISK-05 | Critical | Rendering blocks audio scheduling (E 1 row 5, E 2.2): a 100-500 ms frame or a heavy scene starves the 25 ms scheduler interval on the shared main thread. | Audio gaps and late notes during complex 3D scenes. | ADR-04 decision 5 (lookahead 120 ms; overdue events scheduled at `now + 0.005` and logged as `sched.stall`); S-10 (at most 4 ms of scheduling work per tick); ADR-03 decision 4 auto-downgrade when the p95 frame time exceeds 33 ms over 5 s; ADR-03 decision 2 (Low tier animates every 2nd frame); Part 4.7.4 (two stalls above 500 ms lower the tier; a stall above 500 ms pauses gameplay modes); audio before decoration (B 12.7). | Any `sched.stall` in the PT full-band scenario; `render.stats` p95 above 25 ms on Balanced; auto-downgrade toasts during LT sessions on capable devices. | Phase 05; re-checked Phase 14 | UT (UT-05-04, UT-05-17, UT-05-20); TT (`render.slowFrames` and `timer.stall`: every late event is logged, none is dropped, order is kept); PT (full band at High with 64 voices, zero `sched.stall`); XT (mid-range Android device). |

### 13.2 Severity classification rules

Severity rates the worst credible impact if the risk materializes before its verification
has passed. It does not rate likelihood: before implementation there is no data to estimate
probabilities from, and a guessed probability would be an invented number (I 19 last
paragraph). Designing a mitigation never lowers a severity; recorded verification changes a
risk's state (13.3), not its severity.

| Severity | Assign when the worst credible impact includes any of | Consequence while the risk is open |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | (a) loss or silent corruption of saved user work or of a previous take; (b) musical timing drift in normal play, or a supported file losing or misordering musical events; (c) sound that persists after stop or a mode change; (d) the shipped file unable to perform a documented core function standalone, offline or from `file://` in a supported browser; (e) a rendering, audio or network failure that disables the transport, the audio or standalone play; (f) a false success or completion report: a save, an export, a requirement status or a compatibility claim; (g) execution of imported content, or exposure of credentials; (h) multiplayer accepting invalid authoritative results. Items (a) to (h) cover the ten E 13 release-blocking conditions and the B 26.8 criterion "no feature is falsely described as complete". | The gate of its retiring phase does not pass until the verification passes, except when the only missing evidence is an owner device test (the risk stays `open` with the note "awaiting owner device test" and the affected R-IDs stay Partial, 0.7 rule 3). At Phase 16 no Critical risk may be `realized` with its defect unfixed. |
| High | (a) a P0 or P1 feature fails for a whole browser, device class, input method or file category while the rest of the product works; (b) resource exhaustion that crashes, reloads or freezes the tab; (c) a misrepresentation of capability or fidelity in the UI or the documents; (d) a release-critical polish requirement (P 6) fails; (e) a process or tooling failure that would let defects pass a phase gate unseen. | Verified at its retiring gate. If the verification cannot pass there, the LEDGER records the reason and the next phase in which it can run; automated verification may not slip beyond Phase 15, device-dependent verification becomes an owner action. At Phase 16 an open High risk appears in the final report under unverified behavior. |
| Medium | (a) a P1 feature degrades while a workaround or fallback exists; (b) a Part 9.1 budget is missed while timing, data and core functions stay intact; (c) a P checklist item other than P 6 fails visibly; (d) a disclosure or usability problem without data loss. | Does not block a gate. At Phase 16 it is `retired`, or `accepted` and listed in the final report's known issues (B 28 item 11). |
| Low | a P2 feature, a cosmetic issue, or a process inefficiency with no effect on product quality. | Does not block a gate; `accepted` at Phase 16 if still open. |

Assignment rules:

1. Test the Critical list first, then High, then Medium; the first level with a matching
   item is the severity. When a reader can argue for two levels, the higher one applies.
2. A risk seeded from an E 1 row keeps at least the E 1 priority (Critical or High).
3. A risk whose materialization would make any E 13 condition true is Critical.
4. A severity changes only when the scope changes (the owner defers a requirement, or a
   feature is added). The change, with its reason, is recorded in the LEDGER "Decisions"
   section, and the register row is patched as a 1.0.x plan correction (0.1).
5. A realized risk becomes a defect row in STATUS.md section 6 with the same severity,
   unless the observed impact is smaller, which the defect row then states. Defects found
   without a matching risk are classified with the same table (0.7 rule 5).
6. Defect consequences: an open Critical defect stops the current T section (it cannot be
   marked done) and every phase gate until it is fixed and its regression test passes; an
   open High defect blocks the gate of the phase that owns the affected module and blocks
   Phase 16; Medium and Low defects do not block gates and are fixed or listed among the
   final report's known issues. Every fixed defect receives a regression test (I 17).
7. The severities in 13.1 were assigned with these rules at plan version 1.0.0.

### 13.3 Review cadence

Risk states. They describe risks, not requirements, and are written in lower case so that
they are never confused with the five requirement status words (0.9.2):

| State | Meaning | Allowed transitions |
|---|---|---|
| `open` | The mitigation is designed but its verification has not yet passed in a recorded run. Every risk is `open` at plan version 1.0.0. | to `retired`, `realized`, or (Medium and Low at Phase 16 only) `accepted` |
| `retired` | Every verification named in the row passed in a recorded run (command and result in the LEDGER) at or after the row's retiring phase. | to `realized` when a later `--all` run or device test fails that verification; the related requirements go back to Partial (0.7 rule 3) |
| `realized` | The risk occurred: an early warning signal was confirmed by a failing test or an observed failure, and a defect row exists in STATUS.md section 6. | to `retired` once the defect is fixed, its regression test passes and the row's verification passes |
| `accepted` | A Medium or Low risk still open at Phase 16, listed in the final report's known issues. Never used for Critical or High. | none |

When the register is reviewed:

1. Baseline (Phase 00). The first LEDGER entry (0.4 step 3) records "Risk register
   baseline: 77 open (Critical 17, High 41, Medium 19, Low 0)" and the result of RISK-72's
   plan validation.
2. Every phase gate (0.4 step 5.2). The full procedure below runs before the gate commit.
3. Event-driven, during any T section. When an early warning signal of any row is
   observed, the session reviews that row at once and writes one LEDGER line (RISK ID,
   signal, evidence). If a test failure confirms the signal, the row becomes `realized` and
   13.2 rule 6 applies before the T section continues.
4. Open questions. When the test that answers OQ-1, OQ-2 or OQ-3 runs (Part 2.19: Phase 15,
   Phase 14 and Phase 13), RISK-53, RISK-54 or RISK-55 is reviewed and the selected default
   or fallback is recorded where Part 2.19 says.
5. Pauses. Before a deliberate pause or on low context (0.4 step 6) no full review is run,
   but the `RESUME:` entry lists every risk that changed state since the last gate.
6. Final review (Phase 16 gate). Every row is reviewed. Release conditions: no Critical or
   High risk is `realized` with its defect unfixed; no Critical risk is `open` except those
   waiting only for an owner device test, which the final report lists as unverified; every
   still-open Medium or Low risk is `accepted` and listed among the known issues; the state
   counts appear in the final report (Part 14).

Gate review procedure:

1. Read every row of 13.1, including rows added by plan patches, not only the rows whose
   retiring phase is the current one.
2. Collect this gate's evidence: the `node tools/selftest.mjs --all` JSON, the
   `node tools/perf.mjs` JSON when the phase runs it, the build report (size against the
   RISK-60 envelope), log extracts from the test runs (`sched.stall`, `E-AUD-006`,
   `E-MODE-001`, `project.saveFailed`, `render.contextLost`, `net.message` with
   `valid:false`), and every XT and LT result recorded since the last gate.
3. For each row whose retiring phase is this phase: check every verification it names.
   Set `retired` when all passed; otherwise keep `open` with the reason and the phase in
   which the verification will run (13.2 table, High row), or set `realized`.
4. For each row whose "re-checked" phase is this phase: repeat its verification on the
   added environments; a failure sets `realized`.
5. For every other `open` row: compare its early warning signal with the evidence. A
   present signal is written to the review block; a confirmed one sets `realized`.
6. For each newly `realized` row: add the defect row to STATUS.md section 6 with severity
   and the regression test to be added, move the affected R-IDs to Partial or Blocked
   (0.7 rule 3), and apply 13.2 rule 6.
7. New risks found during the phase get the next free number (the numbers after RISK-77), all eight
   columns, a severity by 13.2, and are added to 13.1 as a 1.0.x plan patch with a LEDGER
   "Decisions" line. Rows are never renumbered or deleted.
8. Write the review block below into the gate's LEDGER entry and include it in the gate
   commit (0.4 step 5.5).

Review block format (one per gate LEDGER entry; rows only for risks whose state changed):

```text
Risk review - Phase <NN> gate (<YYYY-MM-DD>)
| RISK | Severity | Before | After | Evidence | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RISK-<nn> | <severity> | <state> | <state> | <command, date, test IDs and results> | <reason or next phase> |
Signals seen without a state change: <RISK-nn: signal and source, or "none">
Counts: Critical <open>/<retired>/<realized>; High <open>/<retired>/<realized>; Medium <open>/<retired>/<realized>/<accepted>; Low <open>/<retired>/<realized>/<accepted>
Retiring next phase: <RISK IDs, or "none">
```

Retirement schedule derived from 13.1 (the "re-checked" column repeats the verification on
more environments; "every gate" rows are process risks watched at every review and retired
at the phase shown):

## 14. Release checklist, polish gates, and final report

This part is the release contract of version 1.0.0 (`FLM.VERSION = '1.0.0'`, T16.01). It
holds the delivery checklist ticked at the final gate (14.1, B 26.8, P 18), the polish gates
with every P checklist line (14.2, P 1-22), the release-blocking gate summary (14.3, E 13,
pointer to Part 12.10), and the templates of the documents the implementing session writes:
`docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` (14.4, Phase 12 and Phase 16), `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md` (14.5, B 28),
the dependency and license inventory (14.6), the known limitations published at v1 (14.7),
the launch and usage instructions (14.8) and the relay deployment instructions (14.9). The
Phase 16 entries T16.01 to T16.10 execute this part.

At plan version 1.0.0 nothing is implemented. Every status below is Unimplemented or
Deferred, every checkbox is unticked, and every result cell of a template is a placeholder.

Rules for this part:

1. Evidence only. A box is ticked, a status changed or a template cell filled only from a
   record of Part 12.11 (LEDGER record line, results JSON of `tools/selftest.mjs` or
   `tools/perf.mjs`, XT or LT record line) made on the release candidate's commit and file
   hash. The "not run", "not measured" and "not yet verified" rules of 12.11.3 apply to
   every template here.
2. Vocabulary. Requirement and T-entry statuses use only Implemented, Partial, Blocked,
   Unimplemented, Deferred (Part 0.9.2); format and browser claims use only Supported,
   Partial, Conversion, Unsupported (Part 0.9.3), plus the qualifier "(not yet verified)".
3. Files. Every document written from a template is UTF-8 with BOM, LF line endings and
   ASCII text (ADR-09). Placeholders are written `<like this>`; no placeholder survives into
   a delivered document, and the result words "not run", "not measured" and "not yet
   verified" are not placeholders.
4. Sources. A template restates numbers and sentences owned by other parts (Part 1.5
   wording, Part 8.7 format matrix, Part 9.1.2 budgets, Part 10.3 licensing, Part 12.10 gate,
   Part 3.7 relay). Where a restated value and its owning part differ, the owning part
   governs and the template is corrected; the difference is a STATUS.md section 6 defect of
   severity Low.
5. Local labels. `RC-nn` (14.1) and `L-nn` (14.7) are labels local to this part; they are not
   requirement or test IDs and are not traced in Part 15.

### 14.2 Polish gates

Every P checklist line appears here: one row per R-P row of Part 15.4, in matrix order, from
R-P0-01 to R-P22-13 (360 rows: 88 P0, 252 P1, 20 P2, of which 1 Deferred). P sections with
numbered subsections (P 2, 5, 6, 7) have one table per subsection under the section heading.

Columns:

- R-ID and Pri: the Part 15.4 row and its priority (B 4.1).
- Checklist item: the Part 15.4 requirement text, which restates the spec line as a testable
  item with the plan's numbers.
- Owning module(s): the Part 15.4 Module(s) cell (a tool or document in backticks where no
  source module carries the item; "none (plan)" where this document satisfies it).
- T section(s): every Part 11 entry whose `Covers:` line names the R-ID (from the 11x
  indexes).
- Verification: `AT-<R-ID>` with its Method from Part 12.13.3 for P0 and P1 rows; P2 rows have
  no AT (Part 12 writes ATs for P0 and P1 only) and name the review evidence instead, taken
  from the owning T entry's Verification or Open items line and the 12.9.15 area mapping.
- Status at v1.0.0: Unimplemented, or Deferred where Part 15.4 says so.

Gate rules:

1. A row becomes Implemented only by Part 0.7 rule 3: every test its Verification cell names
   passes in one `node tools/selftest.mjs --all --slow` run on the gated commit and every named
   XT and LT has a passing record on the release candidate hash (AT-R-P0-03: never after one
   successful run). P2 rows follow the same rule with their review evidence.
2. A P section or subsection gate is "met" when every row in it is Implemented, or Deferred
   with its STATUS.md section 3 row and user-facing wording (Part 0.6). Otherwise it reads
   "not met: <R-IDs>". P2 rows count toward the gate like any other row.
3. The P 6 tables are release-critical (R-P6-01): an open failure in them blocks the release
   through T16.09. The P 22 rows are the subsystem review of T16.09; R-P22-11 and R-P22-12
   are also supplementary release checks (14.3.3).
4. In T16.09 the Status column of every table is overwritten from STATUS.md, the "Gate at
   delivery" column of 14.2.23 is filled, and the same summary is copied into
   `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md` item 4. The tables are never edited to remove or merge rows.

### 14.3 Release-blocking gate summary

The binding gate is Part 12.10: its rules (12.10.1), the E 13 rows G-01 to G-11 (12.10.2),
the B 26.8 rows D-01 to D-06 (12.10.3) with their automated, device and manual tests, and the
procedure (12.10.4). This section restates the list so the release decision can be read in one
place, names the T entry that decides each row, adds three supplementary checks from P 20 and
P 22, and fixes the release status sentences. When this list and 12.10 differ, 12.10 governs
(rule 4 of this part).

#### 14.3.4 Release status sentences

Exactly one of these sentences is written, at T16.10, at the top of `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md`,
in `README.md` under the first paragraph, and in the STATUS.md header block (as a line
"Release status: ..."):

```text
Release status: production-ready. All 17 release-blocking conditions and the 3 supplementary checks are resolved for build <FLM.VERSION>, file SHA-256 <hash>.
```

```text
Release status: not production-ready. Unresolved release conditions for build <FLM.VERSION>, file SHA-256 <hash>: <comma-separated gate rows and checks, each with "tests failing: <IDs>" or "awaiting owner device test: <IDs>">.
```

SCR-About shows the one-line form "Release status: production-ready." or "Release status:
not production-ready; see docs/FINAL-REPORT.md." under the version line; its text id is
added to the Part 7.11 catalog. No document, screen or commit message calls the release
complete, final or production-ready while the second sentence applies (12.10 preamble).

### 14.4 `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` template

Written first in T12.08 (Phase 12) with every evidence cell "not run" and every claim
"(not yet verified)", extended with the browser and device sections in T15.04 and T15.06,
and finalized in T16.06. Sections 1 to 7 are the Part 8.7.2 layout in its order; sections 8
and 9 hold the browser matrix and the device matrix that Part 12.11.1 and Part 9.2.2 place in
this file. Filling rules:

1. Section 2 copies the Part 8.7.1 summary matrix row for row (13 rows); only the Status
   cell may gain the suffix " (not yet verified)", which it carries until section 5 holds a
   passing evidence row for that row on the release candidate.
2. Publication rule (G-09): a format version is written Supported (or Conversion, for the
   rows 8.7.1 marks Conversion) without the suffix only with at least two passing valid FT
   files and one passing malformed FT file of that version in section 5; otherwise it is
   published Partial with the missing evidence named.
3. A browser is written Supported in section 8 only when every XT ID of its 12.8.18 column
   passes in every context its claim names on every tested version (Part 1.6 policy 1);
   otherwise Partial with the failing or untested capabilities named, or Unsupported. Until
   then the claim is "not yet verified".
4. Every result cell is "pass", "fail: <reason>", "n/a: <reason>" or "not run" (12.11.2);
   measured values carry their unit; headless values carry "(software GL)" where rendering is
   involved and never fill a device row (12.11.3).
5. `FLM.Import.COMPATIBILITY` (Part 6.14.4.9) and the SCR-About rendering (Part 8.7.3) are
   compared with sections 2 and 4 line by line in T16.06 (FT-095, UT-14-19); a difference is
   fixed in the code or the document before delivery, never by editing the test.

## 4. Fixed statements
- Audio files are imported as backing audio only. Notes cannot be generated from audio in
  this version; use a MIDI, MusicXML or Guitar Pro file for a playable chart.
- MusicXML files are imported as musical events (notes, timing, dynamics, tempo). Sheet
  music is not displayed.
- This is a Guitar Pro 6 or 7 file (.gpx or .gp). Only Guitar Pro 3, 4 and 5 files (.gp3,
  .gp4, .gp5) can be imported. Export the file as GP5 or as MIDI from Guitar Pro and import
  that.
- Instruments are synthesized; timbres approximate General MIDI programs.
- Import never changes the open project until you confirm.

### 14.5 `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md` template

Written in T16.07 (items 4.3 and 4.4 completed by T16.09 and T16.04, items 12 and 13 by
T16.08) and committed in T16.10. Its fourteen numbered sections are the fourteen items of
B 28 in their order; Part 12.11.1 maps every kind of result to its item.

Rules:

1. Evidence only (rule 1 of this part). Every number, result word and claim cites the record
   it comes from (LEDGER entry date, results JSON file, XT or LT record line, test IDs).
2. Separation (B 28 last paragraph, R-B28-15). Every row of the Part 15 matrix belongs to
   exactly one of five groups, decided from its final STATUS.md status:

   | Group | Label in the report | Rows in the group |
   |---|---|---|
   | A | Implemented and tested | Status Implemented: every test named for the row passed in the final `--all --slow` run, every named XT and LT has a passing record on the release candidate hash, and for P0 and P1 the `AT-<R-ID>` passes (Part 0.7 rule 3) |
   | B | Partial | Status Partial with a reason other than "awaiting owner device test": code exists and a named test fails or a named part is missing |
   | C | Unverified | Status Partial with the reason "awaiting owner device test": code exists, the automated tests pass, and a named XT or LT row is "not run" (12.11.3 rule 6) |
   | D | Not implemented | Status Unimplemented or Blocked at delivery (Blocked rows name the blocker) |
   | E | Future work | Status Deferred (Part 1.5 and the Deferred registers T03.11, T04.11, T11.12, T12.09, T13.11, T14.08), plus every Unsupported row of `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` |

   Wording: only group A rows are described as "implemented and tested". Groups B to E are
   never described as complete, done, working, verified or supported; group C rows are
   described as "implemented, not yet verified on devices". A feature in item 4 takes the
   lowest group of its rows (A highest, E lowest).
3. Item 4 ends with the LT result table (4.2) and the "Release-blocking gate" table (4.4) as
   Part 12.11.1 places them; every unresolved gate row and check is repeated in item 11.
4. The report is regenerated, not patched, when a new release candidate supersedes the
   evidence (12.11.3 rule 7); superseded results are not copied.

### 14.6 Dependency and license inventory template

Filled in T16.05 and copied into `docs/FINAL-REPORT.md` item 6. The expected content is fixed
by ADR-02, Part 2.17 and Part 10.3: zero runtime dependencies, all embedded content original,
four development tools, two optional external services, and the game license notice in force.
A row whose "Checked" cell is not "pass" keeps gate D-03 unresolved. Versions are read, never
assumed: Node from `process.versions.node`, Playwright from

`browser.version()`, Git from `git --version`.
